requirements: typeface may be null to indicate an empty typeface (draws nothing) only where allowed by Skia; object will still be created.
size is in local coordinate units and should be non-negative and finite for meaningful results (otherwise behavior is implementation-defined in later calls).

functions.name: SkFont::SkFont
functions.description: Constructs a SkFont with the provided typeface and default size and other parameters.
requirements: typeface may be null to indicate an empty typeface (draws nothing) only where allowed by Skia; object will still be created.

functions.name: SkFont::SkFont
functions.signature: SkFont::SkFont(sk_sp<SkTypeface> typeface, SkScalar size, SkScalar scaleX, SkScalar skewX)
functions.description: Constructs a SkFont with the provided typeface, EM size, horizontal scale (condense/expand), and horizontal skew (oblique).
requirements: typeface may be null to indicate an empty typeface (draws nothing).
size should be non-negative and finite for meaningful results.
scaleX is a scalar horizontal scale factor; no explicit range constraints documented.
skewX is a scalar horizontal skew; no explicit range constraints documented.

functions.name: SkFont::operator==
functions.description: Compares this SkFont with another for equivalence of font configuration. May consider different SkTypeface pointers unequal even if contents are identical.
requirements: No special requirements; both SkFont objects must be valid.

functions.name: SkFont::operator!=
functions.description: Returns true if this SkFont and the other are not equivalent. Inverse of operator==.
requirements: No special requirements; both SkFont objects must be valid.

functions.name: SkFont::isForceAutoHinting
functions.description: Reports whether the font is configured to always hint glyphs. Only meaningful on platforms using FreeType.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::isEmbeddedBitmaps
functions.description: Reports whether the font may use embedded bitmaps instead of outlines.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::isSubpixel
functions.description: Reports whether sub-pixel positioning may be used for glyphs.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::isLinearMetrics
functions.description: Reports whether linearly scalable font and glyph metrics are requested.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::isEmbolden
functions.description: Reports whether fake bolding (increasing stroke width when rasterizing) is requested.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::isBaselineSnap
functions.description: Reports whether baselines will be snapped to pixel positions when the current transform is axis-aligned.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::setForceAutoHinting
functions.description: Requests that glyphs always be auto-hinted. Only affects platforms using FreeType.
requirements: None; boolean flag toggles the behavior.

functions.name: SkFont::setEmbeddedBitmaps
functions.description: Requests use of embedded font bitmaps instead of outlines when available.
requirements: None; boolean flag toggles the behavior.

functions.name: SkFont::setSubpixel
functions.description: Requests sub-pixel positioning for glyphs.
requirements: None; boolean flag toggles the behavior.

functions.name: SkFont::setLinearMetrics
functions.description: Requests linearly scalable font and glyph metrics (ignoring hinting/rounding for outline fonts). Bitmap formats may ignore this.
requirements: None; boolean flag toggles the behavior.

functions.name: SkFont::setEmbolden
functions.description: Enables fake bolding by increasing stroke width when creating glyph bitmaps.
requirements: None; boolean flag toggles the behavior.

functions.name: SkFont::setBaselineSnap
functions.description: Requests snapping of baselines to pixels when the current transformation matrix is axis-aligned.
requirements: None; boolean flag toggles the behavior.

functions.name: SkFont::getEdging
functions.description: Returns the current glyph edge rendering mode (alias, anti-alias, or subpixel anti-alias).
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::setEdging
functions.description: Requests how glyph edge pixels are rendered (opaque aliasing, grayscale AA, or subpixel AA).
requirements: edging must be one of SkFont::Edging enum values.

functions.name: SkFont::setHinting
functions.description: Sets the glyph outline hinting level. This function does not validate the provided hinting value.
requirements: hintingLevel is passed as-is; caller must supply a valid SkFontHinting value.

functions.name: SkFont::getHinting
functions.description: Returns the current glyph outline hinting level.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::makeWithSize
functions.description: Returns a copy of this font with the specified EM size. Documentation states invalid sizes (<0, infinite, or NaN) are not accepted.
requirements: size must be >= 0.
size must be finite (not infinity, not NaN).

functions.name: SkFont::getTypeface
functions.description: Returns the underlying SkTypeface pointer without altering its reference count. Non-null under normal operation.
requirements: Returned pointer is valid as long as the SkFont (and its internal sk_sp) keeps it alive.
Caller must not attempt to unref the returned pointer.

functions.name: SkFont::getSize
functions.description: Returns the current EM size in local coordinate units.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::getScaleX
functions.description: Returns the current horizontal text scale factor. Default is 1.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::getSkewX
functions.description: Returns the current horizontal text skew factor. Default is 0.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::refTypeface
functions.description: Returns a smart pointer reference (sk_sp) to the underlying SkTypeface, incrementing its reference count.
requirements: Caller receives an sk_sp and owns a reference; manage lifetime accordingly.

functions.name: SkFont::setTypeface
functions.description: Sets the SkTypeface for this font, decreasing the previous typeface's refcount and taking a reference to the new one. Passing nullptr sets an empty typeface (draws nothing).
requirements: tf may be nullptr to clear the typeface.
Ownership is transferred via sk_sp; the function increments tf's refcount by one.

functions.name: SkFont::setSize
functions.description: Sets the EM size in local coordinate units. Has no effect if textSize is negative.
requirements: textSize must be >= 0 for the size to change.
Size is in local coordinate units.

functions.name: SkFont::setScaleX
functions.description: Sets the horizontal text scale factor.
requirements: No explicit range constraints documented.

functions.name: SkFont::setSkewX
functions.description: Sets the horizontal text skew factor (shear).
requirements: No explicit range constraints documented.

functions.name: SkFont::textToGlyphs
functions.signature: size_t SkFont::textToGlyphs(const void* text, size_t byteLength, SkTextEncoding encoding, SkSpan<SkGlyphID> glyphs) const
functions.description: Converts a buffer of text in the specified encoding to glyph indices. Returns the number of glyphs represented. Can be used to query glyph count by passing an empty destination span.
requirements: If byteLength is 0, the function returns 0.
If encoding is UTF-8 and text contains an invalid UTF-8 sequence, the function returns 0.
If encoding is UTF-8/UTF-16/UTF-32, each Unicode codepoint maps to a single glyph using the typeface’s default cmap; unsupported characters map to glyph ID 0.
If glyphs.size() is insufficient to store all glyphs, no glyphs are copied; the total glyph count is still returned so the caller can reallocate.
Function does not validate that character codes or glyph indices are semantically valid beyond mapping.
If byteLength includes a partial character, the partial character is ignored.

functions.name: SkFont::textToGlyphs
functions.signature: int SkFont::textToGlyphs(const void* text, size_t byteLength, SkTextEncoding encoding, SkGlyphID glyphs[], int maxGlyphCount) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Converts a text buffer to glyph indices, writing into a C-array up to maxGlyphCount entries and returning the glyph count. Use with legacy array-based code.
requirements: If byteLength is 0, the function returns 0.
If encoding is UTF-8 and text contains an invalid UTF-8 sequence, the function returns 0.
If encoding is UTF-8/UTF-16/UTF-32, each Unicode codepoint maps to one glyph; unsupported characters map to 0.
If maxGlyphCount is insufficient, no glyphs are copied; the total glyph count is returned so the caller can reallocate and retry.
glyphs may be nullptr with maxGlyphCount == 0 to query count only.

functions.name: SkFont::unicharToGlyph
functions.description: Maps a single Unicode codepoint to a glyph index using the font’s character map. Returns 0 if the character is not supported by the typeface.
requirements: uni is a Unicode scalar value; unsupported values result in glyph 0.

functions.name: SkFont::unicharsToGlyphs
functions.signature: void SkFont::unicharsToGlyphs(SkSpan<const SkUnichar> src, SkSpan<SkGlyphID> dst) const
functions.description: Maps an array of Unicode codepoints to glyph indices using the font’s character map. Results are written for up to min(src.size(), dst.size()) elements.
requirements: dst should be at least as large as src to receive all mappings; otherwise only min sizes are written.
Unsupported characters map to glyph ID 0.

functions.name: SkFont::unicharsToGlyphs
functions.signature: void SkFont::unicharsToGlyphs(const SkUnichar uni[], int count, SkGlyphID glyphs[]) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Maps an array of Unicode codepoints to glyph indices into a C-array of SkGlyphID.
requirements: glyphs must point to an array with at least count entries.
Unsupported characters map to glyph ID 0.

functions.name: SkFont::countText
functions.signature: size_t SkFont::countText(const void* text, size_t byteLength, SkTextEncoding encoding) const
functions.description: Returns the number of glyphs represented by the provided text buffer and encoding. Equivalent to textToGlyphs with an empty destination.
requirements: Same input constraints as textToGlyphs (e.g., UTF-8 invalid sequence returns 0; partial trailing character ignored).

functions.name: SkFont::measureText
functions.signature: SkScalar SkFont::measureText(const void* text, size_t byteLength, SkTextEncoding encoding, SkRect* bounds = nullptr) const
functions.description: Returns the total advance width of the text. Optionally returns the text bounding box relative to (0, 0).
requirements: bounds may be nullptr if no bounds are needed.
Text buffer and encoding must correspond; if byteLength is 0 the advance is 0.

functions.name: SkFont::measureText
functions.signature: SkScalar SkFont::measureText(const void* text, size_t byteLength, SkTextEncoding encoding, SkRect* bounds, const SkPaint* paint) const
functions.description: Returns the total advance width of the text. Optionally returns the text bounding box relative to (0, 0). Paint’s stroke, mask filter, or path effect may modify bounds.
requirements: bounds may be nullptr if no bounds are needed.
paint may be nullptr to ignore paint effects on bounds.
Text buffer and encoding must correspond; if byteLength is 0 the advance is 0.

functions.name: SkFont::getWidthsBounds
functions.signature: void SkFont::getWidthsBounds(SkSpan<const SkGlyphID> glyphs, SkSpan<SkScalar> widths, SkSpan<SkRect> bounds, const SkPaint* paint) const
functions.description: Retrieves per-glyph advances and bounds for the provided glyph IDs. Writes up to the minimum of the provided span sizes and glyph count. Paint may affect bounds via stroking, path effect, and mask filter.
requirements: widths receives up to min(widths.size(), glyphs.size()) values if widths is non-empty.
bounds receives up to min(bounds.size(), glyphs.size()) values if bounds is non-empty.
paint may be nullptr; when non-null, its stroking, SkPathEffect, and SkMaskFilter affect bounds.

functions.name: SkFont::getWidthsBounds
functions.signature: void SkFont::getWidthsBounds(const SkGlyphID glyphs[], int count, SkScalar widths[], SkRect bounds[], const SkPaint* paint) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Retrieves per-glyph advances and bounds for glyphs into C-arrays. Writes count widths if widths != nullptr; writes count bounds if bounds != nullptr. Paint’s stroking, path effect, and mask filter may affect bounds.
requirements: glyphs must point to an array with at least count entries.
If widths is non-null, it must have space for at least count entries.
If bounds is non-null, it must have space for at least count entries.
paint may be nullptr.

functions.name: SkFont::getWidths
functions.signature: void SkFont::getWidths(SkSpan<const SkGlyphID> glyphs, SkSpan<SkScalar> widths) const
functions.description: Retrieves per-glyph advance widths for the provided glyph IDs. Writes up to min(widths.size(), glyphs.size()) values.
requirements: widths span should have capacity for at least glyphs.size() to receive all advances; otherwise only min size is written.

functions.name: SkFont::getWidths
functions.signature: void SkFont::getWidths(const SkGlyphID glyphs[], int count, SkScalar widths[], SkRect bounds[]) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Convenience overload that fills widths and optionally bounds (if non-null) for count glyphs.
requirements: glyphs must point to an array with at least count entries.
If widths is non-null, it must have space for at least count entries.
If bounds is non-null, it must have space for at least count entries.

functions.name: SkFont::getWidths
functions.signature: void SkFont::getWidths(const SkGlyphID glyphs[], int count, SkScalar widths[], std::nullptr_t) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Convenience overload that fills widths array only for count glyphs.
requirements: glyphs must point to an array with at least count entries.
widths must point to an array with at least count entries.

functions.name: SkFont::getWidths
functions.signature: void SkFont::getWidths(const SkGlyphID glyphs[], int count, SkScalar widths[]) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Convenience overload that fills widths array only for count glyphs.
requirements: glyphs must point to an array with at least count entries.
widths must point to an array with at least count entries.

functions.name: SkFont::getWidth
functions.description: Returns the advance width for a single glyph ID.
requirements: glyph is a glyph index; 0 is typically the missing-glyph index.

functions.name: SkFont::getBounds
functions.signature: void SkFont::getBounds(SkSpan<const SkGlyphID> glyphs, SkSpan<SkRect> bounds, const SkPaint* paint) const
functions.description: Retrieves per-glyph bounds for the provided glyph IDs. Writes up to min(bounds.size(), glyphs.size()) values. Respects stroking, SkPathEffect, and SkMaskFilter when paint is provided.
requirements: bounds span should have capacity for at least glyphs.size() to receive all bounds; otherwise only min size is written.
paint may be nullptr; when non-null, its stroking, path effect, and mask filter influence bounds.

functions.name: SkFont::getBounds
functions.signature: SkRect SkFont::getBounds(SkGlyphID glyph, const SkPaint* paint) const
functions.description: Returns the bounds rectangle for a single glyph ID, optionally considering paint’s stroking, path effect, and mask filter.
requirements: paint may be nullptr; when non-null, its stroking, path effect, and mask filter influence bounds.

functions.name: SkFont::getBounds
functions.signature: void SkFont::getBounds(const SkGlyphID glyphs[], int count, SkRect bounds[], const SkPaint* paint) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Retrieves per-glyph bounds for glyphs into a C-array, respecting paint’s stroking, path effect, and mask filter.
requirements: glyphs must point to an array with at least count entries.
bounds must point to an array with at least count entries.
paint may be nullptr.

functions.name: SkFont::getPos
functions.signature: void SkFont::getPos(SkSpan<const SkGlyphID> glyphs, SkSpan<SkPoint> pos, SkPoint origin = {0, 0}) const
functions.description: Computes positions for each glyph starting from the specified origin. Writes up to min(pos.size(), glyphs.size()) points.
requirements: pos span should have capacity for at least glyphs.size() to receive all positions; otherwise only min size is written.

functions.name: SkFont::getPos
functions.signature: void SkFont::getPos(const SkGlyphID glyphs[], int count, SkPoint pos[], SkPoint origin = {0, 0}) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Computes positions for each glyph starting from origin and writes them into a C-array.
requirements: pos must point to an array with at least count entries.
glyphs must point to an array with at least count entries.

functions.name: SkFont::getXPos
functions.signature: void SkFont::getXPos(SkSpan<const SkGlyphID> glyphs, SkSpan<SkScalar> xpos, SkScalar origin = 0) const
functions.description: Computes x-positions for each glyph starting from the specified x origin. Writes up to min(xpos.size(), glyphs.size()) values.
requirements: xpos span should have capacity for at least glyphs.size() to receive all positions; otherwise only min size is written.

functions.name: SkFont::getXPos
functions.signature: void SkFont::getXPos(const SkGlyphID glyphs[], int count, SkScalar xpos[], SkScalar origin = 0) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Computes x-positions for each glyph starting from an x origin and writes them into a C-array.
requirements: xpos must point to an array with at least count entries.
glyphs must point to an array with at least count entries.

functions.name: SkFont::getIntercepts
functions.signature: std::vector<SkScalar> SkFont::getIntercepts(SkSpan<const SkGlyphID> glyphs, SkSpan<const SkPoint> pos, SkScalar top, SkScalar bottom, const SkPaint* = nullptr) const
functions.description: Computes x-intervals [start, end] for intersections of a horizontal band [top, bottom] with the provided positioned glyphs. Returns a vector of start/end pairs.
requirements: pos must correspond 1:1 with glyphs for meaningful results (same length).
paint may be nullptr; when non-null, its effects may influence outlines used for intersection.

functions.name: SkFont::getIntercepts
functions.signature: std::vector<SkScalar> SkFont::getIntercepts(const SkGlyphID glyphs[], int count, const SkPoint pos[], SkScalar top, SkScalar bottom, const SkPaint* paint = nullptr) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Computes x-intervals [start, end] for intersections of a horizontal band [top, bottom] with the positioned glyphs and returns them as a vector.
requirements: glyphs must point to an array with at least count entries.
pos must point to an array with at least count entries (positions correspond 1:1 with glyphs).
paint may be nullptr; when non-null, its effects may influence outlines used for intersection.

functions.name: SkFont::getPath
functions.description: Returns the outline path for the specified glyph if representable as a path; returns empty optional if represented with a bitmap. An ‘empty’ glyph can return a path with zero contours.
requirements: glyphID is a glyph index; some glyphs may not have scalable outlines and thus return empty.

functions.name: SkFont::getPaths
functions.signature: void SkFont::getPaths(SkSpan<const SkGlyphID> glyphIDs, void (*glyphPathProc)(const SkPath* pathOrNull, const SkMatrix& mx, void* ctx), void* ctx) const
functions.description: Invokes a callback for each glyph ID, providing either a pointer to the glyph’s path (or null if none) and a matrix to position/scale it. Useful for bulk path extraction/processing.
requirements: glyphPathProc must be a valid function pointer (non-null).
ctx is an opaque pointer passed through to the callback.

functions.name: SkFont::getPaths
functions.signature: void SkFont::getPaths(const SkGlyphID glyphIDs[], int count, void (*glyphPathProc)(const SkPath* pathOrNull, const SkMatrix& mx, void* ctx), void* ctx) const
functions.description: UNSPANNED API. Invokes a callback for each glyph ID, providing a path pointer (or null) and a transform matrix.
requirements: glyphPathProc must be a valid function pointer (non-null).
glyphIDs must point to at least count entries.
ctx is an opaque pointer passed through to the callback.

functions.name: SkFont::getMetrics
functions.description: Returns recommended line spacing (descent + ascent + leading), optionally copying the font metrics. Values are scaled by text size and do not account for scaleX, skewX, fake bold, style stroke, or path effects.
requirements: metrics may be nullptr if the caller only needs the spacing value.

functions.name: SkFont::getSpacing
functions.description: Returns the recommended line spacing (descent + ascent + leading). Equivalent to getMetrics(nullptr).
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkFont::dump
functions.description: Dumps the font’s fields to SkDebugf for debugging. Output format is not stable.
requirements: Intended for debugging only; callers should not parse or depend on the output format.

functions.name: SkFontStyleSet::count
functions.description: Returns the number of typefaces/styles available in this style set. Call before indexing into the set.
requirements: Must be called on a valid SkFontStyleSet instance.
Use the returned value as the exclusive upper bound for index parameters passed to other SkFontStyleSet methods (e.g., 0 <= index < count()).

functions.name: SkFontStyleSet::getStyle
functions.signature: virtual void SkFontStyleSet::getStyle(int index, SkFontStyle* style, SkString* styleName) = 0;
functions.description: Retrieves the style information and human-readable style name for the typeface at the given index in the set.
requirements: index must be in the range [0, SkFontStyleSet::count()).
The receiver object must be a valid SkFontStyleSet.
style and styleName are output parameters; whether nullptr is permitted is not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: SkFontStyleSet::createTypeface
functions.description: Creates and returns a typeface corresponding to the entry at the given index in this style set.
requirements: index must be in the range [0, SkFontStyleSet::count()).
Returned sk_sp<SkTypeface> may be null if the index is invalid or creation fails (unknown; not documented).
Caller should handle a potentially null result before use.

functions.name: SkFontStyleSet::matchStyle
functions.description: Finds and returns the closest matching typeface in this style set to the provided style pattern.
requirements: pattern must refer to a valid SkFontStyle object.
Returned sk_sp<SkTypeface> may be null if no acceptable match exists (unknown; not documented).
Caller should handle a potentially null result before use.

functions.name: SkFontStyleSet::CreateEmpty
functions.description: Creates and returns an empty style set with no typefaces. Useful as a sentinel or when a family is not found.
requirements: Returned set contains zero entries; callers should expect count() == 0.
Use sk_sp to manage the returned reference.

functions.name: SkFontMgr::countFamilies
functions.description: Returns the number of font families known to this font manager.
requirements: Call on a valid SkFontMgr instance.
Use the returned value as the exclusive upper bound for family index parameters in related APIs (e.g., 0 <= index < countFamilies()).

functions.name: SkFontMgr::getFamilyName
functions.signature: void SkFontMgr::getFamilyName(int index, SkString* familyName) const;
functions.description: Writes the name of the font family at the specified index to the provided SkString.
requirements: index must be in the range [0, SkFontMgr::countFamilies()).
familyName must point to a valid SkString to receive the result.

functions.name: SkFontMgr::createStyleSet
functions.description: Returns a style set for the font family at the given index.
requirements: index must be in the range [0, SkFontMgr::countFamilies()).
Returned sk_sp<SkFontStyleSet> may be empty if the family has no styles (unknown; not documented).
Caller should handle a valid-but-empty set.

functions.name: SkFontMgr::matchFamily
functions.description: Returns a style set matching the specified family name. If the name is not found, returns an empty set. Passing nullptr returns the default system family when available. May return sets not enumerated by indices due to hidden or auto-activated fonts.
requirements: familyName may be nullptr to request the default system family (may still yield an empty set on most systems).
Never returns null; handle the empty set case.
Returned style set may not correspond to any index from createStyleSet(int) due to hidden/auto-activated fonts.

functions.name: SkFontMgr::matchFamilyStyle
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkTypeface> SkFontMgr::matchFamilyStyle(const char familyName[], const SkFontStyle& style) const;
functions.description: Finds the closest matching typeface for the given family name and style. Passing nullptr for familyName requests the default system font. May match fonts not accessible via indices due to hidden or auto-activated fonts.
requirements: familyName may be nullptr to request the default system font.
Returns nullptr if no acceptable match is found; callers must check for null before use.
style must be a valid SkFontStyle reference.

functions.name: SkFontMgr::matchFamilyStyleCharacter
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkTypeface> SkFontMgr::matchFamilyStyleCharacter(const char familyName[], const SkFontStyle& style, const char* bcp47[], int bcp47Count, SkUnichar character) const;
functions.description: Uses system fallback to find a typeface that can render the specified character, considering preferred languages (BCP47) and an optional family/style hint. bcp47[0] is least significant; bcp47[bcp47Count-1] is most significant. If no language matches, any font containing the character may be chosen. Passing nullptr for familyName requests the default system font.
requirements: Returns nullptr if no family can be found for the character; callers must check for null.
familyName may be nullptr to request the default system font.
If bcp47Count > 0, bcp47 must point to an array of at least bcp47Count valid C strings; ordering is from least to most significant as documented.
style must be a valid SkFontStyle reference.

functions.name: SkFontMgr::makeFromData
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkTypeface> SkFontMgr::makeFromData(sk_sp<SkData> data, int ttcIndex = 0) const;
functions.description: Creates a typeface from in-memory font data. If the data is a TrueType Collection, select a face with ttcIndex (0 for none). Returns null if the data is not recognized.
requirements: data must hold valid font bytes for a supported format.
ttcIndex selects a face in a TrueType Collection; pass 0 if not applicable (non-negative value implied; exact bounds not documented).
Returns nullptr on failure; callers must check for null.
Ownership of data is shared via sk_sp.

functions.name: SkFontMgr::makeFromStream
functions.description: Creates a typeface by reading from the provided stream. If the stream contains a TrueType Collection, select a face with ttcIndex (0 for none). Returns null if the stream is not recognized.
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable SkStreamAsset providing the font bytes.
After the call, the SkFontMgr takes ownership of the stream via unique_ptr.
ttcIndex selects a face in a TrueType Collection; pass 0 if not applicable (non-negative value implied; exact bounds not documented).
Returns nullptr on failure; callers must check for null.

functions.name: SkFontMgr::makeFromFile
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkTypeface> SkFontMgr::makeFromFile(const char path[], int ttcIndex = 0) const;
functions.description: Creates a typeface from a font file at the given path. If the file is a TrueType Collection, select a face with ttcIndex (0 for none). Returns null if the file is not found or contents are not recognized.
requirements: path must point to a valid, readable file containing a supported font format.
ttcIndex selects a face in a TrueType Collection; pass 0 if not applicable (non-negative value implied; exact bounds not documented).
Returns nullptr on failure; callers must check for null.

functions.name: SkFontMgr::legacyMakeTypeface
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkTypeface> SkFontMgr::legacyMakeTypeface(const char familyName[], SkFontStyle style) const;
functions.description: Legacy API to create or find a typeface using a family name and style. Intended for compatibility with older behavior. Details beyond parameters are not documented here.
requirements: familyName may be subject to the same conventions as matchFamilyStyle (inference; exact behavior unknown).
Returns sk_sp<SkTypeface>, which may be null if creation or match fails (unknown; not documented).
style must be a valid SkFontStyle value.

functions.name: SkFontMgr::RefEmpty
functions.description: Returns an empty font manager instance with no typeface dependencies. Useful for environments where no system fonts are available or for testing.
requirements: Returned manager has no installed families; callers should expect countFamilies() == 0 and that matching calls will yield empty sets or null typefaces as applicable.
Manage lifetime via sk_sp.

functions.name: SkFontArguments::SkFontArguments
functions.description: Default-constructs a SkFontArguments with collection index 0, no variation design coordinates, and palette index 0 with no overrides. Use this as a mutable argument bundle to configure font selection and rendering parameters before passing to APIs that accept SkFontArguments.

functions.name: SkFontArguments::setCollectionIndex
functions.description: Sets the index of the desired font within a font collection (e.g., TTC, DFONT, CFF, CID, PFR, Type 42, Type 1, FON). Returns a reference to this SkFontArguments to allow chaining.
requirements: collectionIndex should refer to a font that exists within the underlying font collection (inferred from description).

functions.name: SkFontArguments::setVariationDesignPosition
functions.description: Specifies a position in the font’s variation design space. Unspecified axes use default values. Axes not present in the font are ignored. The position’s coordinate array pointer is stored, not copied, so the caller controls the lifetime of the data. Returns a reference to this SkFontArguments to allow chaining.
requirements: position.coordinates must remain valid for the lifetime of this SkFontArguments (explicitly documented: not copied).
position.coordinateCount must match the number of Coordinate entries accessible via position.coordinates.
Each Coordinate.axis is a four-byte tag identifying a variation axis; Coordinate.value is the requested value for that axis. Axes not present in the font will be ignored (documented).

functions.name: SkFontArguments::getCollectionIndex
functions.description: Returns the currently configured collection index for font selection.

functions.name: SkFontArguments::getVariationDesignPosition
functions.description: Returns the currently configured variation design position (pointer and count). The returned structure references the same coordinate memory provided to setVariationDesignPosition.
requirements: The returned VariationPosition may reference caller-managed memory; ensure the original coordinates remain valid while using the returned data.

functions.name: SkFontArguments::setPalette
functions.description: Sets the palette index and optional per-entry color overrides for a color font palette. Override entries with out-of-range indices will not be applied, and later overrides take precedence over earlier ones. The overrides pointer is stored, not deep-copied (inferred from implementation). Returns a reference to this SkFontArguments to allow chaining.
requirements: palette.overrides must remain valid for the lifetime of this SkFontArguments (inferred from the setter assigning the pointer).
palette.overrideCount must correspond to the number of Override entries accessible via palette.overrides.
Override entries with indices outside the palette’s range are ignored (documented).
When multiple overrides target the same index, later entries override earlier ones (documented).

functions.name: SkFontArguments::getPalette
functions.description: Returns the currently configured palette selection and overrides. The returned structure contains the stored overrides pointer and count.
requirements: The returned Palette may reference caller-managed memory originally provided to setPalette; ensure that memory remains valid while using the returned data.

functions.name: SkFontMetrics::operator==
functions.description: Compares two SkFontMetrics instances for exact equality across all stored fields and flags. Intended to check if two metric snapshots are identical. Usage: call on a valid SkFontMetrics instance to compare with another instance; returns true only if every compared data member matches bit-for-bit, including flags and scalar values.
requirements: Both this and the input SkFontMetrics objects must be valid, initialized metric structures.

Equality is strict: all fields (fFlags, fTop, fAscent, fDescent, fBottom, fLeading, fAvgCharWidth, fMaxCharWidth, fXMin, fXMax, fXHeight, fCapHeight, fUnderlineThickness, fUnderlinePosition, fStrikeoutThickness, fStrikeoutPosition) must match exactly for the function to return true.

functions.name: SkFontMetrics::hasUnderlineThickness
functions.description: Checks whether the underline thickness metric is valid and, if so, writes the thickness to the provided output pointer and returns true. If not valid, returns false and leaves the output untouched. Typically used when rendering underlines according to font-provided metrics.
requirements: thickness must be a valid, non-null, writable pointer when the font metric is valid, because the function will dereference it when returning true.
Caller should not assume any value is written when the function returns false.
May be called on a const SkFontMetrics instance; relies on fFlags including kUnderlineThicknessIsValid_Flag to determine validity.

functions.name: SkFontMetrics::hasUnderlinePosition
functions.description: Checks whether the underline position metric is valid and, if so, writes the position to the provided output pointer and returns true. If not valid, returns false and ignores the output pointer. The position is the distance from the baseline to the top of the underline stroke (typically positive in Skia’s y-down coordinates).
requirements: position must be a valid, non-null, writable pointer when the font metric is valid, because the function will dereference it when returning true.
Caller should not assume any value is written when the function returns false.
Uses kUnderlinePositionIsValid_Flag in fFlags to determine validity; callable on const instances.

functions.name: SkFontMetrics::hasStrikeoutThickness
functions.description: Checks whether the strikeout thickness metric is valid and, if so, writes the thickness to the provided output pointer and returns true. If not valid, returns false and leaves the output pointer untouched. Useful when drawing strikeout lines according to font metrics.
requirements: thickness must be a valid, non-null, writable pointer when the font metric is valid, because the function will dereference it when returning true.
Caller should not assume any value is written when the function returns false.
Validity is indicated by kStrikeoutThicknessIsValid_Flag in fFlags; callable on const instances.

functions.name: SkFontMetrics::hasStrikeoutPosition
functions.description: Checks whether the strikeout position metric is valid and, if so, writes the position to the provided output pointer and returns true. If not valid, returns false and ignores the output. The position is the distance from the baseline to the bottom of the strikeout stroke (typically negative in Skia’s y-down coordinates).
requirements: position must be a valid, non-null, writable pointer when the font metric is valid, because the function will dereference it when returning true.
Caller should not assume any value is written when the function returns false.
Validity is indicated by kStrikeoutPositionIsValid_Flag in fFlags; callable on const instances.

functions.name: SkFontMetrics::hasBounds
functions.description: Reports whether bounding metrics (fTop, fBottom, fXMin, fXMax) are valid for this SkFontMetrics. Returns true if the font specifies maximum glyph bounds; false if bounds are invalid (e.g., when kBoundsInvalid_Flag is set).
requirements: Callable on a const SkFontMetrics instance.
Return value indicates only the validity of fTop, fBottom, fXMin, and fXMax; callers must check the return value before relying on those fields.

functions.name: SkImageFilter::filterBounds
functions.signature: SkIRect SkImageFilter::filterBounds(const SkIRect& src, const SkMatrix& ctm, MapDirection, const SkIRect* inputRect = nullptr) const
functions.description: Maps a device-space rectangle through the image filter DAG either forward (destination coverage of a given source rect) or reverse (source rect needed to produce a given destination). Used for clipping and temporary buffer allocation. The result may be conservative (larger than strictly necessary) but must not be smaller than the true required bounds. In reverse mode, inputRect provides the device-space bounds of already-known input pixels; in forward mode inputRect should be null.
requirements: src must be specified in device space.
ctm is the current canvas-to-device transformation matrix associated with the draw; it should match the transform under which the filter is evaluated.

MapDirection selects forward or reverse mapping; choose kForward_MapDirection for destination coverage of a given source rect, and kReverse_MapDirection to compute needed source coverage for a destination rect.
In kForward_MapDirection, inputRect should be null.
In kReverse_MapDirection, inputRect should point to the device-space bounds of known input pixels; if null in reverse mode, the result may be incorrect.
Callers must not assume the returned bounds are tight; they are guaranteed to be no smaller than the true required bounds.

functions.name: SkImageFilter::isColorFilterNode
functions.description: Reports whether this image filter node is a color-filter node. If true, and filterPtr is non-null, sets *filterPtr to a ref-counted SkColorFilter representing this node. If false, filterPtr is left unchanged. Useful for optimization when the image filter is actually just a color transform.
requirements: filterPtr may be null; if non-null and the function returns true, *filterPtr will be set to a non-null, ref-counted SkColorFilter that the caller must manage (follow Skia ref-counting semantics for the returned object).
If the function returns false, the caller must not assume any change to *filterPtr.

functions.name: SkImageFilter::asColorFilter
functions.description: Deprecated alias of isColorFilterNode(); forwards directly to isColorFilterNode. Provided for backward compatibility.
requirements: Same requirements as isColorFilterNode.
Callers should prefer isColorFilterNode instead of this deprecated method.

functions.name: SkImageFilter::asAColorFilter
functions.description: If the entire image filter can be exactly represented by an equivalent SkColorFilter, returns true and, if filterPtr is non-null, stores a ref-counted color filter into *filterPtr. This means applying the returned color filter would have the same visual effect as this image filter DAG.
requirements: filterPtr may be null; if non-null and the function returns true, *filterPtr will be set to a non-null, ref-counted SkColorFilter that the caller must manage according to Skia ref-counting rules.
If the function returns false, the caller must not assume any change to *filterPtr.

functions.name: SkImageFilter::countInputs
functions.description: Returns the number of input image-filter connections this filter accepts. Some inputs may be null depending on the specific filter configuration.
requirements: None beyond standard object validity; use this to discover the valid index range for getInput.

functions.name: SkImageFilter::getInput
functions.description: Returns the input filter at index i, or null if no filter is connected at that index. The meaning and usage of indices are filter-specific.
requirements: i should refer to an input slot defined by this filter type; typical range is 0 to countInputs()-1.
The returned pointer may be null, indicating no connected input at that index.
The returned pointer is owned by the filter; do not delete it. Retain or ref-count according to Skia conventions if you need to keep it beyond the lifetime of the parent filter.

functions.name: SkImageFilter::computeFastBounds
functions.signature: virtual SkRect SkImageFilter::computeFastBounds(const SkRect& bounds) const
functions.description: Computes a conservative object-space bounding rectangle after applying this filter to an input object-space rectangle. The default implementation returns the union of all input bounds, but subclasses may provide tighter bounds.
requirements: bounds is specified in object/local space matching the filter’s local space.
Result is conservative and may be larger than the true bounds; callers must not assume tight bounds.

functions.name: SkImageFilter::canComputeFastBounds
functions.description: Indicates whether this filter DAG can compute resulting bounds for an object-space rectangle via computeFastBounds. Useful to avoid expensive operations when bounds cannot be determined conservatively.
requirements: Call before relying on computeFastBounds for layout or culling decisions.

functions.name: SkImageFilter::makeWithLocalMatrix
functions.description: Returns an equivalent image filter that represents this filter composed with the provided local matrix, if possible. If not representable in this form, returns null. This enables factoring a local transform out of a filter for reuse/optimization.
requirements: matrix is applied in the filter’s local space; it should be a valid SkMatrix.
Caller must handle a null return, which indicates this representation is not supported for this filter DAG.

functions.name: SkImageFilter::Deserialize
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilter::Deserialize(const void* data, size_t size, const SkDeserialProcs* procs = nullptr)
functions.description: Deserializes a SkImageFilter from a binary blob produced by SkFlattenable serialization. Returns a smart pointer to the filter on success or null on failure. Optional deserialization procs can be supplied to control object reconstruction.
requirements: data should point to a buffer containing a serialized SkImageFilter payload.
size must be the number of bytes available at data.
procs may be null; when provided, they must be compatible with objects serialized in the blob.
Caller must verify the return value is non-null before use.

functions.name: SkShader::isOpaque
functions.description: Reports whether the shader is guaranteed to produce only opaque colors (assuming the SkPaint alpha is opaque). Useful for optimization decisions. Intended to be overridden by subclasses; default returns false.
requirements: No inputs; callable on any SkShader instance.
Return value should not be assumed to imply anything about the paint’s alpha modulation.

functions.name: SkShader::isAImage
functions.signature: SkImage* SkShader::isAImage(SkMatrix* localMatrix, SkTileMode xy[2]) const
functions.description: If the shader is backed by a single SkImage, returns a pointer to that SkImage; otherwise returns nullptr. Optionally provides the local matrix and tile modes associated with the image-based shader when non-null pointers are supplied.
requirements: localMatrix may be nullptr; if non-null and the shader is image-backed, it may be written with the shader’s local matrix (exact behavior not fully documented).
xy may be nullptr; if non-null and the shader is image-backed, elements xy[0] and xy[1] may be written with the tile modes (exact behavior not fully documented).
If a non-null SkImage* is returned and the caller needs to keep it beyond the lifetime of the shader, the caller must ref() it (i.e., retain a reference).
Returned SkImage pointer may be nullptr if the shader is not image-backed.

functions.name: SkShader::makeWithLocalMatrix
functions.description: Creates a new shader that applies the provided local matrix before any existing local matrix of this shader, effectively transforming the shader’s coordinate space.
requirements: The provided SkMatrix must represent the desired local transform; specific constraints (e.g., invertibility, finiteness) are not documented.
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.

functions.name: SkShader::makeWithColorFilter
functions.description: Creates a shader that produces the same colors as this shader and then applies the given SkColorFilter to those colors.
requirements: The color filter parameter may be null or non-null; precise behavior when null is not documented (likely returns an equivalent shader).
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.

functions.name: SkShader::makeWithWorkingColorSpace
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> SkShader::makeWithWorkingColorSpace(sk_sp<SkColorSpace> inputCS, sk_sp<SkColorSpace> outputCS = nullptr) const
functions.description: Wraps this shader so that child shaders are evaluated in inputCS and the wrapped shader is assumed to produce RGBA values in outputCS. The wrapper converts from outputCS to the destination color space after evaluation. Useful for custom color-space management within shaders.
requirements: If inputCS is null, the destination color space is assumed for inputCS.
If outputCS is null, it is assumed to be equal to inputCS.
Returned shader’s output is always converted from outputCS to the destination surface color space.
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.
The shader is assumed to return premultiplied values unless otherwise specified by internal Skia behavior; additional constraints are not documented.

functions.name: SkShaders::Empty
functions.description: Creates a shader that represents an empty/degenerate source. Intended as a utility shader; exact color output is not explicitly documented here and is inferred to likely be transparent black.
requirements: No arguments.
Behavioral specifics (e.g., whether it always returns transparent black) are not documented and therefore unknown.
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.

functions.name: SkShaders::Color
functions.description: Creates a solid-color shader from a 32-bit SkColor value. Useful for drawing with a constant color via a shader interface.
requirements: SkColor must be a valid 32-bit color value (ARGB in Skia convention).
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.

functions.name: SkShaders::Color
functions.description: Creates a solid-color shader from a floating-point SkColor4f, interpreted in the provided SkColorSpace.
requirements: SkColor4f components are expected to be in the provided color space; specific range constraints are not documented here.
Color space parameter may be null (behavior not documented; commonly implies a default/destination space, but this is unknown here).
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.

functions.name: SkShaders::Blend
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> SkShaders::Blend(SkBlendMode mode, sk_sp<SkShader> dst, sk_sp<SkShader> src)
functions.description: Creates a shader that blends two child shaders (dst and src) using the specified SkBlendMode. The result samples both shaders and combines their colors per the mode.
requirements: dst and src should be valid shaders; behavior when either is null is not documented here.
The chosen SkBlendMode determines how colors are combined; ensure it is a valid enumerator.
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.

functions.name: SkShaders::Blend
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> SkShaders::Blend(sk_sp<SkBlender>, sk_sp<SkShader> dst, sk_sp<SkShader> src)
functions.description: Creates a shader that blends two child shaders (dst and src) using a custom SkBlender. The blender defines how the colors are combined.
requirements: The SkBlender should be a valid object; behavior when null is not documented here.
dst and src should be valid shaders; behavior when either is null is not documented here.
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.

functions.name: SkShaders::CoordClamp
functions.description: Wraps a shader so that sampling coordinates are clamped to the given subset rectangle before sampling, effectively restricting sampling to that region.
requirements: The input shader should be valid; behavior when null is not documented here.
subset defines the clamp bounds; exact expectations on rectangle validity (e.g., finite, non-empty, sorted) are not documented here.
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.

functions.name: SkShaders::Image
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> SkShaders::Image(sk_sp<SkImage> image, SkTileMode tmx, SkTileMode tmy, const SkSamplingOptions& options, const SkMatrix* localMatrix = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates a shader that samples the provided SkImage, equivalent to SkImage::makeShader. Supports tile modes in X and Y, sampling options, and an optional local matrix.
requirements: image should be a valid SkImage; behavior if null is not documented and likely results in a null shader, but this is unknown here.
tmx and tmy must be valid SkTileMode values.
options must be a valid SkSamplingOptions instance.
localMatrix may be nullptr; if non-null, it is used as the shader’s local matrix transform.
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.

functions.name: SkShaders::RawImage
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> SkShaders::RawImage(sk_sp<SkImage> image, SkTileMode tmx, SkTileMode tmy, const SkSamplingOptions& options, const SkMatrix* localMatrix = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates an image shader that samples the SkImage with minimal processing, equivalent to SkImage::makeRawShader. Intended for advanced usage where color space or other conversions are bypassed.
requirements: image should be a valid SkImage; behavior if null is not documented and likely results in a null shader, but this is unknown here.
tmx and tmy must be valid SkTileMode values.
options must be a valid SkSamplingOptions instance.
localMatrix may be nullptr; if non-null, it is used as the shader’s local matrix transform.
Returns a reference-counted shader; handle sk_sp ownership semantics accordingly.

functions.name: SkColorFilter::asAColorMode
functions.signature: bool SkColorFilter::asAColorMode(SkColor* color, SkBlendMode* mode) const;
functions.description: Reports whether this color filter is equivalent to applying a constant source color with a SkBlendMode. On success, returns true and writes the source color and blend mode to the provided pointers; otherwise returns false and leaves the outputs unspecified/ignored. Useful for introspection/optimization.
requirements: color may be nullptr; if nullptr and the filter is representable, only mode may be set (if non-null).
mode may be nullptr; if nullptr and the filter is representable, only color may be set (if non-null).
On return false, any provided output pointers must be ignored by the caller.

functions.name: SkColorFilter::asAColorMatrix
functions.description: Reports whether this color filter can be represented as a 5x4 color matrix in row-major order (20 floats). On success, returns true and writes the matrix; otherwise returns false and the output is ignored.
requirements: matrix must point to writable storage for 20 floats (5x4 row-major).
On return false, the caller must ignore the contents of matrix.

functions.name: SkColorFilter::isAlphaUnchanged
functions.description: Returns true if the filter is guaranteed to not modify the alpha channel of any color it processes. Useful for pipeline optimization and blending decisions.

functions.name: SkColorFilter::filterColor4f
functions.signature: SkColor4f SkColorFilter::filterColor4f(const SkColor4f& srcColor, SkColorSpace* srcCS, SkColorSpace* dstCS) const;
functions.description: Converts srcColor from its source color space (srcCS) to the destination color space (dstCS), applies this color filter, and returns the filtered color expressed in the destination color space.
requirements: srcCS may be nullptr only if the implementation permits; behavior with nullptr is not specified in this header (unknown).
dstCS should be a valid destination SkColorSpace pointer; behavior if nullptr is not specified in this header (unknown).
srcColor must be expressed in srcCS for correct results.

functions.name: SkColorFilter::makeComposed
functions.description: Creates a composed color filter that first applies the provided inner filter, then applies this filter to the result: result = this(inner(...)).
requirements: inner is moved into the composition; after the call, the caller should not assume inner retains its original value.
Behavior if inner is null is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: SkColorFilter::makeWithWorkingColorSpace
functions.description: Returns a color filter that evaluates this filter in a specific working color space rather than the destination surface space. Intended for filters like Blend or Matrix to perform math in a known color space.
requirements: The SkColorSpace argument is moved into the returned filter; the caller should not reuse it after passing.
Behavior if the SkColorSpace argument is null is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: SkColorFilter::Deserialize
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkColorFilter> SkColorFilter::Deserialize(const void* data, size_t size, const SkDeserialProcs* procs = nullptr);
functions.description: Deserializes a SkColorFilter from a byte buffer. Optionally uses custom deserialization procedures via procs. Returns a smart pointer to the created filter or null on failure.
requirements: data must point to a buffer of at least size bytes containing a serialized SkColorFilter.
size must be the exact length of the serialized data block.
procs may be nullptr to use default deserialization behavior.
Caller must handle a null return in case of invalid or incompatible data.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::Compose
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkColorFilter> SkColorFilters::Compose(const sk_sp<SkColorFilter>& outer, sk_sp<SkColorFilter> inner);
functions.description: Utility to compose two filters. If outer is non-null, returns outer->makeComposed(std::move(inner)). If outer is null, simply returns inner. The resulting filter applies inner first, then outer.
requirements: outer may be null; in that case the function returns inner unchanged.
inner is moved; the caller should not use inner after the call expecting its original value.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::Blend
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkColorFilter> SkColorFilters::Blend(const SkColor4f& c, sk_sp<SkColorSpace>, SkBlendMode mode);
functions.description: Creates a color filter that blends a constant color c with the input color using the specified SkBlendMode. The constant color is interpreted in the provided color space; if that color space is null, c is assumed to be in sRGB.
requirements: The SkColorSpace argument may be null; null implies the constant color is defined in sRGB.
mode must be a valid SkBlendMode value.
c must be expressed in the provided SkColorSpace for correct results.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::Blend
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkColorFilter> SkColorFilters::Blend(SkColor c, SkBlendMode mode);
functions.description: Creates a color filter that blends the given 32-bit SkColor constant with the input color using the specified SkBlendMode. The constant color is interpreted in sRGB.
requirements: mode must be a valid SkBlendMode value.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::Matrix
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkColorFilter> SkColorFilters::Matrix(const SkColorMatrix&, Clamp clamp = Clamp::kYes);
functions.description: Creates a color filter that applies the given 5x4 color matrix (SkColorMatrix) to input colors. Optionally clamps results to the valid channel range.
requirements: clamp controls whether the result is clamped; valid values are Clamp::kYes or Clamp::kNo.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::Matrix
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkColorFilter> SkColorFilters::Matrix(const float rowMajor[20], Clamp clamp = Clamp::kYes);
functions.description: Creates a color filter that applies the given 5x4 color matrix specified as 20 floats in row-major order. Optionally clamps results to the valid channel range.
requirements: rowMajor must point to an array of at least 20 floats (5x4 row-major).
clamp controls whether the result is clamped; valid values are Clamp::kYes or Clamp::kNo.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::HSLAMatrix
functions.description: Creates a color filter that applies a 5x4 matrix in HSLA space. Internally performs HSLA-to-RGBA(Matrix(RGBA-to-HSLA(input))).

functions.name: SkColorFilters::HSLAMatrix
functions.description: Creates a color filter that applies a 5x4 matrix (20 floats, row-major) in HSLA space, equivalent to HSLA-to-RGBA(Matrix(RGBA-to-HSLA(input))).
requirements: rowMajor must point to an array of at least 20 floats (5x4 row-major).

functions.name: SkColorFilters::LinearToSRGBGamma
functions.description: Creates a color filter that converts from linear gamma to sRGB gamma.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::SRGBToLinearGamma
functions.description: Creates a color filter that converts from sRGB gamma to linear gamma.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::Lerp
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkColorFilter> SkColorFilters::Lerp(float t, sk_sp<SkColorFilter> dst, sk_sp<SkColorFilter> src);
functions.description: Creates a color filter that interpolates between two color filters, typically blending their effects by parameter t. Exact behavior and t’s expected range are not documented here.
requirements: t’s valid range and behavior for values outside [0,1] are not specified in this header (unknown).
dst and src are moved; the caller should not reuse them after the call expecting original values.
Behavior if either dst or src is null is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: SkColorFilters::Table
functions.description: Creates a lookup-table color filter that applies the same 256-entry table to all four channels (A, R, G, B). Processing occurs in unpremultiplied space; premultiplied inputs are unpremultiplied, tabled, then remultiplied.
requirements: table must point to an array of at least 256 bytes.
Input colors may be premultiplied; the filter handles unpremultiply/remultiply internally.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::Table
functions.description: Creates a lookup-table color filter that holds a reference to a shared SkColorTable object instead of copying the table.
requirements: table is moved into the filter; the caller should not reuse it after the call expecting its original value.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::TableARGB
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkColorFilter> SkColorFilters::TableARGB(const uint8_t tableA[256], const uint8_t tableR[256], const uint8_t tableG[256], const uint8_t tableB[256]);
functions.description: Creates a lookup-table color filter with separate 256-entry tables for A, R, G, and B. Null tables are treated as identity for that component. Non-null tables are copied into the filter.
requirements: Each non-null table pointer must point to an array of at least 256 bytes.
Any of tableA, tableR, tableG, tableB may be nullptr to indicate identity mapping for that component.

functions.name: SkColorFilters::Lighting
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkColorFilter> SkColorFilters::Lighting(SkColor mul, SkColor add);
functions.description: Creates a color filter that multiplies the input RGB channels by mul’s RGB, then adds add’s RGB, clamping each component to [0..255]. The alpha components of mul and add are ignored.
requirements: mul’s alpha is ignored; only RGB are used.
add’s alpha is ignored; only RGB are used.

functions.name: SkMaskFilter::MakeBlur
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkMaskFilter> SkMaskFilter::MakeBlur(SkBlurStyle style, SkScalar sigma, bool respectCTM = true);
functions.description: Creates a blur mask filter that applies a Gaussian blur to masks before drawing. Use to soften the edges of drawn content with the specified blur style and blur amount. The blur’s effective sigma may be adjusted by the current transform matrix when respectCTM is true.
requirements: sigma must be greater than 0 (as documented).
style must be a valid SkBlurStyle enumerator.
When respectCTM is true, callers should expect the blur radius to vary with the current transform matrix (CTM).
Returned value is a reference-counted sk_sp<SkMaskFilter>; callers should hold it as long as needed and allow automatic release when the smart pointer goes out of scope.

functions.name: SkMaskFilter::Deserialize
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkMaskFilter> SkMaskFilter::Deserialize(const void* data, size_t size, const SkDeserialProcs* procs = nullptr);
functions.description: Reconstructs a SkMaskFilter instance from a serialized byte buffer. Typically used to load a previously flattened mask filter, optionally using custom deserialization procedures. Returns a smart pointer to the deserialized filter or null on failure (inferred from common Skia patterns; exact failure behavior not specified in this header).
requirements: data should point to a buffer containing a serialized SkMaskFilter object (inferred from name and signature).
size specifies the number of bytes available at data and must match the serialized data length for successful deserialization (inferred).
procs may be null; when provided, they supply custom deserialization hooks (type name implies purpose; details not specified here).
Returned value is a reference-counted sk_sp<SkMaskFilter>; callers should check for null before use and manage the smart pointer’s lifetime normally (inferred).

functions.name: SkBlender::Mode
functions.description: Creates and returns a SkBlender that implements the specified SkBlendMode, combining source (paint) and destination (canvas) colors according to that mode. Typical usage is to obtain a standard blending behavior as a reusable blender object for use in Skia’s rendering pipeline. Returns a reference-counted sk_sp<SkBlender> to the created blender. Further behavior or failure modes beyond this summary are not documented in the provided header.
requirements: mode must be a valid SkBlendMode enumerator.
The caller should retain the returned sk_sp<SkBlender> for as long as the blender is needed; it is reference-counted and may be null or non-null depending on implementation (not specified here).
Thread-safety, error signaling (e.g., nullptr returns), and performance characteristics are unknown based on the provided header.

functions.name: SkSurfaces::Null
functions.description: Creates a surface with no backing pixels. Drawing to its SkCanvas has no effect and makeImageSnapshot() on it returns nullptr. Use for sizing or API plumbing where a real surface is not yet required.
requirements: width must be greater than 0; otherwise nullptr is returned.
height must be greater than 0; otherwise nullptr is returned.
Expect that drawing to the returned surface has no effect.
Calling makeImageSnapshot() on the returned surface will return nullptr.

functions.name: SkSurfaces::Raster
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkSurface> SkSurfaces::Raster(const SkImageInfo& imageInfo, size_t rowBytes, const SkSurfaceProps* surfaceProps);
functions.description: Allocates a raster SkSurface with pixels owned by the surface. The pixels are zero-initialized. If rowBytes is 0, a minimum valid row stride is used. Pixels are freed when the surface is released.
requirements: imageInfo.width() must be > 0.
imageInfo.height() must be > 0.
imageInfo.colorType() and imageInfo.alphaType() must be supported by raster surfaces.
If rowBytes is non-zero, it must be at least imageInfo.minRowBytes() for the given info.
surfaceProps may be nullptr.
On success, pixel memory size is imageInfo.height() * chosen rowBytes; failure returns nullptr.

functions.name: SkSurfaces::WrapPixels
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkSurface> SkSurfaces::WrapPixels(const SkImageInfo& imageInfo, void* pixels, size_t rowBytes, const SkSurfaceProps* surfaceProps = nullptr);
functions.description: Creates a raster SkSurface that draws directly into the caller-provided pixel buffer. The surface does not take ownership of the pixels and does not initialize them.
requirements: imageInfo.width() must be > 0.
imageInfo.height() must be > 0.
imageInfo.colorType() and imageInfo.alphaType() must be supported by raster surfaces.
pixels must be non-null.
rowBytes must be large enough to contain imageInfo.width() pixels of the specified SkColorType.
The pixel buffer should be at least imageInfo.height() * rowBytes bytes.
surfaceProps may be nullptr.
Pixels are not initialized; use peekPixels() or readPixels() to access after drawing.

functions.name: SkSurface::isCompatible
functions.description: Returns whether this surface is compatible with the provided GrSurfaceCharacterization, indicating it can be a destination for a GrDeferredDisplayList.
requirements: characterization must describe properties compatible with this surface for a true result.
No side effects; const method.

functions.name: SkSurface::width
functions.description: Returns the surface width in pixels.

functions.name: SkSurface::height
functions.description: Returns the surface height in pixels.

functions.name: SkSurface::imageInfo
functions.description: Returns an SkImageInfo describing the surface. The base implementation returns an unknown SkImageInfo with this surface’s width and height; subclasses may provide a fully-specified info.

functions.name: SkSurface::generationID
functions.description: Returns a unique identifier for the current content of the surface. The id changes whenever the surface’s content changes or when notifyContentWillChange() is called.
requirements: Content id may change after any draw or after notifyContentWillChange().

functions.name: SkSurface::notifyContentWillChange
functions.description: Notifies Skia that the surface contents will be modified externally. This forces a new generationID to be reported on the next generationID() call. Mode kDiscard may allow discarding the current contents; kRetain requests preservation.
requirements: mode must be SkSurface::kDiscard_ContentChangeMode or kRetain_ContentChangeMode.
After calling, generationID() will return a different value.

functions.name: SkSurface::recordingContext
functions.description: Returns the Ganesh GrRecordingContext used by this surface if available, or nullptr otherwise.

functions.name: SkSurface::recorder
functions.description: Returns the Graphite Recorder used by this surface if available, or nullptr otherwise.

functions.name: SkSurface::baseRecorder
functions.description: Returns the base SkRecorder used by this surface. For drawable surfaces this should be non-null.

functions.name: SkSurface::replaceBackendTexture
functions.signature: virtual bool SkSurface::replaceBackendTexture(const GrBackendTexture& backendTexture, GrSurfaceOrigin origin, ContentChangeMode mode = kRetain_ContentChangeMode, TextureReleaseProc textureReleaseProc = nullptr, ReleaseContext releaseContext = nullptr) = 0;
functions.description: For surfaces created from a backend texture, replaces the backing texture with a new one. The previous contents are copied into the new texture (subject to mode), and the surface’s canvas state is preserved. On success, the provided release proc is called when it is safe to delete the texture in the backend API.
requirements: This may only be used if the surface was created via MakeFromBackendTexture.
The replacement texture’s GrBackendFormat and dimensions must exactly match the original.
The original sample count is used; caller must provide a compatible texture.
origin must be a valid GrSurfaceOrigin for the backend.
If textureReleaseProc is provided, the caller must not delete or reuse the provided backend texture until textureReleaseProc(releaseContext) is called.
On SkSurface creation failure, textureReleaseProc (if non-null) is called before this function returns.

functions.name: SkSurface::getCanvas
functions.description: Returns the SkCanvas that draws into this surface. The same canvas is returned on subsequent calls and is owned by the surface.
requirements: The returned SkCanvas must not be deleted by the caller; it is owned by the SkSurface.

functions.name: SkSurface::capabilities
functions.description: Returns the capabilities of the device backing this surface.

functions.name: SkSurface::makeSurface
functions.description: Creates a new surface compatible with this one (same backing type: raster/GPU/null) but with the provided image info. Pixels are not shared.
requirements: imageInfo.width() must be > 0; otherwise returns nullptr.
imageInfo.height() must be > 0; otherwise returns nullptr.
imageInfo must be compatible with this surface’s capabilities; otherwise returns nullptr.

functions.name: SkSurface::makeSurface
functions.description: Creates a new surface compatible with this one using this surface’s ImageInfo but with the specified dimensions. Pixels are not shared.
requirements: width must be > 0; otherwise returns nullptr.
height must be > 0; otherwise returns nullptr.
Result must be compatible with this surface’s configuration; otherwise returns nullptr.

functions.name: SkSurface::makeImageSnapshot
functions.description: Returns an SkImage capturing the current contents of the surface. Subsequent draws to the surface are not reflected in the image. Budgeting matches the surface’s creation budget.
requirements: None beyond having valid surface content. Returns a non-null SkImage on success.

functions.name: SkSurface::makeImageSnapshot
functions.description: Returns an SkImage of the current surface contents restricted to the given bounds. Bounds are sanitized to intersect the surface; if there is no intersection returns nullptr.
requirements: bounds outside the surface are trimmed; if the intersection is empty, returns nullptr.

functions.name: SkSurface::makeTemporaryImage
functions.description: Returns an SkImage view of the current surface contents without copying. The image’s contents remain valid only until the next write to the surface. Intended for short-lived use or when either the surface or image will be destroyed before further writes.
requirements: If the surface is written to after creation of the temporary image, the image’s contents become undefined.
For GPU surfaces, this avoids an internal copy; caller should ensure lifetime/usage aligns with the transient validity semantics.

functions.name: SkSurface::draw
functions.signature: void SkSurface::draw(SkCanvas* canvas, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, const SkSamplingOptions& sampling, const SkPaint* paint);
functions.description: Draws the surface’s current contents into the provided canvas at (x, y). Optional paint controls filtering, alpha, color/image filters, and blend mode. Sampling controls how pixels are sampled.
requirements: canvas must be non-null.
paint may be nullptr.
sampling must be a valid SkSamplingOptions.

functions.name: SkSurface::draw
functions.signature: void SkSurface::draw(SkCanvas* canvas, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, const SkPaint* paint = nullptr);
functions.description: Convenience overload that draws the surface’s contents into the canvas at (x, y) using default sampling options.
requirements: canvas must be non-null.
paint may be nullptr.

functions.name: SkSurface::peekPixels
functions.description: If the surface’s pixels are directly accessible, copies their address, row bytes, and image info into pixmap and returns true. The pixmap refers to the surface’s pixels and is invalidated by any subsequent change to the surface.
requirements: pixmap must be non-null if you expect output.
The returned pixmap becomes invalid after any future modification to the surface.

functions.name: SkSurface::readPixels
functions.signature: bool SkSurface::readPixels(const SkPixmap& dst, int srcX, int srcY);
functions.description: Copies an axis-aligned rectangle of readable pixels from the surface into the destination SkPixmap without scaling. Converts to dst.colorType()/dst.alphaType() if needed. Returns true on success.
requirements: Readable pixels are available for raster surfaces or when backed by the Ganesh GPU backend.
dst must have allocated pixel storage; its rowBytes() must be large enough for one row.
Only the intersection of source and destination rectangles is copied; returns false if they do not intersect.
Passing negative srcX or srcY offsets the copy into dst.
Graphite backend deprecates this API in favor of an asynchronous Context API.

functions.name: SkSurface::readPixels
functions.signature: bool SkSurface::readPixels(const SkImageInfo& dstInfo, void* dstPixels, size_t dstRowBytes, int srcX, int srcY);
functions.description: Copies readable pixels from the surface into a caller-provided buffer described by dstInfo/dstRowBytes without scaling, converting formats as needed. Returns true on success.
requirements: Readable pixels are available for raster surfaces or when backed by the Ganesh GPU backend.
dstPixels must be non-null and large enough for dstInfo.height() * dstRowBytes bytes.
dstRowBytes must be sufficient for one row of dstInfo.width() in dstInfo.colorType().
Only intersecting source/destination rectangles are copied; returns false if they do not intersect.
May fail if conversion to dstInfo.colorType()/alphaType() is not supported.
Negative srcX or srcY offsets the copy into dst.
Graphite backend deprecates this API in favor of an asynchronous Context API.

functions.name: SkSurface::readPixels
functions.signature: bool SkSurface::readPixels(const SkBitmap& dst, int srcX, int srcY);
functions.description: Copies readable pixels from the surface into the provided SkBitmap without scaling, converting formats as needed. Returns true on success.
requirements: Readable pixels are available for raster surfaces or when backed by the Ganesh GPU backend.
dst must be able to allocate pixel storage; if allocation fails the copy fails.
dst.rowBytes() must be sufficient for one row of dst.width().
Only intersecting source/destination rectangles are copied; returns false if they do not intersect.
May fail if conversion to dst.colorType()/alphaType() is not supported.
Negative srcX or srcY offsets the copy into dst.
Graphite backend deprecates this API in favor of an asynchronous Context API.

functions.name: SkSurface::asyncRescaleAndReadPixels
functions.signature: void SkSurface::asyncRescaleAndReadPixels(const SkImageInfo& info, const SkIRect& srcRect, RescaleGamma rescaleGamma, RescaleMode rescaleMode, ReadPixelsCallback callback, ReadPixelsContext context);
functions.description: Asynchronously (when supported) reads a subset of the surface’s pixels, optionally transforms to linear gamma, rescales to info’s size, and converts to info’s color space/type/alpha. Invokes callback with an AsyncReadResult on completion or nullptr on failure.
requirements: srcRect must be contained within the surface bounds; otherwise fails and callback receives nullptr.
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked with (context, result).
In non-supported backends this may operate synchronously; in Ganesh GPU it flushes work and requires a submit for bounded completion time.
The AsyncReadResult data remains valid for the lifetime of the result; for GPU-backed surfaces it is invalidated if the context is abandoned or destroyed.

functions.name: SkSurface::asyncRescaleAndReadPixelsYUV420
functions.signature: void SkSurface::asyncRescaleAndReadPixelsYUV420(SkYUVColorSpace yuvColorSpace, sk_sp<SkColorSpace> dstColorSpace, const SkIRect& srcRect, const SkISize& dstSize, RescaleGamma rescaleGamma, RescaleMode rescaleMode, ReadPixelsCallback callback, ReadPixelsContext context);
functions.description: Like asyncRescaleAndReadPixels, but converts the resized image to YUV420 and returns three planes (Y, U, V) as an AsyncReadResult with count()==3. The U and V planes are half resolution. Fails if dstSize has odd width or height or if srcRect is out of bounds.
requirements: srcRect must be contained within the surface bounds; otherwise fails.
dstSize.width() and dstSize.height() must be even; otherwise fails.
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked with (context, result).
yuvColorSpace specifies the RGB->YUV transform applied after converting to dstColorSpace.
For GPU surfaces, completion timing requires a submit; data is invalidated if context is abandoned or destroyed.

functions.name: SkSurface::asyncRescaleAndReadPixelsYUVA420
functions.signature: void SkSurface::asyncRescaleAndReadPixelsYUVA420(SkYUVColorSpace yuvColorSpace, sk_sp<SkColorSpace> dstColorSpace, const SkIRect& srcRect, const SkISize& dstSize, RescaleGamma rescaleGamma, RescaleMode rescaleMode, ReadPixelsCallback callback, ReadPixelsContext context);
functions.description: Like asyncRescaleAndReadPixelsYUV420, but returns a fourth plane containing the alpha channel at full resolution (Y plane size). The AsyncReadResult will have count()==4.
requirements: srcRect must be contained within the surface bounds; otherwise fails.
dstSize.width() and dstSize.height() should be even (inherits YUV420 constraints).
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked with (context, result).
For GPU surfaces, completion timing requires a submit; data is invalidated if context is abandoned or destroyed.

functions.name: SkSurface::writePixels
functions.signature: void SkSurface::writePixels(const SkPixmap& src, int dstX, int dstY);
functions.description: Writes pixels from the source SkPixmap into this surface without scaling, converting formats to the surface’s color/alpha types as needed. Only the intersecting area is written.
requirements: src must refer to readable pixel data with sufficient rowBytes for its width.
dstX and dstY set the top-left of the write in surface coordinates and may be negative; only the intersection is written.

functions.name: SkSurface::writePixels
functions.signature: void SkSurface::writePixels(const SkBitmap& src, int dstX, int dstY);
functions.description: Writes pixels from the source SkBitmap into this surface without scaling, converting formats to the surface’s color/alpha types as needed. Only the intersecting area is written.
requirements: src must contain readable pixel data with allocated storage.
dstX and dstY set the top-left of the write in surface coordinates and may be negative; only the intersection is written.

functions.name: SkSurface::props
functions.description: Returns the surface properties (e.g., LCD text settings and orientation).

functions.name: SkSurface::wait
functions.signature: bool SkSurface::wait(int numSemaphores, const GrBackendSemaphore* waitSemaphores, bool deleteSemaphoresAfterWait = true);
functions.description: For GPU-backed surfaces, inserts semaphores that the backend must wait on before executing further GPU work for this surface. Returns true if the GPU will wait on the semaphores.
