requirements: If numSemaphores > 0, waitSemaphores must point to an array of at least numSemaphores valid GrBackendSemaphore objects.
If this call returns false, the GPU backend will not wait and the client retains ownership of the semaphores regardless of deleteSemaphoresAfterWait.
If deleteSemaphoresAfterWait is false, the client must not destroy or reuse the semaphores until it knows Skia has finished waiting (e.g., via finishedProcs on flush).

functions.name: SkSurface::characterize
functions.description: Initializes a GrSurfaceCharacterization describing this surface for recording GPU work (e.g., tiling and DDL recording). Returns true if the surface supports characterization; raster surfaces return false.
requirements: characterization must be a valid pointer to receive the properties.
Only supported for appropriate GPU-backed surfaces; raster surfaces will return false.

functions.name: SkPixelGeometryIsRGB
functions.description: Returns true if the provided pixel geometry enum is a known RGB geometry (horizontal or vertical). Use to gate LCD/text rendering paths that depend on RGB stripe order.
requirements: Argument geo must be a valid SkPixelGeometry value; kUnknown_SkPixelGeometry will yield false.
No side effects; may be called at any time.

functions.name: SkPixelGeometryIsBGR
functions.description: Returns true if the provided pixel geometry enum is a known BGR geometry (horizontal or vertical). Use to conditionally enable BGR-specific rendering paths.
requirements: Argument geo must be a valid SkPixelGeometry value; kUnknown_SkPixelGeometry will yield false.
No side effects; may be called at any time.

functions.name: SkPixelGeometryIsH
functions.description: Returns true if the provided pixel geometry enum is a known horizontal geometry (RGB_H or BGR_H).
requirements: Argument geo must be a valid SkPixelGeometry value; kUnknown_SkPixelGeometry will yield false.
No side effects; may be called at any time.

functions.name: SkPixelGeometryIsV
functions.description: Returns true if the provided pixel geometry enum is a known vertical geometry (RGB_V or BGR_V).
requirements: Argument geo must be a valid SkPixelGeometry value; kUnknown_SkPixelGeometry will yield false.
No side effects; may be called at any time.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::SkSurfaceProps
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes a SkSurfaceProps with no flags, unknown pixel geometry, and platform-default text contrast/gamma. Use when you do not wish to specify any surface properties.
requirements: No arguments or preconditions.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::SkSurfaceProps
functions.description: Constructs SkSurfaceProps with the given flags and pixel geometry; text contrast and gamma are set to platform defaults. Use to control rendering behavior (e.g., device-independent fonts, dynamic MSAA, dithering, preserving transparent draws).
requirements: flags is a bitmask composed of SkSurfaceProps::Flags values.
pixelGeometry may be any SkPixelGeometry value, including kUnknown_SkPixelGeometry.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::SkSurfaceProps
functions.signature: SkSurfaceProps::SkSurfaceProps(uint32_t flags, SkPixelGeometry pixelGeometry, SkScalar textContrast, SkScalar textGamma)
functions.description: Constructs SkSurfaceProps with explicit flags, pixel geometry, text contrast, and text gamma. Use when fine-tuning LCD text rendering characteristics alongside surface flags.
requirements: flags is a bitmask composed of SkSurfaceProps::Flags values.
pixelGeometry may be any SkPixelGeometry value, including kUnknown_SkPixelGeometry.
textContrast should be within [SkSurfaceProps::kMinContrastInclusive, SkSurfaceProps::kMaxContrastInclusive] (i.e., [0, 1]).
textGamma should be within [SkSurfaceProps::kMinGammaInclusive, SkSurfaceProps::kMaxGammaExclusive] (i.e., [0, 4)).

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Replaces this instance’s properties with those of another SkSurfaceProps.
requirements: other must be a valid SkSurfaceProps instance. Self-assignment is allowed.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::cloneWithPixelGeometry
functions.description: Returns a copy of this SkSurfaceProps with the pixel geometry replaced by newPixelGeometry; all other properties (flags, text contrast, text gamma) are preserved. The original object is not modified.
requirements: newPixelGeometry may be any SkPixelGeometry value, including kUnknown_SkPixelGeometry.
May be called on any valid SkSurfaceProps instance.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::flags
functions.description: Returns the flags bitmask describing rendering behavior for the surface.
requirements: Object must be a valid SkSurfaceProps instance.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::pixelGeometry
functions.description: Returns the pixel geometry associated with the surface, or kUnknown_SkPixelGeometry if unspecified.
requirements: Object must be a valid SkSurfaceProps instance.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::textContrast
functions.description: Returns the text contrast value used for mask coverage blending.
requirements: Object must be a valid SkSurfaceProps instance.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::textGamma
functions.description: Returns the text gamma value used for mask coverage blending.
requirements: Object must be a valid SkSurfaceProps instance.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::isUseDeviceIndependentFonts
functions.description: Returns true if the kUseDeviceIndependentFonts_Flag is set in the flags, indicating device-independent font rendering preferences.
requirements: Object must be a valid SkSurfaceProps instance.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::isAlwaysDither
functions.description: Returns true if the kAlwaysDither_Flag is set, indicating dithering should always be enabled (primarily affects GPU backends).
requirements: Object must be a valid SkSurfaceProps instance.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::preservesTransparentDraws
functions.description: Returns true if the kPreservesTransparentDraws_Flag is set, meaning transparent draws are preserved rather than skipped.
requirements: Object must be a valid SkSurfaceProps instance.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::operator==
functions.description: Compares two SkSurfaceProps for equality of flags, pixel geometry, text contrast, and text gamma.
requirements: that must be a valid SkSurfaceProps instance.

functions.name: SkSurfaceProps::operator!=
functions.description: Returns true if this SkSurfaceProps differs from another in any of flags, pixel geometry, text contrast, or text gamma.
requirements: that must be a valid SkSurfaceProps instance.

functions.name: SkPicture::~SkPicture
functions.description: Destructor for SkPicture. Releases any resources owned by the picture instance. Called automatically when the last reference is released.

functions.name: SkPicture::MakeFromStream
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkPicture> MakeFromStream(SkStream* stream, const SkDeserialProcs* procs = nullptr);
functions.description: Deserializes a SkPicture from a stream. Returns a new SkPicture on success, or nullptr if the stream does not contain a valid serialized picture. Optional custom deserializers can be supplied via procs.
requirements: stream must point to a readable stream positioned at the start of a serialized SkPicture.
If procs is provided, its fPictureProc (if non-null) must be able to decode a picture from the provided bytes; fPictureCtx is passed through to that proc.
Caller must check for a nullptr return to handle invalid or corrupted data.

functions.name: SkPicture::MakeFromData
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkPicture> MakeFromData(const SkData* data, const SkDeserialProcs* procs = nullptr);
functions.description: Deserializes a SkPicture from an SkData buffer. Returns a new SkPicture on success, or nullptr if the data does not represent a valid serialized picture. Optional custom deserializers can be supplied via procs.
requirements: data must not be nullptr and must contain a complete serialized SkPicture payload.
If procs is provided, its fPictureProc (if non-null) must be able to decode a picture from the provided bytes; fPictureCtx is passed through to that proc.
Caller must check for a nullptr return to handle invalid or corrupted data.

functions.name: SkPicture::MakeFromData
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkPicture> MakeFromData(const void* data, size_t size, const SkDeserialProcs* procs = nullptr);
functions.description: Deserializes a SkPicture from a raw memory buffer. Returns a new SkPicture on success, or nullptr if the buffer does not represent a valid serialized picture. Optional custom deserializers can be supplied via procs.
requirements: data must not be nullptr if size > 0 and must point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
size must be the exact size of the serialized SkPicture data.
If procs is provided, its fPictureProc (if non-null) must be able to decode a picture from the provided bytes; fPictureCtx is passed through to that proc.
Caller must check for a nullptr return to handle invalid or corrupted data.

functions.name: SkPicture::playback
functions.signature: virtual void playback(SkCanvas* canvas, AbortCallback* callback = nullptr) const = 0;
functions.description: Replays this picture’s recorded draw commands onto the provided canvas. If callback is supplied, playback may be aborted early when callback->abort() returns true.
requirements: canvas must be a valid, non-null SkCanvas pointer for the duration of the call.

If callback is provided, it must remain alive for the entire duration of playback and its abort() must be thread-safe if playback is done on multiple threads (unknown; typical usage is single-threaded).

Caller should not assume any specific subset of commands executed if aborted; partial drawing is undefined beyond the guarantee that canvas state is restored to pre-playback save/clip/matrix state if abort occurs within saved state.

functions.name: SkPicture::cullRect
functions.description: Returns the cull rectangle provided when the picture was created. This is a bounding hint only and not an enforced clip.

functions.name: SkPicture::uniqueID
functions.description: Returns a process-unique non-zero identifier for this picture instance. Useful for caching or tracking.

functions.name: SkPicture::serialize
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkData> serialize(const SkSerialProcs* procs = nullptr) const;
functions.description: Serializes this picture into an SkData buffer. Custom encoding of embedded objects can be provided via procs. By default, SkImages are encoded as nullptr unless procs supplies an image encoder.
requirements: If procs is provided and its fPictureProc is non-null, it must accept a pointer to SkPicture and its user context.
Caller must handle the returned SkData; it will be non-null on success.
Embedded SkImages will be serialized as nullptr unless procs->fImageProc is provided to encode them.

functions.name: SkPicture::serialize
functions.signature: void serialize(SkWStream* stream, const SkSerialProcs* procs = nullptr) const;
functions.description: Serializes this picture into a writable stream. Custom encoding of embedded objects can be provided via procs. By default, SkImages are encoded as nullptr unless procs supplies an image encoder.
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable SkWStream for the duration of the call.
If procs is provided and its fPictureProc is non-null, it must accept a pointer to SkPicture and its user context.
Caller should handle any stream I/O errors; this function does not return a status.

functions.name: SkPicture::MakePlaceholder
functions.description: Creates a placeholder picture that draws nothing but carries the provided cull rectangle and a unique ID. Can be used as a stand-in to be intercepted during playback.
requirements: cull should define the placeholder dimensions in picture coordinates; no clipping is implied.

functions.name: SkPicture::approximateOpCount
functions.signature: virtual int approximateOpCount(bool nested = false) const = 0;
functions.description: Returns an approximate count of operations represented by this picture. If nested is true, includes counts from nested pictures; otherwise counts only top-level operations.

functions.name: SkPicture::approximateBytesUsed
functions.description: Returns the approximate number of bytes used by this picture, excluding large externally referenced objects.

functions.name: SkPicture::makeShader
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> makeShader(SkTileMode tmx, SkTileMode tmy, SkFilterMode mode, const SkMatrix* localMatrix, const SkRect* tileRect) const;
functions.description: Creates a shader that renders this picture as a tiled image. Tiling modes, filtering, an optional local sampling matrix, and an optional tile rectangle in picture coordinates can be specified. The function never returns null.
requirements: localMatrix may be nullptr; if provided, it is applied when sampling the picture.
tileRect may be nullptr; if provided, it specifies the subset/superset of the picture used for building a tile and is not affected by localMatrix (no scaling implied, only translation/cropping).

functions.name: SkPicture::makeShader
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> makeShader(SkTileMode tmx, SkTileMode tmy, SkFilterMode mode) const;
functions.description: Convenience overload that creates a picture shader using the specified tiling and filtering, with no local matrix and using the picture bounds as the tile rectangle. The function never returns null.

functions.name: SkPicture::AbortCallback::~AbortCallback
functions.description: Destructor for AbortCallback. Override if the callback manages resources; default implementation does nothing.

functions.name: SkPicture::AbortCallback::abort
functions.description: Invoked during picture playback to determine whether playback should be aborted. Return true to stop playback; false to continue. The exact command at which playback stops is undefined.
requirements: Must be safe to call from the playback context. Implementations should avoid throwing exceptions and should complete quickly to avoid stalling playback.

functions.name: SkPictureRecorder::SkPictureRecorder
functions.description: Default constructor for SkPictureRecorder. Creates a recorder object that can begin recording drawing commands into an SkPicture or SkDrawable via beginRecording().

functions.name: SkPictureRecorder::~SkPictureRecorder
functions.description: Destructor for SkPictureRecorder. Cleans up any recorder state. Recording should be finished before destruction using one of the finishRecording* methods.

functions.name: SkPictureRecorder::beginRecording
functions.signature: SkCanvas* SkPictureRecorder::beginRecording(const SkRect& bounds, sk_sp<SkBBoxHierarchy> bbh)
functions.description: Begins recording drawing commands into a new recording using the provided cull rect and an optional bounding box hierarchy (BBH) implementation. Returns the SkCanvas to issue draw calls to; these are recorded until a finishRecording* call is made.
requirements: bounds specifies the cull rectangle; behavior for drawing outside this rect is undefined (it may or may not be recorded/drawn).
bbh is optional; a null sk_sp indicates no acceleration structure will be used.
The returned SkCanvas is owned by the recorder; do not delete or ref/unref it.
The returned SkCanvas becomes invalid after a call to any finishRecording* method; do not use it thereafter.
Call one of finishRecordingAsPicture(), finishRecordingAsPictureWithCull(), or finishRecordingAsDrawable() to end the recording.

functions.name: SkPictureRecorder::getRecordingCanvas
functions.description: Returns the current recording canvas if a recording is active, or null if not. Does not change the canvas’s ref count.
requirements: Only returns non-null while a recording session is active (i.e., after beginRecording() and before a finishRecording* call).
Caller must not ref/unref or delete the returned SkCanvas; ownership remains with the recorder.
Do not use the returned canvas after a finishRecording* call, as it becomes invalid.

functions.name: SkPictureRecorder::finishRecordingAsPicture
functions.description: Ends the current recording and returns an immutable SkPicture containing the recorded content. Invalidates the recording canvas returned by beginRecording()/getRecordingCanvas(). Any SkDrawable objects recorded are snapshotted into the picture at record time; the picture does not hold live references to them.
requirements: Must be called to end a recording begun with beginRecording().
After this call, any previously returned SkCanvas from beginRecording()/getRecordingCanvas() is invalid and must not be used.
The returned SkPicture is immutable; subsequent changes to any original SkDrawable sources will not affect it.
The returned object is managed by sk_sp; retain it as needed via smart-pointer semantics.

functions.name: SkPictureRecorder::finishRecordingAsPictureWithCull
functions.description: Ends the current recording and returns an immutable SkPicture, updating the cull rectangle used for BBH generation to the provided cullRect before finalizing. Otherwise behaves like finishRecordingAsPicture().
requirements: Must be called to end a recording begun with beginRecording().
After this call, any previously returned SkCanvas from beginRecording()/getRecordingCanvas() is invalid and must not be used.
cullRect replaces the initial cull rect for BBH generation and subsequent culling.
The returned SkPicture is immutable; subsequent changes to any original SkDrawable sources will not affect it.
The returned object is managed by sk_sp; retain it as needed via smart-pointer semantics.

functions.name: SkPictureRecorder::finishRecordingAsDrawable
functions.description: Ends the current recording and returns an SkDrawable that replays the recorded content. Unlike finishRecordingAsPicture(), the returned drawable may hold live references to recorded SkDrawables, so drawing it (or making a snapshot) reflects their current state. Invalidates the recording canvas.
requirements: Must be called to end a recording begun with beginRecording().
After this call, any previously returned SkCanvas from beginRecording()/getRecordingCanvas() is invalid and must not be used.
The returned SkDrawable may contain live references to nested SkDrawables and will reflect their current state when drawn or when snapshot via drawable->makePictureSnapshot().
The returned object is managed by sk_sp; retain it as needed via smart-pointer semantics.

functions.name: SkData::operator==
functions.description: Compares two SkData instances for equality. Returns true if both have the same size and identical byte contents. All empty SkData objects compare equal.

functions.name: SkData::operator!=
functions.description: Logical inequality operator. Returns true if operator== would return false.

functions.name: SkData::equals
functions.description: Null-safe equality check. Returns false if other is null; otherwise compares this and *other for equal size and contents (same semantics as operator==).

functions.name: SkData::Equals
functions.signature: static bool SkData::Equals(const SkData* a, const SkData* b)
functions.description: Null-safe static equality test for two SkData pointers. Returns true if both are null, or if both are non-null and have the same size and identical bytes.

functions.name: SkData::size
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes stored in this SkData.

functions.name: SkData::data
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the underlying data buffer. The pointer and size remain constant for the lifetime of the SkData.

functions.name: SkData::empty
functions.description: Returns true if this SkData contains zero bytes.

functions.name: SkData::bytes
functions.description: Returns the data pointer reinterpreted as a pointer to bytes (uint8_t).

functions.name: SkData::byteSpan
functions.description: Returns a span view over the bytes of this SkData, covering [bytes(), bytes()+size()).

functions.name: SkData::writable_data
functions.description: Returns a writable pointer to the underlying data buffer. Intended for cautious, controlled mutation scenarios.
requirements: Do not allow other owners of this SkData to access it concurrently from another thread while writing (thread-safety requirement stated).

functions.name: SkData::copySubset
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkData> SkData::copySubset(size_t offset, size_t length) const
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of a subset of this data starting at offset and spanning length bytes. Returns nullptr if offset + length exceeds size().
requirements: offset + length must be <= size() to obtain a non-null result.

functions.name: SkData::shareSubset
functions.description: Returns a SkData that references a subset of this data without copying. Retains a reference to the original data. Returns nullptr if offset + length exceeds size().
requirements: offset + length must be <= size() to obtain a non-null result.
Caller should not assume a deep copy; the returned data shares storage with the original.

functions.name: SkData::shareSubset
functions.signature: sk_sp<const SkData> SkData::shareSubset(size_t offset, size_t length) const
functions.description: Const overload. Returns a SkData that references a subset of this data without copying. Retains a reference to the original data. Returns nullptr if offset + length exceeds size().
requirements: offset + length must be <= size() to obtain a non-null result.
Returned object shares storage with the original; no deep copy is made.

functions.name: SkData::copyRange
functions.signature: size_t SkData::copyRange(size_t offset, size_t length, void* buffer) const
functions.description: Copies up to length bytes starting at offset into a caller-provided buffer. The method clamps offset/length to this->size() and returns the actual number of bytes copied. If buffer is NULL, no bytes are written and only the would-be number of bytes is returned.
requirements: If buffer is non-null, it must point to a writable region of at least the returned number of bytes.
Function may clamp the request; callers should use the return value to know how many bytes were (or would be) copied.

functions.name: SkData::MakeWithCopy
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkData> SkData::MakeWithCopy(const void* data, size_t length)
functions.description: Allocates a new SkData and copies length bytes from data into its own storage.
requirements: Unknown whether data may be null when length > 0 (not specified). Callers should provide a valid pointer when length > 0.
If length == 0, data may be ignored.

functions.name: SkData::MakeUninitialized
functions.description: Allocates a new SkData with uninitialized contents of the given length. Caller may write to the buffer via writable_data() before the object is shared.
requirements: Any writes via writable_data() must be performed before another ref() is made (before sharing the SkData).

functions.name: SkData::MakeZeroInitialized
functions.description: Allocates a new SkData with zero-initialized contents of the given length. Caller may write to the buffer via writable_data() before the object is shared.
requirements: Any writes via writable_data() must be performed before another ref() is made (before sharing the SkData).

functions.name: SkData::MakeWithCString
functions.description: Creates a new SkData by copying a C-string, including its terminating NUL. The resulting size() equals strlen(cstr) + 1. If cstr is NULL, it is treated as an empty string.

functions.name: SkData::MakeWithProc
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkData> SkData::MakeWithProc(const void* ptr, size_t length, ReleaseProc proc, void* ctx)
functions.description: Creates a new SkData that refers to an existing buffer ptr of length bytes. When the SkData is destroyed, proc (if non-null) is called with (ptr, ctx) to release the memory.
requirements: proc may be NULL; in that case SkData will not free ptr.
If proc is provided, it must be safe to call when the SkData is destroyed and must correctly release the memory/resources for ptr.
ptr must reference at least length bytes for the lifetime of the SkData or until proc releases it.

functions.name: SkData::MakeWithoutCopy
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkData> SkData::MakeWithoutCopy(const void* data, size_t length)
functions.description: Creates a new SkData that refers to an existing, immutable buffer without copying. Intended for data with static/global lifetime.
requirements: data must outlive the returned SkData (SkData will not free it).
The buffer is treated as const; callers must not modify it through other means while shared by SkData.

functions.name: SkData::MakeFromMalloc
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkData> SkData::MakeFromMalloc(const void* data, size_t length)
functions.description: Creates a new SkData that takes ownership of a buffer allocated by malloc. The SkData will free it (via sk_free) when destroyed.
requirements: data must have been allocated with malloc (or be compatible with sk_free).
Ownership of data is transferred to SkData; do not free it manually after calling this.

functions.name: SkData::MakeFromFileName
functions.description: Creates a new SkData by reading the entire file at the given path. Returns null on failure.
requirements: path must refer to a readable file for success.

functions.name: SkData::MakeFromFILE
functions.description: Creates a new SkData by reading from the given stdio FILE*. Does not take ownership and does not close the FILE. The FILE must be opened for reading. Returns null on failure.
requirements: f must be a valid FILE* opened for reading.
Caller retains ownership and may close f at its convenience.

functions.name: SkData::MakeFromFD
functions.description: Creates a new SkData by reading from the given file descriptor. Does not take ownership and does not close the descriptor. The descriptor must be open for reading. Returns null on failure.
requirements: fd must be a valid file descriptor opened for reading.
Caller retains ownership and may close fd at its convenience.

functions.name: SkData::MakeFromStream
functions.description: Attempts to read size bytes from the given SkStream into a new SkData. Returns null on read failure. The stream's cursor may be advanced regardless of success.
requirements: Stream pointer should be valid and positioned appropriately for reading size bytes.
Caller should not assume the stream position is unchanged after the call.

functions.name: SkData::MakeSubset
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkData> SkData::MakeSubset(const SkData* src, size_t offset, size_t length)
functions.description: Deprecated helper equivalent to src->shareSubset(offset, length), except that it returns an empty SkData instead of null if the range is out of bounds.
requirements: src must be non-null.
If offset + length is out of range, the function returns an empty SkData instead of null.

functions.name: SkData::MakeEmpty
functions.description: Returns a new or shared empty SkData. The caller receives a ref and must eventually release it (via smart pointer semantics).

functions.name: SkData::isEmpty
functions.description: Deprecated; use empty(). Returns true if this SkData contains zero bytes.

functions.name: SkStream::MakeFromFile
functions.description: Create a stream backed by the file at path. Returns nullptr on failure. Use when you need an SkStreamAsset from a file path.
requirements: path must point to a readable file; if the file cannot be opened, nullptr is returned

functions.name: SkStream::read
functions.signature: virtual size_t SkStream::read(void* buffer, size_t size) = 0
functions.description: Read or skip bytes from the stream. If buffer is nullptr, skip size bytes; otherwise copy up to size bytes into buffer. Returns the number of bytes actually read/skipped.
requirements: If buffer is not nullptr, it must point to at least size writable bytes
size may be any non-negative value expressible by size_t
Implementations must not read past stream end; return the actual number of bytes read/skipped

functions.name: SkStream::skip
functions.description: Skip size bytes in the stream. Convenience wrapper that calls read(nullptr, size). Returns the number of bytes actually skipped.
requirements: No buffer provided; behavior and limits are the same as read(nullptr, size)
size may be any non-negative value expressible by size_t

functions.name: SkStream::peek
functions.signature: virtual size_t SkStream::peek(void* buffer, size_t size) const
functions.description: Attempt to read up to size bytes without advancing the stream position. If unsupported or no bytes can be peeked, returns 0 and leaves buffer unchanged.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL and must point to at least size writable bytes
The stream position must be unchanged after this call regardless of success or failure

functions.name: SkStream::isAtEnd
functions.description: Report whether all bytes in the stream have been read. May return false if the final length is unknown even if nothing more is currently available. May return true early or late relative to an unsuccessful read.

functions.name: SkStream::readS8
functions.description: Read a signed 8-bit integer from the stream into the provided pointer. Returns true on success, false on failure or insufficient bytes. Implementation not shown in this header.
requirements: Output pointer must be non-null and point to writable int8_t storage
Stream must contain at least 1 byte to succeed

functions.name: SkStream::readS16
functions.description: Read a signed 16-bit integer from the stream into the provided pointer. Returns true on success. Endianness/encoding unspecified in this header.
requirements: Output pointer must be non-null and point to writable int16_t storage
Stream must contain at least 2 bytes to succeed

functions.name: SkStream::readS32
functions.description: Read a signed 32-bit integer from the stream into the provided pointer. Returns true on success. Endianness/encoding unspecified in this header.
requirements: Output pointer must be non-null and point to writable int32_t storage
Stream must contain at least 4 bytes to succeed

functions.name: SkStream::readS64
functions.description: Read a signed 64-bit integer from the stream into the provided pointer. Returns true on success. Endianness/encoding unspecified in this header.
requirements: Output pointer must be non-null and point to writable int64_t storage
Stream must contain at least 8 bytes to succeed

functions.name: SkStream::readU8
functions.description: Read an unsigned 8-bit integer into i. Delegates to readS8 reinterpret-casting the pointer. Returns true on success.
requirements: i must be non-null and point to writable uint8_t storage
Stream must contain at least 1 byte to succeed

functions.name: SkStream::readU16
functions.description: Read an unsigned 16-bit integer into i. Delegates to readS16 reinterpret-casting the pointer. Returns true on success.
requirements: i must be non-null and point to writable uint16_t storage
Stream must contain at least 2 bytes to succeed

functions.name: SkStream::readU32
functions.description: Read an unsigned 32-bit integer into i. Delegates to readS32 reinterpret-casting the pointer. Returns true on success.
requirements: i must be non-null and point to writable uint32_t storage
Stream must contain at least 4 bytes to succeed

functions.name: SkStream::readU64
functions.description: Read an unsigned 64-bit integer into i. Delegates to readS64 reinterpret-casting the pointer. Returns true on success.
requirements: i must be non-null and point to writable uint64_t storage
Stream must contain at least 8 bytes to succeed

functions.name: SkStream::readBool
functions.description: Read a boolean value (1 byte) into b. Non-zero is treated as true. Returns true on success.
requirements: b must be non-null and point to writable bool storage
Stream must contain at least 1 byte to succeed

functions.name: SkStream::readScalar
functions.description: Read an SkScalar from the stream into the provided pointer. Returns true on success. Exact size/encoding depends on SkScalar configuration; not specified here.
requirements: Output pointer must be non-null and point to writable SkScalar storage
Stream must contain enough bytes for one SkScalar

functions.name: SkStream::readPackedUInt
functions.description: Read a variable-length, packed unsigned integer into the provided size_t pointer. Returns true on success. Encoding details are not in this header.
requirements: Output pointer must be non-null and point to writable size_t storage
Stream must contain enough bytes for a packed integer encoding

functions.name: SkStream::rewind
functions.description: Attempt to reset the stream position to the beginning. Default implementation returns false (not supported). Streams that support rewind override this.
requirements: May be unsupported; callers must check the return value

functions.name: SkStream::duplicate
functions.description: Create a new stream duplicating the same data, positioned at the beginning. May return nullptr if duplication is unsupported.
requirements: Caller must handle nullptr return if duplication is unsupported

functions.name: SkStream::fork
functions.description: Create a new stream sharing the same data, positioned at the same position as this stream. May return nullptr if forking is unsupported.
requirements: Caller must handle nullptr return if forking is unsupported

functions.name: SkStream::hasPosition
functions.description: Return whether the stream can report its current position. Default returns false; seekable streams override.

functions.name: SkStream::getPosition
functions.description: Return the current position in the stream. Default returns 0 if unsupported.
requirements: If hasPosition() is false, the value may be meaningless; callers should check hasPosition() first

functions.name: SkStream::seek
functions.description: Seek to an absolute position. If unsupported, returns false. Seeking past end clamps to end of stream.
requirements: position is an absolute offset from the beginning of the stream
Callers must check the boolean return for success
If attempting to seek past end, resulting position will be at end

functions.name: SkStream::move
functions.description: Seek to a position relative to the current position. If unsupported, returns false. Positions outside the stream are clamped to the beginning or end.
requirements: offset is relative to the current position and may be positive or negative
Callers must check the boolean return for success

functions.name: SkStream::hasLength
functions.description: Return whether the stream can report its total length. Default returns false; asset streams override.

functions.name: SkStream::getLength
functions.description: Return the total length of the stream. Default returns 0 if unsupported.
requirements: If hasLength() is false, the value may be meaningless; callers should check hasLength() first

functions.name: SkStream::getMemoryBase
functions.description: Return a pointer to the beginning of the underlying memory, if available. Default returns nullptr for non-memory streams.
requirements: Pointer, if non-null, is read-only and valid for the lifetime defined by the stream implementation

functions.name: SkStream::getData
functions.description: Return an SkData snapshot of the stream's underlying data if available. Default returns nullptr.
requirements: Caller must handle nullptr when data is unavailable

functions.name: SkStreamRewindable::rewind
functions.description: Reset position to the beginning. For SkStreamRewindable, this is required and must succeed or accurately report failure. Pure-virtual in this class.
requirements: Implementation must override and attempt to rewind; callers should check return value

functions.name: SkStreamRewindable::duplicate
functions.description: Create a duplicate stream positioned at the beginning. Guaranteed available for rewindable streams (pure-virtual hook implemented by subclasses). May still return nullptr if subclass cannot duplicate.
requirements: Caller must handle nullptr return

functions.name: SkStreamSeekable::duplicate
functions.description: Create a duplicate of this seekable stream at the beginning. Implemented via subclass hook.
requirements: Caller must handle nullptr return

functions.name: SkStreamSeekable::hasPosition
functions.description: Seekable streams always report position. Overrides to return true.

functions.name: SkStreamSeekable::getPosition
functions.description: Return the current absolute position within the stream. Pure-virtual; subclasses must implement.

functions.name: SkStreamSeekable::seek
functions.description: Seek to an absolute position. Pure-virtual; subclasses must implement. Clamps to end if seeking past end (per base class contract).
requirements: Callers must check the boolean return for success

functions.name: SkStreamSeekable::move
functions.description: Seek to a position relative to the current position. Pure-virtual; subclasses must implement. Clamps to bounds (per base class contract).
requirements: Callers must check the boolean return for success

functions.name: SkStreamSeekable::fork
functions.description: Create a new stream positioned the same as this one. Implemented via subclass hook. May return nullptr if unsupported.
requirements: Caller must handle nullptr return

functions.name: SkStreamAsset::hasLength

functions.name: SkString::insert
functions.signature: void SkString::insert(size_t offset, const char text[])

requirements: `text` must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated C string.
`offset` must be between 0 and size(), or (size_t)-1 to append; behavior for other values is unspecified here.

functions.name: SkDocument::beginPage
functions.signature: SkCanvas* SkDocument::beginPage(SkScalar width, SkScalar height, const SkRect* content = nullptr)
functions.description: Begins a new page in the document and returns a document-owned SkCanvas to draw that page’s content. If a page is already active, this implicitly ends it before starting the new one. The returned canvas remains valid only until endPage() or close() is called, or the document is destroyed. The optional content rectangle may hint the intended content area; null is allowed. Typical usage: canvas = doc->beginPage(w, h, ...); draw; doc->endPage();
requirements: May be called even if a page is currently active; doing so will implicitly call endPage() on the active page.
The returned SkCanvas is owned by the SkDocument; callers must not delete it and must not use it after endPage(), close(), or document destruction.
Callers should finish the page by calling endPage() (or by calling close(), which also ends the page and invalidates the canvas).
The content parameter may be null; if non-null it must point to a valid SkRect for the duration of the call.
Width and height are passed as SkScalar; specific unit, range, and validation behavior are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: SkDocument::endPage
functions.description: Ends the current page. After this call, the SkCanvas returned by the most recent beginPage() is invalid and must not be used. Use this when you have finished drawing the current page.
requirements: Should be called only when a page is currently active (i.e., after a successful beginPage()).
After calling endPage(), do not use the previously returned SkCanvas.
Calling beginPage() while a page is active will implicitly call endPage() first.

functions.name: SkDocument::close
functions.description: Closes the document and finalizes output to the underlying file/stream. After close(), no new pages can be added and any active page’s canvas becomes invalid. Deleting the document will automatically call close() if needed.
requirements: Should be called when all pages have been drawn; after close() you must not call beginPage().
Do not use any page canvas after close().
Close is expected to be called at most once per document instance (additional calls are unspecified; behavior not documented).

functions.name: SkDocument::abort
functions.description: Immediately aborts document production. Output written to the stream must be ignored and should not be trusted. Use when you need to stop generation without producing a valid document.
requirements: After abort(), the produced stream output is invalid and must not be consumed.
Further use of the document after abort() is unspecified (unknown); callers should avoid adding pages or closing for a valid output.

functions.name: SkDocument::getStream
functions.description: Protected helper for subclasses to access the underlying SkWStream so they can write as pages are produced.
requirements: Intended for use by subclasses only; not part of the public document-writing workflow.
Returned pointer is the stream supplied at construction time; lifetime is managed externally to SkDocument (exact ownership semantics are not documented here, unknown).
Callers must ensure any direct writes are consistent with the document’s write protocol defined by the concrete subclass.

functions.name: SkDocument::getState
functions.description: Returns the document’s current state: between pages, in a page, or closed. Useful for subclass or internal logic to gate operations based on lifecycle.
requirements: Read-only query; may be called at any time to check state.
Interpretation of states is: kBetweenPages_State, kInPage_State, kClosed_State, but exact transitions beyond those documented in comments are not further specified.

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::SubsamplingFactors
functions.description: Returns the subsampling ratio between Y/A and U/V in x and y for a given Subsampling mode. Useful for computing chroma plane resolutions relative to luma.
requirements: Input Subsampling must be a valid enum value; kUnknown yields unknown behavior based on implementation (not specified).
Return is a pair {x_factor, y_factor} giving the Y/A-to-UV resolution ratio.

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::PlaneSubsamplingFactors
functions.signature: static std::tuple<int, int> SkYUVAInfo::PlaneSubsamplingFactors(SkYUVAInfo::PlaneConfig, SkYUVAInfo::Subsampling, int planeIdx)
functions.description: Returns SubsamplingFactors(Subsampling) for UV planes and {1,1} for non-UV planes when inputs are valid; returns {0,0} for invalid PlaneConfig/Subsampling/planeIdx combinations.
requirements: planeIdx must refer to a valid plane index for the provided PlaneConfig.
The PlaneConfig/Subsampling combination must be compatible (e.g., subsampling other than k444 is only valid when U and V are in different planes from Y and A).
Callers must treat a return value of {0,0} as an invalid-input indicator.

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::PlaneDimensions
functions.signature: static int SkYUVAInfo::PlaneDimensions(SkISize imageDimensions, SkYUVAInfo::PlaneConfig, SkYUVAInfo::Subsampling, SkEncodedOrigin, SkISize planeDimensions[SkYUVAInfo::kMaxPlanes])
functions.description: Computes the expected size of each plane given the image dimensions as displayed, plane configuration, subsampling, and origin. Writes the per-plane dimensions as stored in memory (which may be rotated relative to display orientation) and returns the number of planes written.
requirements: planeDimensions must point to an array with capacity at least SkYUVAInfo::kMaxPlanes.
imageDimensions are in display orientation (after applying origin), but outputs are in memory/storage orientation.
Caller should only read planeDimensions[0..ret-1], where ret is the return value.
PlaneConfig/Subsampling/Origin must be a valid combination for the intended image format.

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::NumPlanes
functions.description: Returns the number of planes implied by the given PlaneConfig. Returns 0 for kUnknown.
requirements: PlaneConfig must be one of the defined enum values; kUnknown yields 0.

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::NumChannelsInPlane
functions.description: Returns the number of Y/U/V/A channels present in plane i for the given PlaneConfig, or 0 if i is invalid for that config.
requirements: i should be a non-negative plane index; values outside the valid range for the config yield 0.

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::GetYUVALocations
functions.description: Converts a PlaneConfig plus per-plane channel flags into a YUVALocations mapping. If the flags don’t match the config (e.g., not enough channels in a plane), returns an invalid mapping (plane indices are -1).
requirements: planeChannelFlags must provide channel flag values for each plane implied by PlaneConfig (at least NumPlanes(config) entries).
Caller must validate the returned locations (e.g., check for -1 plane indices) before use.

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::HasAlpha
functions.description: Returns true if the PlaneConfig includes alpha in any plane; false otherwise.

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::SkYUVAInfo
functions.description: Default-constructs a SkYUVAInfo with unknown/zero fields. Typically followed by assignment or initialization via other APIs before use.
requirements: Object fields are default-initialized: dimensions {0,0}; PlaneConfig kUnknown; Subsampling kUnknown; YUV color space kIdentity; origin kTopLeft; siting centered.
isValid() will return false until a non-unknown PlaneConfig is set.

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::operator=

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::computeTotalBytes
functions.signature: size_t SkYUVAInfo::computeTotalBytes(const size_t rowBytes[SkYUVAInfo::kMaxPlanes], size_t planeSizes[SkYUVAInfo::kMaxPlanes] = nullptr) const
functions.description: Given per-plane row bytes, computes the total allocation size for all planes. Optionally returns each plane’s size in planeSizes. On overflow, returns SIZE_MAX and sets all planeSizes entries to SIZE_MAX.
requirements: rowBytes must provide entries for each plane (at least numPlanes() elements expected).
Caller must handle SIZE_MAX as an overflow/error indicator and must not use planeSizes except to detect overflow when they are all SIZE_MAX.
planeSizes may be nullptr if per-plane sizes are not needed.

requirements: channelFlags must provide flags for each plane implied by this->planeConfig() (at least numPlanes() entries).

functions.name: SkYUVAInfo::makeDimensions
functions.description: Returns a copy of this SkYUVAInfo with replaced dimensions. If the passed dimensions are empty, the result will be an invalid SkYUVAInfo.

functions.description: Returns a SupportedDataTypes instance that enables all legal combinations of PlaneConfig and DataType (i.e., any plane/channel count for which a default SkColorType exists). Use to quickly allow any supported YUVA plane channel formats.

functions.description: Enables support in this SupportedDataTypes instance for pixmaps that have numChannels channels where each channel is represented by dataType. Use to incrementally allow specific channel-count/data-type combinations.
requirements: numChannels should be between 1 and 4 inclusive (the structure supports up to 4 channels).

functions.signature: static constexpr SkColorType SkYUVAPixmapInfo::DefaultColorTypeForDataType(SkYUVAPixmapInfo::DataType dataType, int numChannels)
functions.description: Returns the default SkColorType to store numChannels channels when each channel is represented by dataType. If no appropriate color type exists, returns kUnknown_SkColorType. Intended for selecting plane SkColorTypes given a YUVA channel representation.
requirements: numChannels must be 1, 2, 3, or 4.
dataType must be one of: kUnorm8, kUnorm16, kFloat16, or kUnorm10_Unorm2.
Caller must handle kUnknown_SkColorType when no mapping exists.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmapInfo::NumChannelsAndDataType
functions.description: For a given SkColorType, returns the number of YUVA channels a plane of this color type can store and the per-channel DataType. If ct is not supported as a YUVA plane, the number of channels is 0 and the DataType in the tuple should be ignored.
requirements: ct must be a valid SkColorType value.
Caller must check the first tuple element; if it is 0 the color type is unsupported for YUVA planes and the returned DataType must be ignored.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmapInfo::computeTotalBytes
functions.description: Computes the total byte size required to store all planes back-to-back. Optionally fills planeSizes with per-plane sizes when non-null. Returns 0 and fills 0s if this is invalid. If the total size would overflow, returns SIZE_MAX and sets all planeSizes entries to SIZE_MAX.
requirements: If planeSizes is non-null, it must point to an array with at least kMaxPlanes entries.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmapInfo::initPixmapsFromSingleAllocation
functions.description: Initializes the first numPlanes() entries of the provided pixmaps array to point into the provided single contiguous memory allocation sized for all planes. Remaining pixmaps entries are default-initialized. Returns false if this SkYUVAPixmapInfo is invalid.
requirements: memory must point to an allocation of at least computeTotalBytes() bytes starting at memory and must remain valid for the lifetime of any SkPixmaps referencing it.
pixmaps must point to an array with at least kMaxPlanes entries.
This SkYUVAPixmapInfo must be valid for initialization to succeed.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmapInfo::isValid
functions.description: Returns true if configured with a non-empty-dimension SkYUVAInfo and compatible color types and row bytes.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmapInfo::isSupported
functions.description: Returns true if this (valid) SkYUVAPixmapInfo uses color types allowed by the given SupportedDataTypes. Useful for filtering candidate formats against a backend’s capabilities.
requirements: supported must be a properly initialized SupportedDataTypes instance.
If this SkYUVAPixmapInfo is invalid, the result may be false; callers should generally check isValid() first.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmaps::RecommendedRGBAColorType
functions.description: Returns the recommended RGBA SkColorType to pair with the given YUVA DataType when producing RGBA outputs. Intended as a helper for selecting a compatible RGBA color type.
requirements: dataType must be a valid SkYUVAPixmaps::DataType value.
Caller must handle cases where the recommendation may depend on backend support (details not documented here).

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmaps::Allocate
functions.description: Allocates internal storage for all planes described by yuvaPixmapInfo and returns a SkYUVAPixmaps that owns this storage and exposes SkPixmap views to it.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmaps::FromData
functions.signature: static SkYUVAPixmaps SkYUVAPixmaps::FromData(const SkYUVAPixmapInfo& info, sk_sp<SkData> data)
functions.description: Creates a SkYUVAPixmaps whose plane pixels are backed by the provided SkData. The SkYUVAPixmaps retains the SkData, thus owning the storage.
requirements: info should be valid to get a valid result.
data must be non-null and point to at least info.computeTotalBytes() bytes starting at offset 0.
Caller must ensure data's contents match the expected plane layout.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmaps::MakeCopy
functions.description: Returns a deep copy of src. The resulting SkYUVAPixmaps owns its planes’ storage.
requirements: src may be valid or invalid; copying an invalid src likely produces an invalid result.
Sufficient memory must be available for the deep copy.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmaps::FromExternalMemory
functions.signature: static SkYUVAPixmaps SkYUVAPixmaps::FromExternalMemory(const SkYUVAPixmapInfo& info, void* memory)
functions.description: Wraps a caller-provided memory block as backing storage for the planes described by info. The returned SkYUVAPixmaps does not own the memory; the caller must keep it allocated and unchanged while in use.
requirements: info should be valid to get a valid result.
memory must be non-null and point to at least info.computeTotalBytes() bytes starting at memory.
Caller must ensure the memory remains valid and correctly laid out for the lifetime of the SkYUVAPixmaps and any SkPixmap views.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmaps::FromExternalPixmaps
functions.signature: static SkYUVAPixmaps SkYUVAPixmaps::FromExternalPixmaps(const SkYUVAInfo& yuvaInfo, const SkPixmap pixmaps[SkYUVAPixmaps::kMaxPlanes])
functions.description: Wraps existing SkPixmap planes according to yuvaInfo. The returned SkYUVAPixmaps does not own the pixel memory. Returns an invalid SkYUVAPixmaps if the pixmaps are incompatible with yuvaInfo (e.g., wrong plane count, mismatched dimensions, or insufficient channel counts).
requirements: pixmaps must provide at least yuvaInfo.numPlanes() entries; extra entries are ignored.
Each provided SkPixmap must match the plane dimensions implied by yuvaInfo and provide sufficient channels for the intended Y/U/V/A data.
Caller must ensure the wrapped SkPixmap pixel memory remains valid during use (no ownership is taken).

functions.description: Default constructor. Produces an invalid SkYUVAPixmaps until initialized by a factory or assignment.

functions.name: SkYUVAPixmaps::toYUVALocations

functions.name: SkVertices::MakeCopy
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkVertices> SkVertices::MakeCopy(VertexMode mode, int vertexCount, const SkPoint positions[], const SkPoint texs[], const SkColor colors[], int indexCount, const uint16_t indices[])
functions.description: Creates an immutable SkVertices by copying client-provided arrays. Texture coordinates and colors may be null. If indexCount is 0, indices are ignored and the geometry is treated as non-indexed. Intended for use with SkCanvas::drawVertices.

vertexCount must be >= 0.
positions must point to an array of at least vertexCount SkPoint elements and must not be null when vertexCount > 0.
texs may be null; if non-null it must point to an array of at least vertexCount SkPoint elements.
colors may be null; if non-null it must point to an array of at least vertexCount SkColor elements.
indexCount must be >= 0.
indices are ignored if indexCount == 0; if indexCount > 0, indices must point to an array of at least indexCount uint16_t elements.

functions.name: SkVertices::Builder::Builder
functions.signature: SkVertices::Builder::Builder(VertexMode mode, int vertexCount, int indexCount, uint32_t flags)
functions.description: Constructs a mutable builder for assembling an SkVertices object with the given topology, counts, and attribute flags. After filling out the returned attribute/index buffers, call detach() to obtain the finalized immutable SkVertices.
requirements: mode must be one of kTriangles_VertexMode, kTriangleStrip_VertexMode, or kTriangleFan_VertexMode.
vertexCount must be >= 0.
indexCount must be >= 0.
flags is a bitmask of BuilderFlags; set kHasTexCoords_BuilderFlag to allocate texCoords, set kHasColors_BuilderFlag to allocate colors.
Call isValid() to confirm successful allocation before accessing buffer pointers.
If indexCount specifies indexed triangle fans, the builder may convert them to indexed triangles on finalize (per comments); caller should not rely on internal index storage format.

functions.name: SkVertices::Builder::isValid
functions.description: Returns true if the builder was constructed successfully and holds valid storage for vertices (i.e., internal fVertices is non-null). Use this to gate access to positions/indices/attributes and to proceed to detach.
requirements: Must be called on a constructed Builder instance.
If returns false, do not call positions(), indices(), texCoords(), colors(), or detach().

functions.name: SkVertices::Builder::positions
functions.description: Returns a writable pointer to the positions array of size vertexCount for populating vertex positions in the builder.
requirements: Builder must be valid (isValid() must return true).
The returned pointer, if non-null, must not be freed by the caller and is only valid while the Builder is alive and before detach().
Caller must write at most vertexCount elements.

functions.name: SkVertices::Builder::indices
functions.description: Returns a writable pointer to the index array used to specify indexed geometry, or null if the builder was created with indexCount == 0.
requirements: Builder must be valid (isValid() must return true).
If indexCount == 0, this returns null and must not be dereferenced.
If non-null, caller must write at most indexCount elements.
The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller and is only valid while the Builder is alive and before detach().

functions.name: SkVertices::Builder::texCoords
functions.description: Returns a writable pointer to the texture coordinate array of size vertexCount, or null if texture coordinates are not allocated. Note: if there are custom attributes (not exposed here), this will always be null.
requirements: Builder must be valid (isValid() must return true).
This returns null if kHasTexCoords_BuilderFlag was not set during construction or if custom attributes are present.
If non-null, caller must write at most vertexCount elements.
The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller and is only valid while the Builder is alive and before detach().

functions.name: SkVertices::Builder::colors
functions.description: Returns a writable pointer to the per-vertex color array of size vertexCount, or null if colors are not allocated. Note: if there are custom attributes (not exposed here), this will always be null.
requirements: Builder must be valid (isValid() must return true).
This returns null if kHasColors_BuilderFlag was not set during construction or if custom attributes are present.
If non-null, caller must write at most vertexCount elements.
The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller and is only valid while the Builder is alive and before detach().

functions.name: SkVertices::Builder::detach
functions.description: Finalizes and detaches the built SkVertices object, returning a reference-counted pointer. After the first successful call, subsequent calls return null. The builder should not be used to write further data after detaching.
requirements: Builder must be valid (isValid() must return true) for a successful detach.
Must be called at most once; after the first call, this will always return null.
After detach(), previously obtained attribute/index pointers from the Builder must not be used.
Caller assumes ownership of the returned sk_sp<SkVertices> reference and should retain it as needed.

functions.name: SkVertices::uniqueID
functions.description: Returns an identifier unique to this SkVertices instance for its lifetime. Useful for caching or deduplication.

Return value is stable for the lifetime of the object.

functions.name: SkVertices::bounds
functions.description: Returns the precomputed bounding rectangle that encloses all vertex positions.

The returned reference remains valid as long as the SkVertices object remains alive; do not modify it.

functions.name: SkVertices::approximateSize
functions.description: Returns the approximate byte size of this SkVertices object, including its internal arrays. Intended for memory accounting and diagnostics.
requirements: May be called on any valid SkVertices instance.
Value is approximate; do not rely on it for exact allocation sizing.

functions.name: SkVertices::priv

functions.name: SkVertices::priv

functions.name: SkPoint3::Length

functions.description: Computes the Euclidean distance from the origin (0,0,0) to the point (x, y, z), i.e., sqrt(x*x + y*y + z*z). Implementation is declared here and defined elsewhere.

Return value is the Euclidean norm; behavior for infinities/NaN depends on SkScalar and implementation (not specified here).

functions.name: SkPoint3::length
functions.description: Returns the Euclidean length (norm) of this vector: SkPoint3::Length(fX, fY, fZ).

functions.name: SkPoint3::operator-

functions.name: SkContourMeasure::length
functions.description: Returns the total measured length of the current contour. Use to bound distance queries for sampling along the contour.

functions.signature: [[nodiscard]] bool SkContourMeasure::getPosTan(SkScalar distance, SkPoint* position, SkVector* tangent) const
functions.description: Computes the position and tangent on the contour corresponding to the given distance along the contour. The distance is pinned to the valid range [0, length()]. Returns true on success. Intended for sampling points/tangents along a path contour.
requirements: distance is pinned internally to 0 <= distance <= length().
Behavior when position or tangent is null is unknown (not documented).
Returns a boolean status; caller should check the return value before using outputs.
May return false if measurement is not possible (details not explicitly documented).

functions.name: SkContourMeasure::getMatrix
functions.signature: [[nodiscard]] bool SkContourMeasure::getMatrix(SkScalar distance, SkMatrix* matrix, SkContourMeasure::MatrixFlags flags = SkContourMeasure::kGetPosAndTan_MatrixFlag) const
functions.description: Computes a matrix at a distance along the contour by calling getPosTan, optionally encoding position and/or tangent depending on flags. The distance is pinned to [0, length()]. Returns false if there is no path or if a zero-length path was specified; in that case, matrix is unchanged.
requirements: distance is pinned internally to 0 <= distance <= length().
matrix must be a valid pointer; it is left unchanged on failure.
Caller must pass appropriate MatrixFlags: use kGetPosition_MatrixFlag to include position, kGetTangent_MatrixFlag to include tangent, or kGetPosAndTan_MatrixFlag for both.

functions.name: SkContourMeasure::getSegment
functions.signature: [[nodiscard]] bool SkContourMeasure::getSegment(SkScalar startD, SkScalar stopD, SkPathBuilder* dst, bool startWithMoveTo) const
functions.description: Extracts the path segment(s) between startD and stopD along the contour and appends them to dst. Distances are pinned to [0, length()]. Returns false if the segment is zero-length or if startD > stopD (dst is then left untouched). When startWithMoveTo is true, the segment begins with a moveTo.
requirements: startD and stopD are pinned internally to 0 <= distance <= length().
If startD > stopD, the function returns false and leaves dst untouched.
If the resulting segment is zero-length, the function returns false.
dst must be a valid pointer to a SkPathBuilder that can receive appended segments.
startWithMoveTo controls whether the extracted segment starts with a moveTo command.

functions.name: SkContourMeasure::isClosed
functions.description: Returns true if the measured contour is closed.

functions.description: Dereferences the iterator to obtain measurement data for the current path verb in the contour, including cumulative distance, verb type, and the verb's defining points.

functions.name: SkContourMeasure::ForwardVerbIterator::operator++
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next verb in forward order over the contour’s segments.

functions.name: SkContourMeasure::ForwardVerbIterator::operator==
functions.description: Compares two iterators for equality, which conceptually means they refer to the same position in the iteration sequence.

requirements: Both iterators should be comparable within the same iteration range (implied by typical iterator semantics; not explicitly documented).

functions.description: Returns an iterator positioned at the first verb of the current contour, for range-based for iteration over verb measurements.

functions.name: SkContourMeasure::end
functions.description: Returns a sentinel iterator representing the end of the contour’s verb sequence, for use with begin() in range-based iteration.

functions.name: SkContourMeasureIter::SkContourMeasureIter
functions.description: Default-constructs a contour-measure iterator with no attached path. Call reset() or use the path constructor before calling next().

functions.signature: SkContourMeasureIter::SkContourMeasureIter(const SkPath& path, bool forceClosed, SkScalar resScale = 1)
functions.description: Constructs an iterator to traverse the non-zero-length contours of the given path. The necessary parts of the path are internally copied, so the caller may modify or delete the original path after construction. resScale controls the precision of measurement; values greater than 1 increase precision (potentially at a performance cost).
requirements: path must be a valid SkPath reference at the time of the call (internally copied thereafter).
forceClosed determines whether contours should be treated as closed for measurement.
resScale controls precision; values > 1 increase precision (no strict range enforced in the declaration).

functions.name: SkContourMeasureIter::~SkContourMeasureIter
functions.description: Destroys the contour-measure iterator and releases associated resources.

functions.name: SkContourMeasureIter::operator=
functions.description: Move-assigns from another SkContourMeasureIter, transferring iteration state and resources.
requirements: The source iterator becomes moved-from; do not rely on its previous state after the assignment.

functions.name: SkContourMeasureIter::reset
functions.signature: void SkContourMeasureIter::reset(const SkPath& path, bool forceClosed, SkScalar resScale = 1)
functions.description: Resets the iterator with a new path. Required parts of the path are copied internally, allowing the caller to freely modify or delete the original path after the call. resScale controls measurement precision; values greater than 1 increase precision (with potential performance impact).
requirements: path must be a valid SkPath reference at the time of the call (internally copied thereafter).
forceClosed determines whether contours should be treated as closed for measurement.
Caller should choose resScale according to desired precision (no strict range enforced in the declaration).

functions.name: SkContourMeasureIter::next
functions.description: Returns a contour-measure object for the next non-zero-length contour in the path, or null when iteration is complete. Contours are delimited by kMove_Verb to the next kMove_Verb, one or more kClose_Verb, or kDone_Verb. Zero-length contours are skipped.
requirements: Caller must check for a null return to detect the end of iteration before using the returned object.
Only non-zero-length contours are returned; zero-length contours are skipped automatically.

functions.name: SkPathIter::SkPathIter
functions.signature: SkPathIter::SkPathIter(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs, SkSpan<const float> cns)
functions.description: Constructs an iterator over a path described by sequences of points, verbs, and conic weights. The iterator trims a trailing kMove verb for backward compatibility. Use this to iterate segments with next() or inspect the upcoming verb with peekNextVerb().
requirements: pts, vbs, and cns are non-owning views (SkSpan); the underlying memory must remain valid for the lifetime of the SkPathIter instance.

The spans must represent a consistent path encoding: vbs contains the sequence of SkPathVerb values; pts provides the points consumed by those verbs in order; cns contains the conic weights for kConic verbs in order.
If vbs ends with SkPathVerb::kMove, it will be ignored (trimmed) by the constructor.

functions.name: SkPathIter::next
functions.description: Advances the iterator and returns the next path element as a Rec containing the verb, its associated points, and a conic weight if applicable. Returns std::nullopt when no more elements are available. Element point counts: move: pts[0]; line: pts[0..1]; quad: pts[0..2]; conic: pts[0..2] with fConicWeight; cubic: pts[0..3]; close: pts[0..1] as if a line from pts[0] to pts[1].
requirements: Call repeatedly until it returns std::nullopt to consume all elements.
For records with fVerb == SkPathVerb::kConic, fConicWeight is valid; for all other verbs, ignore fConicWeight.
For records with fVerb == SkPathVerb::kClose, the points are provided as if the close were a line segment from the current point to the contour’s start point.

functions.name: SkPathIter::peekNextVerb
functions.description: Returns the next verb without advancing the iterator, or std::nullopt if there are no more verbs. Useful for lookahead when processing path elements.
requirements: Do not rely on this modifying iterator state; it is const and does not advance.
If std::nullopt is returned, the iterator is exhausted and next() will also return std::nullopt.

functions.name: SkPathContourIter::SkPathContourIter
functions.signature: SkPathContourIter::SkPathContourIter(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs, SkSpan<const float> cns)
functions.description: Constructs an iterator that yields entire contours of a path as slices (spans) of points, verbs, and conic weights. Use next() to retrieve successive contours.
requirements: pts, vbs, and cns are non-owning views (SkSpan); the underlying memory must remain valid for the lifetime of the SkPathContourIter instance.

The spans must represent a consistent path encoding across contours: vbs contains verb sequence for the whole path; pts provides corresponding points in order; cns contains conic weights for kConic verbs in order.

functions.name: SkPathContourIter::next
functions.description: Advances to the next contour and returns a Rec containing spans that slice the original arrays for that contour (points, verbs, and conic weights). Returns std::nullopt when no more contours are available.
requirements: Call repeatedly until std::nullopt is returned to iterate all contours.
The returned Rec contains spans referencing the original input memory; do not free or modify that memory while using the spans.

functions.name: SkRegion::SkRegion
functions.description: Constructs a rectangular region matching rect. If rect is empty, the region is empty.
requirements: rect must be a valid SkIRect; if rect is empty the resulting region is empty.

functions.name: SkRegion::~SkRegion
functions.description: Destructor. Releases ownership of any shared data and frees resources if this is the sole owner.

functions.name: SkRegion::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment. Makes this region identical by value to region, using shared storage until modified (copy-on-write).
requirements: region must be a valid SkRegion object (initialized).

functions.name: SkRegion::operator==
functions.description: Equality comparison. Returns true if both regions enclose exactly the same area.
requirements: other must be a valid SkRegion object (initialized).

functions.name: SkRegion::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality comparison. Returns true if regions do not enclose the same area.
requirements: other must be a valid SkRegion object (initialized).

functions.name: SkRegion::set
functions.description: Sets this region to src (copy-by-value with shared storage). Returns true if the resulting region is non-empty.
requirements: src must be a valid SkRegion object (initialized).

functions.name: SkRegion::swap
functions.description: Swaps the internal data of this and other. Lightweight pointer swap; does not allocate.
requirements: other must be a valid SkRegion object (initialized).

functions.name: SkRegion::isEmpty
functions.description: Returns true if the region is empty (has no width or height).

functions.name: SkRegion::isRect
functions.description: Returns true if the region is exactly one rectangle with positive dimensions.

functions.name: SkRegion::isComplex
functions.description: Returns true if the region is non-empty and described by more than one rectangle.

functions.name: SkRegion::getBounds
functions.description: Returns the minimal bounding rectangle of the region, or (0,0,0,0) if empty.
requirements: Returned reference is valid as long as the SkRegion object remains alive and unmodified.

functions.name: SkRegion::computeRegionComplexity
functions.description: Returns a value corresponding to the number of elements in the region: 0 for empty, 1 for a single rect, >1 for complex regions. Useful for relative complexity comparisons.

functions.name: SkRegion::addBoundaryPath
functions.description: Appends the boundary of the region to a path builder. Returns true if the region is not empty; otherwise returns false and leaves the builder unmodified.
requirements: The SkPathBuilder* argument must be non-null.
The builder must be in a valid state to accept appended geometry.

functions.name: SkRegion::getBoundaryPath
functions.description: Returns the region boundary as a path. If the region is empty, returns an empty path.

functions.name: SkRegion::setEmpty
functions.description: Sets the region to empty. Always returns false (the region is empty).

functions.name: SkRegion::setRect
functions.description: Sets the region to the rectangular bounds of rect. Returns true if rect is not empty; otherwise sets the region empty and returns false.
requirements: rect must be a valid SkIRect.

functions.name: SkRegion::setRects
functions.signature: bool SkRegion::setRects(const SkIRect rects[], int count)
functions.description: Sets the region as the union of the input rectangles. If count is zero the region is set empty. Returns true if the constructed region is non-empty.
requirements: If count > 0, rects must point to an array of at least count SkIRect entries.
count must be non-negative.

functions.name: SkRegion::setRegion
functions.description: Sets this region to a copy of region (copy-by-value with shared storage). Returns true if the resulting region is non-empty.
requirements: region must be a valid SkRegion object (initialized).

functions.name: SkRegion::setPath
functions.signature: bool SkRegion::setPath(const SkPath& path, const SkRegion& clip)
functions.description: Sets this region to the filled coverage of path clipped by clip, matching disabled antialias rendering. Returns true if the resulting region is non-empty.
requirements: path must be a valid SkPath.
clip must be a valid SkRegion (typically non-empty to produce output).

functions.name: SkRegion::intersects
functions.description: Returns true if this region intersects rect; false if either is empty or they do not intersect.
requirements: rect must be a valid SkIRect.

functions.name: SkRegion::intersects
functions.description: Returns true if this region intersects other; false if either is empty or they do not intersect.
requirements: other must be a valid SkRegion (initialized).

functions.name: SkRegion::contains
functions.signature: bool SkRegion::contains(int32_t x, int32_t y) const
functions.description: Returns true if the point (x, y) lies inside the region; false if the region is empty or does not contain the point.

functions.name: SkRegion::contains
functions.description: Returns true if other is completely inside this region; false if either is empty or containment fails.
requirements: other must be a valid SkIRect.

functions.name: SkRegion::contains
functions.description: Returns true if other is completely inside this region; false if either is empty or full containment does not hold.
requirements: other must be a valid SkRegion (initialized).

functions.name: SkRegion::quickContains
functions.description: Fast containment check that returns true only if this region is a single rectangle and that rectangle contains r. May return false even if the region actually contains r.
requirements: r must describe a non-empty rectangle (r.fLeft < r.fRight and r.fTop < r.fBottom) for a possible true result.

functions.name: SkRegion::quickReject
functions.description: Fast rejection test. Returns true if this region and rect are guaranteed not to intersect. May return false in some non-intersecting cases.
requirements: rect must be a valid SkIRect.

functions.name: SkRegion::quickReject
functions.description: Fast rejection test. Returns true if this region and rgn are guaranteed not to intersect. May return false in some non-intersecting cases.
requirements: rgn must be a valid SkRegion (initialized).

functions.name: SkRegion::translate
functions.description: Translates this region in-place by (dx, dy). No effect if the region is empty.

functions.name: SkRegion::translate
functions.signature: void SkRegion::translate(int dx, int dy, SkRegion* dst) const
functions.description: Translates this region by (dx, dy) and writes the result into dst. If dst is this, translates in place. If dst is nullptr, no result is written. If this region is empty, dst is set to empty.
requirements: dst may be nullptr; if non-null it must point to a valid SkRegion.

functions.name: SkRegion::op
functions.signature: bool SkRegion::op(const SkIRect& rect, Op op)
functions.description: Replaces this region with the result of applying the boolean operation op between this region and rect. Returns true if the result is non-empty. Optimized path for intersect when this is a rect.
requirements: rect must be a valid SkIRect.
op must be a valid SkRegion::Op value.

functions.name: SkRegion::op
functions.signature: bool SkRegion::op(const SkRegion& rgn, Op op)
functions.description: Replaces this region with the result of applying op between this region and rgn. Returns true if the result is non-empty.
requirements: rgn must be a valid SkRegion (initialized).
op must be a valid SkRegion::Op value.

functions.name: SkRegion::op
functions.signature: bool SkRegion::op(const SkIRect& rect, const SkRegion& rgn, Op op)
functions.description: Replaces this region with rect op rgn. Returns true if the result is non-empty.
requirements: rect must be a valid SkIRect.
rgn must be a valid SkRegion (initialized).
op must be a valid SkRegion::Op value.

functions.name: SkRegion::op
functions.signature: bool SkRegion::op(const SkRegion& rgn, const SkIRect& rect, Op op)
functions.description: Replaces this region with rgn op rect. Returns true if the result is non-empty.
requirements: rgn must be a valid SkRegion (initialized).
rect must be a valid SkIRect.
op must be a valid SkRegion::Op value.

functions.name: SkRegion::op
functions.signature: bool SkRegion::op(const SkRegion& rgna, const SkRegion& rgnb, Op op)
functions.description: Replaces this region with rgna op rgnb. Returns true if the result is non-empty.
requirements: rgna and rgnb must be valid SkRegion objects (initialized).
op must be a valid SkRegion::Op value.

functions.name: SkRegion::op
functions.signature: bool SkRegion::op(const SkIRect& rect, SkRegion::Op op)
functions.description: Replaces this region with the result of applying the specified boolean operation between the current region and the given rectangle. Returns true if the resulting region is non-empty, false otherwise. Typical use is to combine or clip the region against a rectangle using operations such as intersect, union, xor, etc. Note: when this is a simple rectangle and the op is kIntersect_Op, an optimized path updates the bounds in place.
requirements: This function mutates the receiver (the left-hand side region).
op must be a valid SkRegion::Op value (kDifference_Op, kIntersect_Op, kUnion_Op, kXOR_Op, kReverseDifference_Op, or kReplace_Op).
rect may be empty; if the operation yields an empty region, the function returns false.
The receiver must be a valid SkRegion instance (not destroyed).

functions.name: SkRegion::Iterator::Iterator
functions.description: Default iterator constructor. Initializes an iterator in the done state. Call reset() later to attach a region.

functions.name: SkRegion::Iterator::Iterator
functions.description: Constructs an iterator over the rectangles in region, sorted by y then x.
requirements: region must remain alive and unmodified while the iterator is used.

functions.name: SkRegion::Iterator::rewind
functions.description: Resets iteration to the start of the current region. Returns true if a region was set.
requirements: The iterator must have been constructed with a region or reset(region) previously for a true result.
