functions.name: SkRegion::Iterator::reset
functions.description: Sets or resets the iterator to iterate over region from the beginning.
requirements: region must remain alive and unmodified while the iterator is used.

functions.name: SkRegion::Iterator::done
functions.description: Returns true if the iterator has reached the end (no more rectangles).

functions.name: SkRegion::Iterator::next
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next rectangle if not done.
requirements: Call done() to ensure there is a current rectangle before calling next() to avoid overrunning.

functions.name: SkRegion::Iterator::rect
functions.description: Returns the current rectangle in the iteration. Results are undefined if the region is empty or the iterator is done.
requirements: Call done() and ensure it returns false before accessing rect().

functions.name: SkRegion::Iterator::rgn
functions.description: Returns the region being iterated, or nullptr if none.

functions.name: SkRegion::Cliperator::Cliperator
functions.signature: SkRegion::Cliperator::Cliperator(const SkRegion& region, const SkIRect& clip)
functions.description: Constructs an iterator over the intersection of region with clip, yielding rectangles sorted by y then x.
requirements: region must remain alive and unmodified while the cliperator is used.
clip must be a valid SkIRect.

functions.name: SkRegion::Cliperator::done
functions.description: Returns true if there are no more rectangles in the clipped iteration.

functions.name: SkRegion::Cliperator::next
functions.description: Advances to the next clipped rectangle, if any.
requirements: Call done() to ensure there is a current rectangle before advancing to avoid overrunning.

functions.name: SkRegion::Cliperator::rect
functions.description: Returns the current rectangle intersected with the clip. Results are undefined if the iterator is done or the region is empty.
requirements: Call done() and ensure it returns false before accessing rect().

functions.name: SkRegion::Spanerator::Spanerator
functions.signature: SkRegion::Spanerator::Spanerator(const SkRegion& region, int y, int left, int right)
functions.description: Constructs a span iterator that enumerates x-intervals where the region covers the horizontal scanline y within [left, right).
requirements: region must remain alive and unmodified while the spanerator is used.
left and right define the horizontal bounds to consider.

functions.name: SkRegion::Spanerator::next
functions.description: Finds the next span intersecting the region on the configured scanline. Writes the span endpoints to left and right if non-null. Returns true if a span was found.
requirements: left and right pointers may be nullptr; if non-null they must point to writable ints.

functions.name: SkRegion::writeToMemory
functions.description: Serializes the region to buffer and returns the number of bytes written. If buffer is nullptr, returns the number of bytes that would be written.
requirements: If buffer is non-null, it must point to a writable block of at least the returned size bytes.

functions.name: SkRegion::readFromMemory
functions.signature: size_t SkRegion::readFromMemory(const void* buffer, size_t length)
functions.description: Deserializes this region from buffer of size length. Returns the number of bytes read, which will be a multiple of four or zero if length was too small.
requirements: buffer must point to at least length readable bytes.
length specifies the available size; only that many bytes will be inspected.

functions.name: SkGraphics::Init
functions.description: Initializes Skia’s global graphics infrastructure when environments disallow static initializers. It is thread-safe and idempotent; calling multiple times has no adverse effect. Typical usage is at process startup before using other Skia APIs that rely on global state.
requirements: May be called zero or more times; it is idempotent.
Safe to call from multiple threads.

functions.name: SkGraphics::GetFontCacheLimit
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of bytes permitted for the font cache before purging occurs. The value can be changed via SetFontCacheLimit().

functions.name: SkGraphics::SetFontCacheLimit
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of bytes that the font cache may use, returning the previous limit. If the cache exceeds the new limit, old entries may be purged.
requirements: bytes is a size in bytes (unsigned).
Callers should be prepared for the cache to purge entries immediately if the new limit is lower than current usage.

functions.name: SkGraphics::GetFontCacheUsed
functions.description: Returns the current number of bytes used by the font cache.

functions.name: SkGraphics::GetFontCacheCountUsed
functions.description: Returns the number of entries currently in the font cache. An entry corresponds to a unique combination of typeface, point size, and matrix.

functions.name: SkGraphics::GetFontCacheCountLimit
functions.description: Returns the current limit on the number of entries allowed in the font cache. An entry corresponds to a unique combination of typeface, point size, and matrix.

functions.name: SkGraphics::SetFontCacheCountLimit
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of entries allowed in the font cache and returns the previous limit. If the new limit is lower, the cache will attempt to purge to meet it.
requirements: count specifies the maximum number of cache entries.
Callers should be prepared for immediate purging if the new limit is lower than the current number of entries.

functions.name: SkGraphics::GetTypefaceCacheCountLimit
functions.description: Returns the current limit on the number of entries in the typeface cache. An entry is associated with each typeface.

functions.name: SkGraphics::SetTypefaceCacheCountLimit
functions.description: Sets the limit on the number of entries in the typeface cache and returns the previous value. Changes take effect the next time the cache is modified.
requirements: count specifies the maximum number of typeface cache entries.
The new limit takes effect on subsequent cache modifications, not retroactively.

functions.name: SkGraphics::PurgeFontCache
functions.description: Attempts to purge the font cache for debugging or memory pressure. Does not change limits; subsequent font operations will recreate needed data.

functions.name: SkGraphics::PurgePinnedFontCache
functions.description: If the strike cache exceeds its limit, attempts to purge strikes that have pinners after clients release locks. Intended to be called after releasing locks on pinned strikes.
requirements: Should be called after clients release locks on pinned strikes.

functions.name: SkGraphics::GetResourceCacheTotalBytesUsed
functions.description: Returns the total memory currently used by the resource cache (temporary images and other resources).

functions.name: SkGraphics::GetResourceCacheTotalByteLimit
functions.description: Returns the current memory usage limit (in bytes) for the resource cache. Entries are purged when usage exceeds this limit.

functions.name: SkGraphics::SetResourceCacheTotalByteLimit
functions.description: Sets the memory usage limit (in bytes) for the resource cache and returns the previous limit. Exceeding the limit triggers purging of entries.
requirements: newLimit is a size in bytes (unsigned).
Callers should expect purging if the new limit is below current usage.

functions.name: SkGraphics::PurgeResourceCache
functions.description: Attempts to purge the resource cache for debugging or to reduce memory. Does not change the configured limits.

functions.name: SkGraphics::GetResourceCacheSingleAllocationByteLimit
functions.description: Returns the per-entry size limit (in bytes) for cacheable resource allocations. Entries exceeding this size will not be cached. Default is zero (no per-entry limit).

functions.name: SkGraphics::SetResourceCacheSingleAllocationByteLimit
functions.description: Sets the per-entry size limit (in bytes) for cacheable resource allocations and returns the previous limit. If a would-be cache entry exceeds this size, it will not be cached.
requirements: newLimit is a size in bytes (unsigned).

functions.name: SkGraphics::DumpMemoryStatistics
functions.description: Dumps memory usage information for caches via the SkTraceMemoryDump interface. Useful for diagnostics and profiling.
requirements: dump should point to a valid SkTraceMemoryDump implementation (inferred from usage).

functions.name: SkGraphics::PurgeAllCaches
functions.description: Purges all private global caches in Skia, including font and image caches, to free as much memory as possible. GPU context–associated caches are not affected.
requirements: Does not affect caches associated with a GPU context.

functions.name: SkGraphics::SetImageGeneratorFromEncodedDataFactory
functions.description: Sets the global factory used to create SkImageGenerator instances from encoded SkData. Skia uses this factory first; if unset or if it returns null, Skia falls back to its internal implementation. Returns the previously set factory (which may be null).
requirements: The factory may be null to clear and use Skia’s internal default.
If provided, the factory must have signature: std::unique_ptr<SkImageGenerator> (*)(sk_sp<const SkData>).

functions.name: SkGraphics::SetOpenTypeSVGDecoderFactory
functions.description: Sets the global factory used by SkTypeface implementations to decode and render OpenType SVG glyph data. If not set, OpenType SVG glyphs will generally not be supported and other glyph representations may be used. Returns the previously set factory.
requirements: The factory may be null to disable OpenType SVG decoding support.
If provided, the factory must have signature: std::unique_ptr<SkOpenTypeSVGDecoder> (*)(const uint8_t* svg, size_t length).

functions.name: SkGraphics::GetOpenTypeSVGDecoderFactory
functions.description: Returns the currently configured global OpenType SVG decoder factory (or null if none is set).

functions.name: SkParse::Count
functions.description: Counts the number of scalar or integer values present in the given C string. Intended for quickly determining how many numeric tokens are present before parsing. Specific token formats and delimiters are not documented here and are therefore unknown.
requirements: str must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
Return value is the count of detectable numeric tokens; the exact definition of a token (allowed formats, delimiters, whitespace rules) is unknown based on this header.

functions.name: SkParse::Count
functions.signature: static int SkParse::Count(const char str[], char separator)
functions.description: Counts the number of tokens in the given C string using the specified separator character, typically representing the number of scalar or integer values separated by that character.
requirements: str must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
separator specifies the delimiter character used to split the string into tokens.
Return value is the number of tokens detected; details on trimming, empty tokens, and numeric validation are unknown based on this header.

functions.name: SkParse::FindColor
functions.signature: static const char* SkParse::FindColor(const char str[], SkColor* value)
functions.description: Parses a color specification from the start (or current position) of the input string and writes the result to value. Returns a pointer that likely indicates the position after the parsed color on success. Exact accepted formats (e.g., #RRGGBB, named colors) and failure behavior are not documented here and thus unknown; the return convention is inferred from the function name and signature.
requirements: str must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
value must be a non-null pointer to writable SkColor storage.
On failure behavior (e.g., nullptr return, leaving value unmodified) is unknown; callers should be prepared for a null return and avoid using value unless success is indicated by the return pointer.

functions.name: SkParse::FindHex
functions.signature: static const char* SkParse::FindHex(const char str[], uint32_t* value)
functions.description: Parses a hexadecimal number from the input string into value. Returns a pointer that likely advances past the parsed hex digits on success; exact syntax (e.g., allowance of 0x prefix, uppercase/lowercase, minimum/maximum digits) and failure signaling are not documented and therefore unknown. The return convention is inferred from the name/signature.
requirements: str must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
value must be a non-null pointer to writable uint32_t storage.
On parse failure, the exact return (e.g., nullptr) and whether value is modified are unknown; callers should assume value is valid only if a non-null, advanced pointer is returned.

functions.name: SkParse::FindNamedColor
functions.signature: static const char* SkParse::FindNamedColor(const char str[], size_t len, SkColor* color)
functions.description: Looks up a color by name in the provided substring [str, str+len) and writes the corresponding SkColor to color. Returns a pointer that likely indicates the position after the matched name or the next parse position. The set of recognized names and exact return/failure behavior are not documented here and are therefore unknown; the return convention is inferred from the name/signature.
requirements: str must point to a memory region containing at least len bytes; it need not be null-terminated.
len specifies the length of the name to consider; it must not exceed the actual accessible length of str.
color must be a non-null pointer to writable SkColor storage.
On failure (e.g., name not recognized), the exact return (e.g., nullptr) and whether color is modified are unknown; callers should use color only if success is indicated by the return pointer.

functions.name: SkParse::FindS32
functions.signature: static const char* SkParse::FindS32(const char str[], int32_t* value)
functions.description: Parses a signed 32-bit integer from the input string and writes it to value. Returns a pointer that likely advances past the parsed integer on success; exact accepted formats (signs, bases, whitespace) and failure signaling are not documented and thus unknown. The return convention is inferred from the name/signature.
requirements: str must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
value must be a non-null pointer to writable int32_t storage.
On parse failure, the exact return (e.g., nullptr) and whether value is modified are unknown; callers should treat value as valid only if a non-null, advanced pointer is returned.

functions.name: SkParse::FindScalar
functions.signature: static const char* SkParse::FindScalar(const char str[], SkScalar* value)
functions.description: Parses a scalar (SkScalar) value from the input string and writes it to value. Returns a pointer that likely advances past the parsed scalar on success; accepted numeric formats (decimal, scientific notation) and failure behavior are not documented and therefore unknown. The return convention is inferred from the name/signature.
requirements: str must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
value must be a non-null pointer to writable SkScalar storage.
On parse failure, the exact return (e.g., nullptr) and whether value is modified are unknown; callers should only use value if a non-null, advanced pointer is returned.

functions.name: SkParse::FindScalars
functions.signature: static const char* SkParse::FindScalars(const char str[], SkScalar value[], int count)
functions.description: Parses up to count scalar (SkScalar) values from the input string into the provided array. Returns a pointer that likely advances to the position after the last parsed scalar on success; accepted formats, delimiters, and partial-parse behavior are not documented and thus unknown. The return convention is inferred from the name/signature.
requirements: str must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
value must be a non-null pointer to an array with capacity for at least count elements.
count must be non-negative.

On parse failure or insufficient tokens, the exact return (e.g., nullptr) and how many elements of value are written are unknown; callers should only consume parsed values if success is indicated by the return pointer.

functions.name: SkParse::FindBool
functions.signature: static bool SkParse::FindBool(const char str[], bool* value)
functions.description: Attempts to parse a boolean value from the input string and write it to value. Returns true on success and false on failure. Exact accepted forms (e.g., "true/false", "1/0", case sensitivity) and whitespace handling are not documented and therefore unknown.
requirements: str must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
value must be a non-null pointer to writable bool storage.
On failure (function returns false), value should be considered undefined; callers must check the return value before using *value.

functions.name: SkParse::FindList
functions.signature: static int SkParse::FindList(const char str[], const char list[])
functions.description: Searches for str within list and returns the index of str in list, or -1 if not found. The structure and delimiter format of list are not documented here and therefore unknown.
requirements: str must point to a valid, null-terminated C string representing the target to find.
list must point to a valid, null-terminated C string containing a list of items in an unspecified format/delimiter.
Function returns -1 if not found, as documented in the header comment.

functions.name: SkParsePath::FromSVGString
functions.description: Parses an SVG path-data string and returns a SkPath if parsing succeeds. Use this to convert standard SVG path commands (e.g., M, L, C, Z) from a null-terminated C string into an SkPath. Returns an engaged std::optional on success or an empty optional on failure.
requirements: str must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated C string.
str should contain valid SVG path data per the SVG specification; otherwise parsing may fail and an empty optional is returned.
Callers must check whether the returned std::optional is engaged before using the SkPath.

functions.name: SkParsePath::FromSVGString
functions.signature: static bool SkParsePath::FromSVGString(const char str[], SkPath* outPath)
functions.description: Deprecated overload. Parses an SVG path-data string into an SkPath written to outPath. Returns true on success and false on failure. Prefer the std::optional-returning overload.
requirements: str must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated C string.
outPath must be a non-null pointer to a writable SkPath instance.
str should contain valid SVG path data per the SVG specification; otherwise the function returns false.
Callers must check the boolean return value and only use the contents of outPath when the function returns true.

functions.name: SkParsePath::ToSVGString
functions.signature: static SkString SkParsePath::ToSVGString(const SkPath& path, PathEncoding encoding = PathEncoding::Absolute)
functions.description: Serializes an SkPath to an SVG path-data string. Use this to export a path in either absolute or relative coordinate form for inclusion in SVG content.
requirements: path must be a valid, initialized SkPath.
encoding must be either PathEncoding::Absolute or PathEncoding::Relative; if omitted, PathEncoding::Absolute is used by default.

functions.name: SkShadowUtils::DrawShadow
functions.signature: static void SkShadowUtils::DrawShadow(SkCanvas* canvas, const SkPath& path, const SkPoint3& zPlaneParams, const SkPoint3& lightPos, SkScalar lightRadius, SkColor ambientColor, SkColor spotColor, uint32_t flags = SkShadowFlags::kNone_ShadowFlag)
functions.description: Draws an offset spot shadow and an outlining ambient shadow for the given occluding path using a disc light. May cache the computed shadow geometry depending on the path type and the canvas matrix (no caching for perspective matrices or volatile paths). Use flags to control occluder transparency, use of analytic geometry, directional light behavior, and concave-path handling.
requirements: canvas must be a valid, non-null pointer to a SkCanvas that is in a state ready for drawing
path must be a valid, initialized SkPath representing the occluder in local coordinates
zPlaneParams defines the plane function giving Z offset as a function of local x and y; must be a valid, initialized SkPoint3
If kDirectionalLight_ShadowFlag is set in flags, lightPos is interpreted as a direction vector toward the light; otherwise it is the 3D light position relative to the canvas plane
If kDirectionalLight_ShadowFlag is set, lightRadius specifies the blur amount at Z == 1; otherwise it is the disc light radius
ambientColor and spotColor must be valid SkColor values
flags should be a bitwise OR combination of SkShadowFlags values

functions.name: SkShadowUtils::GetLocalBounds
functions.signature: static bool SkShadowUtils::GetLocalBounds(const SkMatrix& ctm, const SkPath& path, const SkPoint3& zPlaneParams, const SkPoint3& lightPos, SkScalar lightRadius, uint32_t flags, SkRect* bounds)
functions.description: Computes the bounding box of the ambient and spot shadows cast by the given path, relative to the path’s local space, taking into account the provided current transformation matrix (to device), lighting, and flags. Returns true on success and writes the combined shadow bounds to bounds.
requirements: ctm must be a valid, initialized SkMatrix representing the current transformation to device space
path must be a valid, initialized SkPath representing the occluder in local coordinates
zPlaneParams defines the plane function giving Z offset as a function of local x and y; must be a valid, initialized SkPoint3
If kDirectionalLight_ShadowFlag is set in flags, lightPos is interpreted as a direction vector toward the light; otherwise it is the 3D light position relative to the canvas plane
If kDirectionalLight_ShadowFlag is set, lightRadius specifies the blur amount at Z == 1; otherwise it is the disc light radius
flags should be a bitwise OR combination of SkShadowFlags values
bounds must be a valid, non-null pointer to a SkRect where the resulting bounds will be stored
Caller must check the boolean return value; on false, bounds contents are unspecified

functions.name: SkShadowUtils::ComputeTonalColors
functions.signature: static void SkShadowUtils::ComputeTonalColors(SkColor inAmbientColor, SkColor inSpotColor, SkColor* outAmbientColor, SkColor* outSpotColor)
functions.description: Computes adjusted ambient and spot colors suitable for one-pass tonal alpha shadow rendering from the provided input ambient and spot colors. Writes the modified colors to the provided output pointers.
requirements: inAmbientColor and inSpotColor must be valid SkColor values
outAmbientColor must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the modified ambient color
outSpotColor must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the modified spot color

functions.name: SkTextUtils::Draw
functions.signature: static void SkTextUtils::Draw(SkCanvas* canvas, const void* text, size_t size, SkTextEncoding encoding, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, const SkFont& font, const SkPaint& paint, Align align = kLeft_Align)
functions.description: Renders a run of text onto the given SkCanvas at the position (x, y) using the specified font, paint, and text encoding. The text is provided as an arbitrary byte buffer (text, size) interpreted according to encoding (e.g., UTF-8/16/32 or glyph IDs). Alignment controls horizontal alignment relative to (x, y). Typical usage is to pass a valid canvas, prepared font and paint, the text buffer with its length in bytes, and choose the desired alignment.
requirements: canvas must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SkCanvas ready for drawing.
text points to a buffer of at least size bytes; may be empty if size == 0.
size is the length in bytes of the text buffer; must not exceed the allocated buffer size.
encoding must be a valid SkTextEncoding corresponding to how the buffer is encoded (e.g., kUTF8, kUTF16, kUTF32, or kGlyphID).
x and y are SkScalar coordinates specifying the text baseline reference point.
font must reference a valid SkFont configured for the desired typeface/size/metrics.
paint must reference a valid SkPaint configured for fill/stroke/color as desired.
align must be one of SkTextUtils::Align values; it affects horizontal positioning relative to x (left/center/right).

functions.name: SkTextUtils::DrawString
functions.signature: static void SkTextUtils::DrawString(SkCanvas* canvas, const char text[], SkScalar x, SkScalar y, const SkFont& font, const SkPaint& paint, Align align = kLeft_Align)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to draw a null-terminated UTF-8 C string at position (x, y) with the given font, paint, and alignment. Internally calls SkTextUtils::Draw with SkTextEncoding::kUTF8 and the byte length computed via strlen(text). Use when your text is a standard C string.
requirements: canvas must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SkCanvas ready for drawing.
text must be a valid, non-null, null-terminated C string encoded in UTF-8.
Because strlen(text) is used, only bytes prior to the first NUL (\0) are drawn; embedded NULs terminate the string.
x and y are SkScalar coordinates specifying the text baseline reference point.
font must reference a valid SkFont configured for the desired typeface/size/metrics.
paint must reference a valid SkPaint configured for fill/stroke/color as desired.
align must be one of SkTextUtils::Align values; it affects horizontal positioning relative to x (left/center/right).

functions.name: SkTextUtils::GetPath
functions.signature: static void SkTextUtils::GetPath(const void* text, size_t length, SkTextEncoding encoding, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, const SkFont& font, SkPath* path)
functions.description: Converts text to vector outlines and appends them to the provided SkPath, positioned relative to (x, y), using the specified font and text encoding. This is used to obtain the geometry of the text (glyph outlines) without drawing to a canvas, suitable for stroking, filling, or further geometric processing.
requirements: text points to a buffer of at least length bytes; may be empty if length == 0.
length is the size in bytes of the text buffer; must not exceed the allocated buffer size.
encoding must be a valid SkTextEncoding corresponding to the buffer (e.g., kUTF8, kUTF16, kUTF32, or kGlyphID).
x and y are SkScalar coordinates specifying the text baseline reference point for the path placement.
font must reference a valid SkFont capable of providing glyph outlines for the requested text.
path must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SkPath; its contents may be appended to or overwritten depending on implementation (callers should assume contents may be modified).

functions.name: SkNoDrawCanvas::SkNoDrawCanvas
functions.description: Constructs a SkNoDrawCanvas with the specified width and height. This canvas is intended for analysis or recording of draw calls without actual rasterization; all draw operations are effectively no-ops. Clipping is handled conservatively using rectangular bounds. Use this when you need a SkCanvas-compatible object that won’t allocate a device or pixels.
requirements: The width and height are integers provided by the caller; the header does not specify valid ranges.
No error reporting mechanism is provided by the constructor; behavior for invalid sizes is unspecified in this header.
Object must be constructed before use like any C++ object; thread-safety and concurrency guarantees are not specified.

functions.name: SkNoDrawCanvas::SkNoDrawCanvas
functions.description: Constructs a SkNoDrawCanvas with the given integer rectangle as its bounds. This is a no-draw canvas for analyzing or recording draw calls without rasterization. Clipping is conservative and constrained to rectangles. Use this overload when you want to specify both origin and size via an SkIRect.
requirements: The bounds parameter must be a valid SkIRect object supplied by the caller; the header does not specify additional constraints (e.g., ordering of edges).
No error reporting mechanism is provided by the constructor; behavior for invalid rectangles is unspecified in this header.
Object must be constructed before use; thread-safety and concurrency guarantees are not specified.

functions.name: SkNoDrawCanvas::resetCanvas
functions.description: Resets the canvas state to be the same as immediately after construction, and sets new bounds using the provided width and height. Intended as an optimization to reuse a SkNoDrawCanvas between drawings without reallocating backing resources. Internally delegates to resetForNextPicture(SkIRect::MakeWH(w, h)).
requirements: The canvas object must be a valid, constructed SkNoDrawCanvas instance.
w and h are integers provided by the caller; the header does not specify valid ranges or behavior for negative/zero values.
The function has no return value and does not report errors; callers should not expect status feedback.
Effects on any existing save/restore stack or pending state are not documented here; callers should assume the state becomes equivalent to post-construction.

functions.name: SkNoDrawCanvas::resetCanvas
functions.description: Resets the canvas state to be the same as immediately after construction, and sets new bounds using the provided rectangle. This is an optimization to reuse a SkNoDrawCanvas across drawings. Internally delegates to resetForNextPicture(rect).
requirements: The canvas object must be a valid, constructed SkNoDrawCanvas instance.
rect must be a valid SkIRect supplied by the caller; the header specifies no further constraints on its contents.
The function has no return value and does not report errors; callers should not expect status feedback.
Effects on any existing save/restore stack or pending state are not documented here; callers should assume the state becomes equivalent to post-construction.

functions.name: SkMakeNullCanvas
functions.description: Constructs and returns a Skia canvas that ignores all draw operations. Useful for performance testing or measuring command overhead without rasterization. Returns a std::unique_ptr<SkCanvas> that can be used anywhere a SkCanvas is expected, but it will produce no visual output.
requirements: No parameters are required.
Callers take ownership of the returned std::unique_ptr<SkCanvas>.
Do not expect any drawing commands issued to this canvas to produce visible output.

functions.name: SkNWayCanvas::SkNWayCanvas
functions.description: Constructs an N-way canvas that forwards drawing operations to zero or more attached SkCanvas instances, while itself deriving from SkNoDrawCanvas (it does not draw). Typically used to broadcast the same draw stream to multiple canvases. The initial width and height set the base canvas dimensions.
requirements: width and height represent canvas dimensions in pixels; values should be non-negative integers (inferred from common SkCanvas/SkNoDrawCanvas size semantics)
No canvases are attached by default; callers must add canvases via addCanvas() to forward draws (inferred)
Threading/ownership behavior is unspecified in this header; callers should avoid sharing the same SkNWayCanvas across threads without external synchronization (unknown beyond typical Skia usage)

functions.name: SkNWayCanvas::~SkNWayCanvas
functions.description: Destructor for SkNWayCanvas. Cleans up the forwarding canvas. It likely stops forwarding to any attached canvases; ownership and lifetime of attached SkCanvas objects are not documented here.
requirements: Do not destroy SkNWayCanvas while it may still be used by other threads or while callbacks/recording are in progress (general C++ object lifetime requirement)
Ownership of attached SkCanvas objects is unspecified; callers should not assume they are deleted by the destructor (unknown; not stated in header)

functions.name: SkNWayCanvas::addCanvas
functions.description: Registers an SkCanvas as a target for forwarded drawing operations. After adding, all subsequent drawing commands issued to this SkNWayCanvas are forwarded to the added canvas as well.
requirements: The SkCanvas* must refer to a valid, live SkCanvas instance for as long as it remains added (inferred from purpose)
Passing nullptr is not documented; callers should pass a non-null pointer (inferred from typical API patterns)
The same SkCanvas should only be added once unless the implementation explicitly supports duplicates (behavior not stated)
Thread-safety is not specified; addCanvas() should be called when no concurrent drawing is occurring on this SkNWayCanvas (inferred)
Ownership is unspecified; callers should retain ownership of the added SkCanvas and ensure its lifetime exceeds its registration (inferred)

functions.name: SkNWayCanvas::removeCanvas
functions.description: Unregisters a previously added SkCanvas so it no longer receives forwarded drawing commands.
requirements: The SkCanvas* should refer to a canvas that was previously added via addCanvas() (inferred)
Behavior when removing a canvas not in the set is unspecified; callers should avoid doing so (inferred)
Do not pass nullptr (not documented; inferred)
Call only when there is no concurrent drawing/forwarding occurring (thread-safety not specified; inferred)
Removal does not imply deletion of the SkCanvas; ownership remains with the caller (inferred)

functions.name: SkNWayCanvas::removeAll
functions.description: Unregisters all previously added canvases, stopping forwarding to any targets.
requirements: Call only when there is no concurrent drawing/forwarding occurring (thread-safety not specified; inferred)
This does not delete the canvases; ownership and lifetime of the previously added canvases remain with the caller (inferred)

functions.name: SkCodec::MinBufferedBytesNeeded
functions.description: Returns the minimum number of bytes a stream must allow peeking or reading to identify the image format before rewinding to the start. Used by MakeFromStream to determine format detection behavior.
requirements: None beyond calling it statically; it returns a compile-time constant (32).

functions.name: SkCodec::ResultToString
functions.description: Converts a SkCodec::Result error/status code to a human-readable C string. Useful for logging or diagnostics.
requirements: Argument must be a valid SkCodec::Result enumerator.

functions.name: SkCodec::MakeFromStream
functions.signature: static std::unique_ptr<SkCodec> SkCodec::MakeFromStream(std::unique_ptr<SkStream> stream, SkSpan<const SkCodecs::Decoder> decoders, SkCodec::Result* result = nullptr, SkPngChunkReader* chunkReader = nullptr, SkCodec::SelectionPolicy selectionPolicy = SkCodec::SelectionPolicy::kPreferStillImage)
functions.description: Creates a codec to decode an image from the given stream using the supplied runtime decoder list. Detects the format by peeking at or reading the first MinBufferedBytesNeeded bytes and rewinding as needed. On success returns a codec owning the stream; on failure returns null and deletes the stream. If a PNG is detected and a chunk reader is provided, it will be used for unknown chunks.
requirements: stream must be non-null and must either support peek() of at least SkCodec::MinBufferedBytesNeeded() bytes or support rewind() so that reads for format detection can be rewound.
If result is non-null, it will be set to kSuccess on success, or a specific failure code on error.

If chunkReader is non-null and the image is PNG: it will be reffed and may be invoked during codec creation or decode to process unknown chunks; failures in the chunk reader can cause codec creation or decode to fail.
If the image is not PNG, chunkReader is ignored.
On failure (returning null), the stream is deleted immediately; on success the SkCodec takes ownership of the stream and will delete it when done.
selectionPolicy controls preference between still image vs. animated sequence for container formats that contain both.

functions.name: SkCodec::MakeFromData
functions.signature: static std::unique_ptr<SkCodec> SkCodec::MakeFromData(sk_sp<const SkData> data, SkSpan<const SkCodecs::Decoder> decoders, SkPngChunkReader* chunkReader = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates a codec to decode an image from immutable in-memory encoded data using the supplied runtime decoder list. If the image is PNG and a chunk reader is provided, it will be used for unknown chunks.
requirements: data must be non-null and contain the complete or at least detectable encoded image.

If chunkReader is non-null and the image is PNG: it will be reffed and may be invoked during codec creation or decode to process unknown chunks; failures in the chunk reader can cause codec creation or decode to fail.
If the image is not PNG, chunkReader is ignored.

functions.name: SkCodec::~SkCodec
functions.description: Virtual destructor for SkCodec. Destroys the codec and releases any owned resources, including the input stream when owned by the codec.
requirements: Do not use the codec after destruction.

functions.name: SkCodec::getInfo
functions.description: Returns a reasonable SkImageInfo describing how to decode the image by default, including dimensions, color type, alpha type, and a color space derived from the encoded ICC profile (or sRGB if the profile does not map to an SkColorSpace).
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkCodec::dimensions
functions.description: Returns the encoded image dimensions as width and height.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkCodec::bounds
functions.description: Returns an SkIRect representing the full image bounds with origin at (0,0) and width/height of the encoded image.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkCodec::getICCProfile
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the ICC profile embedded in the encoded data, if present. May be used for color management decisions.
requirements: Caller must treat the returned pointer as owned by the codec; do not free it and do not use it after the codec is destroyed.

functions.name: SkCodec::getHdrMetadata
functions.description: Returns HDR metadata associated with this image. Even SDR images may provide HDR-related metadata for inverse tone mapping on HDR displays.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkCodec::hasHighBitDepthEncodedData
functions.description: Returns true if the encoded input uses 16 or more bits per component. This is a coarse indicator of high bit depth encodings.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkCodec::getOrigin
functions.description: Returns the image orientation from EXIF data. Returns kTopLeft if EXIF is absent or unreadable.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkCodec::getScaledDimensions
functions.description: Returns the closest natively supported dimensions approximating the desired scale factor. Scale <= 0 is invalid; scale >= 1 returns the original dimensions. For other scales, the codec suggests a supported size.
requirements: desiredScale must be greater than 0.
Upscaling is not supported; requesting >= 1.0 will return the original size.

functions.name: SkCodec::getValidSubset
functions.description: Validates and possibly adjusts a requested subset rectangle to one that the codec can decode. Returns true if the (possibly modified) subset is supported; false if subsets are unsupported or the request cannot be satisfied.
requirements: desiredSubset must be non-null.
Input desiredSubset should be within the full image bounds (as from getInfo()).
If false is returned, desiredSubset’s value is undefined and should not be used further.

functions.name: SkCodec::getEncodedFormat
functions.description: Returns the format of the encoded image data (e.g., PNG, JPEG, WEBP).
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkCodec::getEncodedData
functions.description: Returns a new stream for the underlying encoded data if available; may return nullptr if the original stream cannot be duplicated.
requirements: Caller assumes ownership of the returned stream.
Returned pointer may be null; caller must check before use.

functions.name: SkCodec::getPixels
functions.signature: SkCodec::Result SkCodec::getPixels(const SkImageInfo& info, void* pixels, size_t rowBytes, const SkCodec::Options* options)
functions.description: Decodes the image into the provided pixel buffer according to info and options. Supports scaling if info dimensions differ from the encoded size (subject to codec capabilities) and performs color space transforms if info has a color space. If a scanline decode is in progress, it will be terminated.
requirements: pixels must be non-null and point to a buffer of at least (info.height - 1) * rowBytes + info.width * bytesPerPixel bytes.
rowBytes must be large enough to contain one decoded row for the given info.
If info dimensions differ from the encoded size, scaling must be supported by the codec; otherwise kInvalidScale is returned.
If options is non-null and options->fSubset is set, it must be within getInfo() bounds; for WEBP subsets, subset left and top must be even.
If options->fZeroInitialized is kYes_ZeroInitialized, the implementation may skip writing zeroes; otherwise the codec must fully initialize memory.
May require the input stream to be rewindable.
For certain codecs (e.g., animated WEBP), decoding to smaller dimensions than the original may produce incorrect results.
On error or partial input, the function may return kIncompleteInput or other Result codes; caller should handle them.

functions.name: SkCodec::getImage
functions.signature: std::tuple<sk_sp<SkImage>, SkCodec::Result> SkCodec::getImage(const SkImageInfo& info, const SkCodec::Options* opts = nullptr)
functions.description: Decodes and returns an SkImage along with the decode Result. If the encoded origin is not top-left, the returned image is rotated accordingly to appear upright.
requirements: info describes the desired output; scaling rules and color space transform behavior are as in getPixels.
If opts is provided, its constraints apply as in getPixels.
Caller must inspect the returned Result to verify success.

functions.name: SkCodec::queryYUVAInfo
functions.signature: bool SkCodec::queryYUVAInfo(const SkYUVAPixmapInfo::SupportedDataTypes& supportedDataTypes, SkYUVAPixmapInfo* yuvaPixmapInfo) const
functions.description: Queries whether decoding to YUVA is supported given the caller’s supported data type and planar configuration combinations. On success, fills yuvaPixmapInfo with the chosen planar config, subsampling, orientation, chroma siting, plane color types, and row bytes.
requirements: yuvaPixmapInfo must be non-null to receive the output.
supportedDataTypes must list the combinations supported by the caller; if no supported combination matches the codec’s capabilities, returns false.

functions.name: SkCodec::getYUVAPlanes
functions.description: Decodes the image into caller-provided YUV(A) pixmaps. Always attempts a full decode. Use queryYUVAInfo() first to configure yuvaPixmaps correctly.
requirements: yuvaPixmaps must be preallocated and configured per a prior successful queryYUVAInfo() call.
If the codec does not support YUVA for the requested configuration, returns an error Result (e.g., kUnimplemented).

functions.name: SkCodec::startIncrementalDecode
functions.signature: SkCodec::Result SkCodec::startIncrementalDecode(const SkImageInfo& dstInfo, void* dst, size_t rowBytes, const SkCodec::Options* options)
functions.description: Prepares the codec for incremental decoding into the destination buffer with the given options. May require rewinding the stream. Intended for progressive or partial data scenarios.
requirements: dst must be non-null and large enough to hold the requested image or subset based on dstInfo and rowBytes.
rowBytes must be sufficient for one row of dstInfo.
If options->fSubset is provided, it must be within the image bounds and adhere to format-specific constraints (e.g., WEBP even top/left).
On kIncompleteInput, this may be called again after more data arrives.
If it returns a failure other than kIncompleteInput, incremental decoding cannot proceed until reinitialized.

functions.name: SkCodec::incrementalDecode
functions.description: Continues an incremental decode previously started with startIncrementalDecode. Returns kSuccess when all requested lines are decoded, or kIncompleteInput if more data is needed. Does not fill uninitialized rows; the caller is responsible for initializing or managing skipped/remaining rows.
requirements: Must only be called after startIncrementalDecode() has been called and returned kSuccess; otherwise returns kInvalidParameters.
If rowsDecoded is non-null, it will be set to the total number of lines initialized so far only when kIncompleteInput is returned.

functions.name: SkCodec::startScanlineDecode
functions.signature: SkCodec::Result SkCodec::startScanlineDecode(const SkImageInfo& dstInfo, const SkCodec::Options* options)
functions.description: Prepares the codec for scanline decoding with the specified destination info and options. After success, getScanlines/skipScanlines may be called. May require rewinding the stream. Not all codecs support scanline decoding.
requirements: If options is provided, it controls zero initialization and subset behavior; for scanline decoding, subset top must be zero and subset height must equal the full height; subset left/width may be used for partial scanlines.
dstInfo may request scaling; if unsupported, an error Result is returned.
Must be called before getScanlines() or skipScanlines().

functions.name: SkCodec::getScanlines
functions.signature: int SkCodec::getScanlines(void* dst, int countLines, size_t rowBytes)
functions.description: Decodes the next countLines scanlines into dst. If fewer lines are decoded than requested (e.g., due to incomplete input), remaining lines are filled with a default value.
requirements: startScanlineDecode() must have been called successfully beforehand.
dst must be non-null and large enough to hold countLines scanlines at the given rowBytes.
rowBytes must be large enough for one decoded row.
countLines must be non-negative and must not request more scanlines than remain without handling the partial return value.

functions.name: SkCodec::skipScanlines
functions.description: Skips the next countLines scanlines during a scanline decode session.
requirements: startScanlineDecode() must have been called successfully beforehand.
countLines must be >= 0 and must not move past the end of the image.
May fail (return false) for reasons including incomplete input or invalid usage.

functions.name: SkCodec::getScanlineOrder
functions.description: Returns the order in which scanlines will be output by the scanline decoder (e.g., top-down or bottom-up). Undefined before startScanlineDecode().
requirements: Call only after a successful startScanlineDecode(); otherwise the value is undefined.

functions.name: SkCodec::nextScanline
functions.description: Returns the y-coordinate of the next output row to be returned by the scanline decoder, accounting for formats with unusual ordering (e.g., bottom-up BMP).
requirements: Meaningful only during an active scanline decoding session; results are undefined otherwise.

functions.name: SkCodec::outputScanline
functions.description: Maps an input scanline index (in encoded order) to the output y-coordinate, accounting for formats with unusual row orderings.
requirements: Meaningful primarily during scanline decoding; caller must ensure inputScanline is within the valid range [0, height).

functions.name: SkCodec::getFrameCount
functions.description: Returns the number of frames in the image. May require reading through the stream; subsequent decode calls may therefore require a rewind. For partial inputs, the reported frame count may increase as more data becomes available.
requirements: None, but callers should be aware this may read/scan the stream and affect subsequent decoding if the stream is not rewindable.

functions.name: SkCodec::getFrameInfo
functions.signature: bool SkCodec::getFrameInfo(int index, SkCodec::FrameInfo* info) const
functions.description: Returns information about a single frame in a multi-frame image. Should be called after getFrameCount() to ensure frames are parsed. Only supported by animated (multi-frame) codecs; non-animated codecs may always return false.
requirements: index must be >= 0.
info must be non-null to receive the frame information.
Caller should invoke getFrameCount() beforehand to parse frames; otherwise the requested frame info may be unavailable.

functions.name: SkCodec::getFrameInfo
functions.description: Returns information for all frames in the image, possibly reading through the stream to determine frame metadata (including frame count). Future decoding may require a rewind after calling this.
requirements: None, but this may read the stream; if the stream is not rewindable, subsequent decode calls may fail without a rewind capability.

functions.name: SkCodec::getRepetitionCount
functions.description: Returns the number of times an animated image should repeat after the first playthrough. Returns kRepetitionCountInfinite (<0) for infinite looping, or 0 for still images or animations that play only once. Use isAnimated() to disambiguate the meaning of 0.
requirements: None, but may read the stream to find the repetition count; subsequent decodes may require a rewind.

functions.name: SkCodec::isAnimated
functions.description: Indicates whether the input is expected to contain more than one image frame. Some codecs may initially return kUnknown for partial inputs and later return kYes or kNo as more data becomes available.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkCodec::Register
functions.signature: static void SkCodec::Register(bool (*peek)(const void* data, size_t len), std::unique_ptr<SkCodec> (*make)(std::unique_ptr<SkStream> stream, SkCodec::Result* result))
functions.description: Registers a runtime decoder by providing a format-detection callback (peek) and a factory (make) that constructs an SkCodec from a stream. Not thread safe; intended for initialization before first use.
requirements: peek must be a valid function pointer returning true if the byte span appears to be this decoder’s format.
make must be a valid function pointer that attempts to construct a codec from the given stream and sets the Result as appropriate.
Not thread-safe: must be invoked during initialization, before concurrent decoding begins.

functions.name: SkCodecs::Register
functions.description: Registers or replaces a decoder entry in the SkCodecs registry used by SkCodec::MakeFromStream with explicit decoder lists. If an existing decoder with the same id exists, it is replaced in place. Not thread safe; initialize before first call.
requirements: d.id should be a stable identifier (e.g., lowercase file extension).
d.isFormat and d.makeFromStream must be valid function pointers.
Not thread-safe; must be called during initialization before the first MakeFromStream using this registry.

functions.name: SkCodecs::DeferredImage
functions.description: Creates an SkImage that defers allocation/decoding until first use, allowing caching on CPU or GPU. If alphaType is nullopt, an appropriate alpha type is chosen automatically. Forcing opaque (kOpaque_SkAlphaType) is not allowed and yields nullptr.
requirements: codec must be non-null and valid; ownership is transferred to the returned image factory.
If alphaType has a value, it must be kPremul_SkAlphaType or kUnpremul_SkAlphaType; passing kOpaque_SkAlphaType is invalid and will return nullptr.
Caller must handle a nullptr return on failure.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::MakeFromCodec
functions.description: Constructs an SkAndroidCodec that wraps an existing SkCodec. Use when you already have an SkCodec instance and want Android-oriented decode APIs. Returns nullptr if the codec is unsupported by SkAndroidCodec.
requirements: Caller must pass ownership of a valid SkCodec via std::unique_ptr; ownership transfers to SkAndroidCodec on success.
If the encoded format is unsupported for Android decoding, the function returns nullptr.
On success the returned SkAndroidCodec owns the SkCodec; the caller must not use the passed-in SkCodec after the call.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::MakeFromStream
functions.description: Creates an SkAndroidCodec from an input stream containing encoded image data. Optionally supplies a PNG chunk reader to handle unknown PNG chunks. Returns nullptr if the stream does not contain a decodable image.
requirements: Caller must pass ownership of the SkStream via std::unique_ptr; if decoding cannot be created, the stream is deleted immediately.
If decoding is created, SkAndroidCodec (via SkCodec) takes ownership of the stream and will delete it when done.
SkPngChunkReader pointer is optional and may be nullptr; if provided, it must remain valid during construction.
The stream must provide the encoded data at its current position; if it does not contain a supported image, nullptr is returned.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::MakeFromData
functions.signature: static std::unique_ptr<SkAndroidCodec> MakeFromData(sk_sp<const SkData>, SkPngChunkReader* = nullptr);
functions.description: Creates an SkAndroidCodec from in-memory encoded image data. Optionally supplies a PNG chunk reader to handle unknown PNG chunks. Returns nullptr if the data is not a supported encoded image.
requirements: Caller must supply a non-null sk_sp<const SkData> referencing the encoded bytes; SkAndroidCodec retains a reference as needed.
SkPngChunkReader pointer is optional and may be nullptr; if provided, it must remain valid during construction.
If the data does not represent a decodable image, the function returns nullptr.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::~SkAndroidCodec
functions.description: Virtual destructor for SkAndroidCodec. Cleans up internal resources and owned objects (such as the underlying SkCodec).
requirements: No special caller requirements. Ensure any non-owning pointers retrieved from this object (e.g., codec()) are not used after destruction.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::getInfo
functions.description: Returns the SkImageInfo describing the encoded image’s dimensions and default output configuration as cached by SkAndroidCodec. Primarily used to know the base size and color/alpha types before decoding.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the SkAndroidCodec instance.
Do not retain the reference beyond the codec’s lifetime.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::getICCProfile
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the ICC profile embedded in the encoded data, if present. Useful for color management when choosing an output color space.
requirements: The returned pointer may be nullptr if no ICC profile is present.
The returned pointer is owned by the codec; it remains valid as long as the SkAndroidCodec (and its SkCodec) remain alive.
Caller must not modify or free the returned profile.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::getEncodedFormat
functions.description: Returns the encoded image format (e.g., JPEG, PNG, etc.) of the source data.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::computeOutputColorType
functions.description: Determines the appropriate output SkColorType for decoding, given a requested type. May override the request (e.g., defaulting to kF16 for high-precision images) if the requested type is not supported or not optimal.
requirements: Caller may pass any SkColorType; the function will return the chosen compatible/output type.
Do not assume the returned type matches the request; use the returned value for subsequent decode setup.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::computeOutputAlphaType
functions.description: Determines the output alpha type for decoding. If the image has alpha, the requested unpremultiplied setting is honored; otherwise, returns the appropriate opaque/premul alpha type.
requirements: requestedUnpremul indicates whether the caller prefers unpremultiplied output when alpha is present.
Caller should use the returned alpha type when constructing the output SkImageInfo.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::computeOutputColorSpace
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkColorSpace> computeOutputColorSpace(SkColorType outputColorType, sk_sp<SkColorSpace> prefColorSpace = nullptr);
functions.description: Selects an appropriate output color space for decoding, given an output color type and an optional preferred color space. The preferred space may be ignored for some color types.
requirements: outputColorType must be the intended decode output color type (often from computeOutputColorType).
prefColorSpace is optional and may be nullptr; the returned color space may differ based on codec capabilities and color type.
Caller should use the returned color space with the output SkImageInfo.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::computeSampleSize
functions.description: Computes a sample size factor to downscale decoding so that the output is as close as possible to the requested size. Also updates the provided size to the actual sampled size chosen (the smallest sampled size larger than the input).
requirements: size must be non-null and contain the desired output dimensions on input.
On return, *size is modified to the codec’s chosen sampled dimensions not smaller than the requested size.
The returned integer is the sample size to set in AndroidOptions::fSampleSize for decoding.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::getSampledDimensions
functions.description: Returns the dimensions of the decoded image when downscaling by the given sampleSize. If the sampleSize does not evenly divide the original, dimensions may be rounded up or down. Output is always at least 1 in each dimension.
requirements: sampleSize must be a positive integer; if larger than an original dimension, the corresponding output dimension will be clamped to at least 1.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::getSupportedSubset
functions.description: Validates and possibly adjusts a requested subset rectangle to one that the codec can decode. Returns true and may modify desiredSubset to a supported rectangle; returns false if invalid.
requirements: desiredSubset must be a pointer to a rectangle within the image bounds as specified by getInfo().
If desiredSubset is nullptr or not fully contained within the image, the function returns false and desiredSubset’s value is undefined.
Caller must be prepared for desiredSubset to be modified to a supported subset even when the input was valid.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::getSampledSubsetDimensions
functions.signature: SkISize getSampledSubsetDimensions(int sampleSize, const SkIRect& subset) const;
functions.description: Returns the output dimensions of decoding a valid subset at the given sampling factor. Returns zero size if inputs are invalid.
requirements: sampleSize must be a positive integer.
subset must be a valid subset of the original image dimensions and be supported by SkAndroidCodec (use getSupportedSubset to obtain/verify).

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::getAndroidPixels
functions.signature: SkCodec::Result getAndroidPixels(const SkImageInfo& info, void* pixels, size_t rowBytes, const AndroidOptions* options);
functions.description: Decodes pixels into the provided buffer using Android-oriented options. Supports optional sampling and subsetting specified via options->fSampleSize and options->fSubset. Returns SkCodec::Result indicating success or specific failure.
requirements: pixels must point to a writable memory block of at least (info.height() - 1) * rowBytes + (info.width() * bytesPerPixel) bytes.
rowBytes must be sufficient for a scanline of the requested info; it must be at least info.minRowBytes().
info describes the desired output format; sizes not matching the source imply a request to scale or subset, which may fail.
options may be nullptr to use defaults (no scaling, no subsetting).
If scaling or subsetting is requested and unsupported, the function returns an error result; caller must handle non-success return values.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::getPixels
functions.signature: SkCodec::Result getPixels(const SkImageInfo& info, void* pixels, size_t rowBytes);
functions.description: Inline wrapper that calls getAndroidPixels with default options (no scaling or subsetting). Provided for API parity with SkCodec.
requirements: Same as getAndroidPixels(info, pixels, rowBytes).
Caller must handle the returned SkCodec::Result.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::codec
functions.description: Returns the underlying SkCodec pointer managed by SkAndroidCodec. Useful for accessing lower-level codec functionality.
requirements: Returned pointer is non-owning and remains valid only while the SkAndroidCodec instance is alive.
Caller must not delete or outlive the returned SkCodec pointer.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::getGainmapAndroidCodec
functions.description: Retrieves the gainmap associated with the image, if any. On success, fills outInfo with parameters for rendering the gainmap and optionally returns a codec to decode the gainmap image. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
requirements: outInfo must be non-null; it will be populated on success.
outCodec is optional and may be nullptr; if non-null, it will be populated with a new SkAndroidCodec for the gainmap image on success (ownership transferred to caller).
Returns false if no gainmap exists or extraction fails; callers must check the boolean result before using outputs.

functions.name: SkAndroidCodec::getAndroidGainmap
functions.description: Retrieves gainmap information and a stream for the gainmap image (currently only works for JPEG images). Intended as a transitional API. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
requirements: This API only works for JPEG images; for other formats it may return false.
outInfo must be non-null; it will be populated on success.
outGainmapImageStream is optionality not explicitly stated; if provided, it will be populated with a stream to the gainmap image on success and the caller assumes ownership of the returned stream.
Callers must check the boolean result before using outputs.

functions.name: SkEncodedOriginToMatrix
functions.signature: static inline SkMatrix SkEncodedOriginToMatrix(SkEncodedOrigin origin, int w, int h)
functions.description: Returns a transform matrix that maps a source image with upper-left at [0,0] and size w×h, interpreted with the given EXIF orientation (origin), into a correctly oriented destination rectangle [0,0,w,h]. Use this to reorient decoded pixel data according to its encoded EXIF orientation before rendering or further processing. Aborts if origin is not a recognized SkEncodedOrigin value.
requirements: origin must be one of the defined SkEncodedOrigin enum constants (kTopLeft_SkEncodedOrigin through kLeftBottom_SkEncodedOrigin); passing other values can trigger SK_ABORT.
w and h represent the source image width and height; they should be non-negative integers matching the actual source dimensions.
The source coordinate system is assumed to have its upper-left corner at [0,0] with extent [0,0,w,h]; callers should supply w and h consistent with that assumption.
Returned SkMatrix is deterministic and has no side effects; no special initialization is required beyond including SkMatrix definitions.

functions.name: SkEncodedOriginToMatrixInverse
functions.signature: static inline SkMatrix SkEncodedOriginToMatrixInverse(SkEncodedOrigin origin, int w, int h)
functions.description: Returns the inverse of SkEncodedOriginToMatrix(origin, w, h), i.e., a matrix that maps from the correctly oriented destination space [0,0,w,h] back to the source space as stored under the given EXIF orientation. Useful for hit-testing or mapping coordinates from display space to the original encoded pixel space. Aborts if origin is not a recognized SkEncodedOrigin value.
requirements: origin must be one of the defined SkEncodedOrigin enum constants (kTopLeft_SkEncodedOrigin through kLeftBottom_SkEncodedOrigin); passing other values can trigger SK_ABORT.
w and h represent the source image width and height; they should be non-negative integers matching the actual source dimensions.
Callers should use the same w and h they would use with SkEncodedOriginToMatrix to ensure the inverse corresponds correctly.
Returned SkMatrix is deterministic and has no side effects; no special initialization is required beyond including SkMatrix definitions.

functions.name: SkEncodedOriginSwapsWidthHeight
functions.description: Returns true if the given EXIF orientation implies a 90° rotation, in which case the perceived width and height are swapped relative to an upright image. Use this to precompute destination dimensions or allocate buffers appropriately when reorienting images.
requirements: origin should be a valid SkEncodedOrigin enum constant; behavior for out-of-range values is not defined by this header.
No additional preconditions; the function is pure and does not modify global state.

functions.name: SkPixmapUtils::Orient
functions.signature: SK_API bool SkPixmapUtils::Orient(const SkPixmap& dst, const SkPixmap& src, SkEncodedOrigin origin);
functions.description: Copies pixels from src into dst, applying the orientation specified by origin (e.g., rotations and/or flips corresponding to SkEncodedOrigin). Returns false and performs no copy if inputs are invalid. Typical usage: prepare a destination pixmap with dimensions that match the source after applying the requested orientation, then call Orient and check the boolean result before using the destination data. Specific format-compatibility details beyond this are not documented in this header and may be implementation-defined.
requirements: Caller must provide initialized SkPixmap objects for both dst (writable) and src (readable).
The destination dimensions must match the source dimensions after applying the specified SkEncodedOrigin transform (e.g., swap width/height for 90°/270° rotations).
origin must be a valid SkEncodedOrigin value.
The caller must check the boolean return value; on false, no copy is performed and dst must not be assumed to contain oriented data.
Any additional constraints on pixel format or color type compatibility are unspecified in this header and may cause the function to return false if not satisfied.

functions.name: SkPixmapUtils::SwapWidthHeight
functions.description: Returns a copy of the provided SkImageInfo with width and height swapped. Use when reinterpreting or allocating pixel storage for images that have been rotated 90°/270° or when an orientation change swaps dimensions.
requirements: Caller must supply a valid, initialized SkImageInfo.
No other preconditions are documented; the function does not fail and returns a new SkImageInfo value.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Arithmetic
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Arithmetic(SkScalar k1, SkScalar k2, SkScalar k3, SkScalar k4, bool enforcePMColor, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> background, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> foreground, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Creates an image filter that blends background and foreground using the arithmetic formula k1*Fg*Bg + k2*Fg + k3*Bg + k4. If either input is null, the implicit source image is used. Optionally clamps RGB to alpha when enforcePMColor is true and can crop inputs/outputs with cropRect.
requirements: background may be null to use the implicit source image.
foreground may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional; if provided, it crops inputs and output.
Return is a reference-counted SkImageFilter; callers must handle a potentially null return only if construction fails (not specified here).

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Blend
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Blend(SkBlendMode mode, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> background, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> foreground = nullptr, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Composites two image filters using the specified SkBlendMode (Dst=background, Src=foreground). If either input is null, uses the implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits inputs and output.
requirements: background may be null to use the implicit source image.
foreground may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops inputs and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Blur
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Blur(SkScalar sigmaX, SkScalar sigmaY, SkTileMode tileMode, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Applies a separable Gaussian blur with given sigmas along X and Y to the input. The tile mode controls sampling when the blur kernel samples outside input bounds. If input is null, the implicit source image is blurred. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: tileMode controls behavior at edges; kMirror may not be supported (per note).
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::ColorFilter
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::ColorFilter(sk_sp<SkColorFilter> cf, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Applies the provided SkColorFilter to the results of the input filter (or the source image if input is null). Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: cf must be a valid SkColorFilter; behavior is undefined if null (unknown per header).
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Compose
functions.description: Composes two filters such that the output is outer(inner(source)). Useful for chaining filters where inner’s output becomes outer’s input.
requirements: outer must be a valid SkImageFilter (unknown behavior if null).
inner must be a valid SkImageFilter (unknown behavior if null).

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Crop
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Crop(const SkRect& rect, SkTileMode tileMode, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input);
functions.description: Applies a crop to the results of the input filter: inside rect is unmodified; outside rect is filled according to tileMode (defaults to kDecal via the other overload). If input is null, the implicit source image is cropped.
requirements: rect defines the crop area in local space.
tileMode applies to pixels outside rect.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::DisplacementMap
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::DisplacementMap(SkColorChannel xChannelSelector, SkColorChannel yChannelSelector, SkScalar scale, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> displacement, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> color, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Offsets the color input per pixel using a vector derived from two channels of the displacement input: scale * (color[xChannel], color[yChannel]). If either input is null, the implicit source image is used. Optional cropRect limits color input and output.
requirements: xChannelSelector and yChannelSelector select RGBA channels to map x and y displacement.
displacement may be null to use the implicit source image for displacement.
color may be null to use the implicit source image for color.
cropRect is optional and crops color input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::DropShadow
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::DropShadow(SkScalar dx, SkScalar dy, SkScalar sigmaX, SkScalar sigmaY, SkColor4f color, sk_sp<SkColorSpace> colorSpace, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Renders a drop shadow of the input content and includes the original content in the result. The shadow is offset by (dx, dy) and blurred with the given sigmas. Shadow color is specified by SkColor4f and optional colorSpace. If input is null, uses the implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: dx and dy are offsets in local space.
sigmaX and sigmaY control blur radius along X and Y.
colorSpace may be null to use a default/implicit space (per inline convenience).
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::DropShadowOnly
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::DropShadowOnly(SkScalar dx, SkScalar dy, SkScalar sigmaX, SkScalar sigmaY, SkColor4f color, sk_sp<SkColorSpace>, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Renders only the drop shadow of the input content (omits original content). Shadow offset and blur are controlled by dx/dy and sigmas. Color is SkColor4f with optional color space. If input is null, uses implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: dx and dy are offsets in local space.
sigmaX and sigmaY control blur radius along X and Y.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Empty
functions.description: Produces an image filter that always evaluates to transparent black.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Image
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Image(sk_sp<SkImage> image, const SkRect& srcRect, const SkRect& dstRect, const SkSamplingOptions& sampling);
functions.description: Produces an image filter that draws a subset of the provided image (srcRect) into dstRect using the specified sampling. If image is null, the filter evaluates to transparent black.
requirements: image may be null; in that case, the filter evaluates to transparent black.
srcRect defines source pixels sampled from the image.
dstRect defines local destination bounds for drawing.
sampling controls how the image is sampled during scaling/transform.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Magnifier
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Magnifier(const SkRect& lensBounds, SkScalar zoomAmount, SkScalar inset, const SkSamplingOptions& sampling, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Applies a magnifying lens effect: content within lensBounds is magnified by zoomAmount with a fish-eye style inset around the edges. Uses sampling when magnifying. If input is null, uses the implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: lensBounds defines the magnifier’s outer bounds.
zoomAmount controls magnification amount.
inset controls the size/width of the distortion band around magnified content.
sampling specifies sampling for magnified pixels.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::MatrixConvolution
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::MatrixConvolution(const SkISize& kernelSize, const SkScalar kernel[], SkScalar gain, SkScalar bias, const SkIPoint& kernelOffset, SkTileMode tileMode, bool convolveAlpha, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Applies an N×M convolution to the input image using the provided kernel values. Allows gain and bias adjustment, an integer kernelOffset for alignment, tile mode for out-of-bounds sampling, and optional alpha convolution. If input is null, uses the implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits processing.
requirements: kernel must contain kernelSize.width * kernelSize.height elements in row-major order.
kernelOffset is applied to pixel coordinates before convolution (e.g., {1,1} for a 3×3 centered kernel).
tileMode controls access outside the image; kMirror may not be supported (per note).
If convolveAlpha is false, only RGB are convolved and alpha is copied from source.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops processing/output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::MatrixTransform
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::MatrixTransform(const SkMatrix& matrix, const SkSamplingOptions& sampling, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input);
functions.description: Transforms the input image by the provided matrix in the filter’s local space (applied prior to any canvas transform). Uses the specified sampling. If input is null, uses the implicit source image.
requirements: matrix is applied in local space to the content prior to canvas transforms.
sampling controls how pixels are sampled during transformation.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Merge
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Merge(sk_sp<SkImageFilter>* const filters, int count, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Merges multiple filters by drawing their outputs in order with src-over blending. Null entries in filters use the implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits all inputs and the output.
requirements: filters must point to an array containing exactly count elements.
Each element of filters may be null to use the implicit source image.
count specifies the number of inputs to merge and must be non-negative (implied by int; exact constraints unknown).
cropRect is optional and crops inputs and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Offset
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Offset(SkScalar dx, SkScalar dy, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Offsets (translates) the input image by (dx, dy) in local space. If input is null, uses the implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: dx and dy specify the translation in local space.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Picture
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Picture(sk_sp<SkPicture> pic, const SkRect& targetRect);
functions.description: Produces an image filter that draws the SkPicture clipped to both targetRect and the picture’s cull rect. If pic is null, the filter evaluates to transparent black.
requirements: pic may be null; in that case, the filter evaluates to transparent black.
targetRect defines the drawing region for the picture.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::RuntimeShader
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::RuntimeShader(const SkRuntimeEffectBuilder& builder, std::string_view childShaderName, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input);
functions.description: Produces an image filter whose output is filled by evaluating a runtime SkShader produced by builder. The runtime shader samples the named child shader using the same coordinate as the parent. Requires GPU backend or SkSL. If input is null, the implicit source image is bound as the child shader. Sample radius defaults to 0 in this overload.
requirements: builder must define a child shader matching childShaderName (or exactly one child if childShaderName is empty).
input may be null to use the implicit source image as the child shader.
Requires GPU backend or SkSL to be compiled in (environment requirement).

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Shader
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Shader(sk_sp<SkShader> shader, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Convenience overload that creates an image filter from an SkShader, defaulting to no dithering. If shader is null, the filter evaluates to transparent black. Optional cropRect can limit output.
requirements: shader may be null; in that case, the filter evaluates to transparent black.
cropRect is optional and crops output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Tile
