functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Tile(const SkRect& src, const SkRect& dst, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input);
functions.description: Tiles the src rectangle from the input image/filter across the dst rectangle, repeating as needed. If input is null, uses the implicit source image.
requirements: src defines the region to tile from the input.
dst defines the region to fill with tiled content in local space.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Dilate
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Dilate(SkScalar radiusX, SkScalar radiusY, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Performs morphological dilation: each pixel channel is replaced with the maximum within the given x/y radii neighborhood. If input is null, uses the implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: radiusX and radiusY define the dilation neighborhood extents along X and Y.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::Erode
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::Erode(SkScalar radiusX, SkScalar radiusY, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Performs morphological erosion: each pixel channel is replaced with the minimum within the given x/y radii neighborhood. If input is null, uses the implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: radiusX and radiusY define the erosion neighborhood extents along X and Y.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::DistantLitDiffuse
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::DistantLitDiffuse(const SkPoint3& direction, SkColor lightColor, SkScalar surfaceScale, SkScalar kd, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Computes diffuse lighting using a distant light. The input’s alpha channel represents a height map used to approximate normals. Surface scale converts alpha to height; kd is the diffuse reflectance. If input is null, uses the implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: direction specifies the light direction.
lightColor sets the light’s color.
surfaceScale scales alpha to height.
kd is the diffuse reflectance coefficient.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::PointLitDiffuse
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::PointLitDiffuse(const SkPoint3& location, SkColor lightColor, SkScalar surfaceScale, SkScalar kd, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Computes diffuse lighting using a point light at location. The input’s alpha acts as height. surfaceScale converts alpha to height; kd is diffuse reflectance. If input is null, uses the implicit source image. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: location specifies the point light position.
lightColor sets the light’s color.
surfaceScale scales alpha to height.
kd is the diffuse reflectance coefficient.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::SpotLitDiffuse
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::SpotLitDiffuse(const SkPoint3& location, const SkPoint3& target, SkScalar falloffExponent, SkScalar cutoffAngle, SkColor lightColor, SkScalar surfaceScale, SkScalar kd, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Computes diffuse lighting using a spot light aimed from location to target. Lighting is limited to within cutoffAngle of the light direction with falloff controlled by falloffExponent. The input’s alpha acts as height; surfaceScale converts alpha to height; kd is diffuse reflectance. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: location specifies the spot light position.
target specifies the spot light aim point.
falloffExponent controls intensity falloff outside the cutoff.
cutoffAngle limits the fully lit cone angle.
lightColor sets the light’s color.
surfaceScale scales alpha to height.
kd is the diffuse reflectance coefficient.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::DistantLitSpecular
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::DistantLitSpecular(const SkPoint3& direction, SkColor lightColor, SkScalar surfaceScale, SkScalar ks, SkScalar shininess, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Computes specular lighting from a distant light. The input’s alpha channel represents a height map for normals. surfaceScale converts alpha to height; ks is specular reflectance; shininess controls highlight size. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: direction specifies the light direction.
lightColor sets the light’s color.
surfaceScale scales alpha to height.
ks is the specular reflectance coefficient.
shininess is the specular exponent (higher is shinier).
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::PointLitSpecular
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::PointLitSpecular(const SkPoint3& location, SkColor lightColor, SkScalar surfaceScale, SkScalar ks, SkScalar shininess, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Computes specular lighting from a point light. The input’s alpha acts as height. surfaceScale converts alpha to height; ks is specular reflectance; shininess controls highlight size. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: location specifies the point light position.
lightColor sets the light’s color.
surfaceScale scales alpha to height.
ks is the specular reflectance coefficient.
shininess is the specular exponent.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkImageFilters::SpotLitSpecular
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkImageFilter> SkImageFilters::SpotLitSpecular(const SkPoint3& location, const SkPoint3& target, SkScalar falloffExponent, SkScalar cutoffAngle, SkColor lightColor, SkScalar surfaceScale, SkScalar ks, SkScalar shininess, sk_sp<SkImageFilter> input, const CropRect& cropRect = {});
functions.description: Computes specular lighting from a spot light aimed from location to target, limited by cutoffAngle with falloff controlled by falloffExponent. The input’s alpha acts as height. surfaceScale converts alpha to height; ks is specular reflectance; shininess controls highlight size. Optional cropRect limits input and output.
requirements: location specifies the spot light position.
target specifies the spot light aim point.
falloffExponent controls intensity falloff outside the cutoff.
cutoffAngle limits the fully lit cone angle.
lightColor sets the light’s color.
surfaceScale scales alpha to height.
ks is the specular reflectance coefficient.
shininess is the specular exponent.
input may be null to use the implicit source image.
cropRect is optional and crops input and output.

functions.name: SkGradient::Interpolation::FromFlags
functions.description: Legacy helper that constructs an Interpolation from a bitfield of flags. Currently only uses bit 0 to select in-premultiplied interpolation; other interpolation fields use defaults. Intended for compatibility paths when upgrading older code.
requirements: flags is a 32-bit bitfield; bit 0 set means InPremul::kYes, otherwise InPremul::kNo.
No other bits are defined by this API; their effect is unknown.

functions.name: SkGradient::Colors::colors
functions.description: Returns the span of color stops (as SkColor4f) associated with this gradient color specification. Use to read the provided color stop array without copying.
requirements: The SkGradient::Colors instance must remain alive while the returned SkSpan is used.
The underlying color data referenced by the span must remain valid for the duration of use.

functions.name: SkGradient::Colors::positions
functions.description: Returns the span of relative positions for the color stops. If empty, colors are distributed evenly. When provided, values must be in [0,1] and strictly increasing; implicit stops at 0 and/or 1 may be added as described in the class docs.
requirements: The SkGradient::Colors instance must remain alive while the returned SkSpan is used.
If non-empty, the span length must equal the colors() span length (otherwise inputs are discarded internally).
If non-empty, each value must be in the range [0.0, 1.0] and strictly increasing.
If the first position is not 0.0, an implicit stop at 0.0 using colors()[0] is added.
If the last position is less than 1.0, an implicit stop at 1.0 using the last color is added.

functions.name: SkGradient::Colors::colorSpace
functions.description: Returns the optional SkColorSpace associated with the provided colors. If null, colors are treated as sRGB.
requirements: Caller must not assume this is non-null; handle the null case as sRGB.
The returned smart pointer reference remains valid while the SkGradient::Colors object remains alive.

functions.name: SkGradient::Colors::tileMode
functions.description: Returns the SkTileMode used for the gradient outside the [0,1] domain of color stops (e.g., clamp, repeat, mirror).

functions.name: SkGradient::colors
functions.description: Returns the Colors specification encapsulated by this SkGradient, including color stops, optional positions, tile mode, and color space.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the SkGradient object remains alive.

functions.name: SkGradient::interpolation
functions.description: Returns the Interpolation settings used by this SkGradient, including in-premul behavior, interpolation color space, and hue method.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the SkGradient object remains alive.

functions.name: SkShaders::LinearGradient
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> SkShaders::LinearGradient(const SkPoint pts[2], const SkGradient& grad, const SkMatrix* lm = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates a shader that draws a linear gradient along the line between two points. Returns nullptr if inputs are invalid.
requirements: pts must point to an array of exactly two valid SkPoint values representing the end points.

grad must be a valid SkGradient describing the colors and interpolation; if grad.colors().positions() is non-empty, its values must be in [0,1] and strictly increasing, with length equal to the number of colors.
lm may be null; if non-null, it must point to a valid SkMatrix.
Caller must handle a potential nullptr return when inputs are invalid.

functions.name: SkShaders::RadialGradient
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> SkShaders::RadialGradient(SkPoint center, float radius, const SkGradient& grad, const SkMatrix* lm = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates a shader that draws a radial gradient centered at center with the given radius. Returns nullptr if inputs are invalid.
requirements: radius must be positive (> 0).
grad must be a valid SkGradient; if positions are provided, they must be in [0,1], strictly increasing, and match the number of colors.
lm may be null; if non-null, it must point to a valid SkMatrix.
Caller must handle a potential nullptr return when inputs are invalid.

functions.name: SkShaders::TwoPointConicalGradient
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> SkShaders::TwoPointConicalGradient(SkPoint start, float startRadius, SkPoint end, float endRadius, const SkGradient& grad, const SkMatrix* lm = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates a shader that draws a conical gradient defined by two circles (start, startRadius) and (end, endRadius), following the HTML5 2D context specification. Returns nullptr if inputs are invalid.
requirements: startRadius must be positive (> 0).
endRadius must be positive (> 0).
grad must be a valid SkGradient; if positions are provided, they must be in [0,1], strictly increasing, and match the number of colors.
lm may be null; if non-null, it must point to a valid SkMatrix.
Caller must handle a potential nullptr return when inputs are invalid.

functions.name: SkShaders::SweepGradient
functions.signature: sk_sp<SkShader> SkShaders::SweepGradient(SkPoint center, float startAngle, float endAngle, const SkGradient& grad, const SkMatrix* lm = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates a shader that draws a sweep (conic) gradient around center, sweeping from startAngle to endAngle. Accepts angles outside [0,360]; only the range between 0 and 360 degrees is drawn per CSS conic-gradient semantics. Returns nullptr if startAngle is not less than endAngle or if other inputs are invalid.
requirements: startAngle must be less than endAngle; otherwise, returns nullptr.

Color stop handling: if grad.colors().positions() do not include 0 or 1 but are within [0,1], the outer stops are repeated at 0 and/or 1. Positions < 0 are clamped to 0; positions > 1 are clamped to 1.
grad must be a valid SkGradient; if positions are provided, they must be in [0,1] and strictly increasing, with length equal to the number of colors.
lm may be null; if non-null, it must point to a valid SkMatrix.
Caller must handle a potential nullptr return when inputs are invalid.

functions.name: SkGradientShader::MakeLinear
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkShader> SkGradientShader::MakeLinear(const SkPoint pts[2], const SkColor colors[], const SkScalar pos[], int count, SkTileMode mode, uint32_t flags = 0, const SkMatrix* localMatrix = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates a linear gradient shader between two points using SkColor stops. Use this to fill along the line segment from pts[0] to pts[1], with colors distributed by pos (or evenly if pos is null). The shader can be tiled outside the 0..1 range per mode. Optional flags can tweak interpolation behavior; an optional localMatrix can transform the gradient in shader space.
requirements: pts must point to an array of exactly 2 SkPoint elements defining the start and end of the gradient.
colors must point to an array of length count containing at least 2 colors.
pos may be NULL; if non-null it must point to an array of length count with values in [0.0, 1.0] that are strictly increasing.
If pos is non-null and pos[0] != 0.0, an implicit stop at 0.0 is added with colors[0].
If pos is non-null and pos[count-1] != 1.0, an implicit stop at 1.0 is added with colors[count-1].
count must be >= 2.
mode specifies tiling behavior outside the gradient range and must be a valid SkTileMode value.
flags is optional; valid meanings include kInterpolateColorsInPremul_Flag as documented (legacy behavior).
localMatrix may be nullptr; if provided, it is applied to shader coordinates.
On degenerate inputs (e.g., pts[0] == pts[1]), behavior follows the class-level degeneracy notes; no error is returned.

functions.name: SkGradientShader::MakeLinear
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkShader> SkGradientShader::MakeLinear(const SkPoint pts[2], const SkColor4f colors[], sk_sp<SkColorSpace> colorSpace, const SkScalar pos[], int count, SkTileMode mode, const SkGradient::Interpolation& interpolation, const SkMatrix* localMatrix)
functions.description: Creates a linear gradient shader between two points using SkColor4f color stops in a specified colorSpace and explicit interpolation parameters. Use when precise color space and interpolation control is required. The gradient runs from pts[0] to pts[1], with stops from pos (or evenly if pos is null), and tiles per mode. An optional localMatrix transforms the gradient.
requirements: pts must point to an array of exactly 2 SkPoint elements defining the gradient line.
colors must point to an array of length count (>=2) of SkColor4f values.
colorSpace provides the color space for colors; exact nullability is not specified in this header (unknown if nullptr is allowed).
pos may be NULL; if non-null it must be an array of length count with values in [0.0, 1.0] that are strictly increasing.
If pos is non-null and pos[0] != 0.0, an implicit stop at 0.0 is added with colors[0].
If pos is non-null and pos[count-1] != 1.0, an implicit stop at 1.0 is added with colors[count-1].
count must be >= 2.
mode must be a valid SkTileMode.
interpolation controls gradient interpolation behavior and must be a valid SkGradient::Interpolation value.
localMatrix may be nullptr; if provided, it is applied to shader coordinates.
Degenerate inputs (e.g., pts[0] == pts[1]) produce defined fallback rendering as described in the class comments; no error is returned.

functions.name: SkGradientShader::MakeRadial
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkShader> SkGradientShader::MakeRadial(const SkPoint& center, SkScalar radius, const SkColor colors[], const SkScalar pos[], int count, SkTileMode mode, uint32_t flags = 0, const SkMatrix* localMatrix = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates a radial gradient shader centered at center with the given radius, using SkColor stops. Colors are distributed from the center (pos==0) to the circle edge (pos==1). The shader tiles outside the range per mode. Optional flags can affect interpolation; an optional localMatrix can transform the gradient.
requirements: radius must be positive.
colors must point to an array of length count containing at least 2 colors.
pos may be NULL; if non-null it must be an array of length count with values in [0.0, 1.0] that are strictly increasing.
If pos is non-null and pos[0] != 0.0, an implicit stop at 0.0 is added with colors[0].
If pos is non-null and pos[count-1] != 1.0, an implicit stop at 1.0 is added with colors[count-1].
count must be >= 2.
mode must be a valid SkTileMode.
flags is optional; valid meanings include kInterpolateColorsInPremul_Flag (legacy behavior).
localMatrix may be nullptr; if provided, it is applied to shader coordinates.
Degenerate radius approaching zero is handled per class comments (e.g., clamp draws last color, repeat/mirror average color, decal draws empty).

functions.name: SkGradientShader::MakeTwoPointConical
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkShader> SkGradientShader::MakeTwoPointConical(const SkPoint& start, SkScalar startRadius, const SkPoint& end, SkScalar endRadius, const SkColor colors[], const SkScalar pos[], int count, SkTileMode mode, uint32_t flags = 0, const SkMatrix* localMatrix = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates a two-point conical gradient shader defined by two circles (start, startRadius) and (end, endRadius) using SkColor stops. This follows the HTML Canvas 2D createRadialGradient semantics for interpreting the circles and color stops. Returns null if inputs are invalid. Optional flags and localMatrix are supported.
requirements: Inputs must describe a valid two-point conical gradient per the HTML Canvas 2D spec at http://dev.w3.org/html5/2dcontext/#dom-context-2d-createradialgradient (exact invalid conditions are not detailed here).
colors must point to an array of length count containing at least 2 colors.
pos may be NULL; if non-null it must be an array of length count with values in [0.0, 1.0] that are strictly increasing.
If pos is non-null and pos[0] != 0.0, an implicit stop at 0.0 is added with colors[0].
If pos is non-null and pos[count-1] != 1.0, an implicit stop at 1.0 is added with colors[count-1].
count must be >= 2.
mode must be a valid SkTileMode.
flags is optional; valid meanings include kInterpolateColorsInPremul_Flag (legacy behavior).
localMatrix may be nullptr; if provided, it is applied to shader coordinates.
Callers must handle the possibility of a null return when inputs are invalid (e.g., check the returned sk_sp before use).

functions.name: SkGradientShader::MakeSweep
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkShader> SkGradientShader::MakeSweep(SkScalar cx, SkScalar cy, const SkColor colors[], const SkScalar pos[], int count, SkTileMode mode, SkScalar startAngle, SkScalar endAngle, uint32_t flags, const SkMatrix* localMatrix)
functions.description: Creates a sweep (conic) gradient shader centered at (cx, cy) using SkColor stops. The gradient spans angles from startAngle to endAngle (degrees), accepting values outside 0..360, and tiles outside this angular range according to mode. If startAngle is not less than endAngle, a null shader is returned. An optional localMatrix can transform the gradient; flags control interpolation behavior.
requirements: colors must point to an array of length count containing at least 2 colors.
pos may be NULL; if non-null it must be an array of length count with values in [0.0, 1.0] that are strictly increasing.
If pos is non-null and pos[0] != 0.0, an implicit stop at 0.0 is added with colors[0].
If pos is non-null and pos[count-1] != 1.0, an implicit stop at 1.0 is added with colors[count-1].
count must be >= 2.
mode must be a valid SkTileMode and controls drawing outside the angular range.
startAngle and endAngle are in degrees; startAngle must be less than endAngle or a null pointer is returned.
Angles may be negative or greater than 360; the shader draws between 0 and 360 consistent with CSS conic-gradient semantics.
Color stops within (0,1) implicitly extend to 0 and/or 1 by repeating the respective outer color stops; stops <0 are clamped to 0 and >1 are clamped to 1.
flags is required for this overload; valid meanings include kInterpolateColorsInPremul_Flag (legacy behavior).
localMatrix may be nullptr; if provided, it is applied to shader coordinates.
Callers must handle a possible null return if startAngle >= endAngle.

functions.name: SkGradientShader::MakeSweep

requirements: colors must point to an array of length count containing at least 2 colors.

If pos is non-null and pos[count-1] != 1.0, an implicit stop at 1.0 is added with colors[count-1].
count must be >= 2.
This overload fixes mode to SkTileMode::kClamp and angular range to 0..360 degrees.
flags is optional; valid meanings include kInterpolateColorsInPremul_Flag (legacy behavior).
localMatrix may be nullptr; if provided, it is applied to shader coordinates.

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::SkColorMatrix
functions.description: Default constructor that initializes the color matrix to the identity transform. Use when you need a no-op color transform as a starting point for subsequent configuration (e.g., scaling, concatenation, saturation).

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::RGBtoYUV
functions.description: Creates a color matrix that converts from RGB to YUV based on the specified YUV color space. Typical usage is to obtain a matrix suitable for converting linear or sRGB RGB values to a chosen YUV space.
requirements: Parameter cs must be a valid SkYUVColorSpace enumerator.

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::YUVtoRGB
functions.description: Creates a color matrix that converts from YUV to RGB for the specified YUV color space. Often used to convert YUV image data to RGB for display or further processing.
requirements: Parameter cs must be a valid SkYUVColorSpace enumerator.

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::setIdentity
functions.description: Resets this matrix to the identity transform (no change to colors). Use to clear prior configuration before applying new transforms.

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::setScale
functions.signature: void SkColorMatrix::setScale(float rScale, float gScale, float bScale, float aScale = 1.0f)
functions.description: Configures this matrix to scale the RGBA channels by the specified factors. Commonly used to adjust brightness per channel or modulate alpha.
requirements: rScale, gScale, bScale, and aScale should be finite floats.
No specific range restrictions are documented; behavior for extreme values depends on downstream usage.

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::postTranslate
functions.signature: void SkColorMatrix::postTranslate(float dr, float dg, float db, float da)
functions.description: Applies an additive translation to the color channels (adds offsets to R, G, B, A). Typically used to bias channels after scaling or other transforms.
requirements: dr, dg, db, and da should be finite floats.

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::setConcat
functions.signature: void SkColorMatrix::setConcat(const SkColorMatrix& a, const SkColorMatrix& b)
functions.description: Sets this matrix to the concatenation of matrices a and b. The exact multiplication order is a then b (this = a ∘ b), as implied by the provided preConcat/postConcat wrappers. Use to combine two transforms into one.
requirements: Both a and b must be valid, initialized SkColorMatrix instances.

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::preConcat
functions.description: Left-concatenates mat with this matrix (this = this ∘ mat). This matches calling setConcat(*this, mat). Use to append a transform that is applied after the current one in typical right-multiplied vector conventions.
requirements: mat must be a valid, initialized SkColorMatrix.

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::postConcat
functions.description: Right-concatenates mat with this matrix (this = mat ∘ this). This matches calling setConcat(mat, *this). Use to prepend a transform that is applied before the current one in typical right-multiplied vector conventions.
requirements: mat must be a valid, initialized SkColorMatrix.

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::setSaturation
functions.description: Configures this matrix to adjust color saturation by the given factor. Typically, sat = 1 leaves colors unchanged, and sat = 0 produces a grayscale result; exact behavior follows Skia’s standard saturation matrix construction.
requirements: sat should be a finite float.
No specific range guarantees are documented.

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::setRowMajor
functions.description: Copies 20 floats from a row-major 4x5 matrix into this color matrix. Use to load a matrix from external storage.
requirements: src must be a valid pointer to at least 20 readable float values.
The values should be arranged row-major (4 rows of 5 floats).

functions.name: SkColorMatrix::getRowMajor
functions.description: Writes the current 4x5 color matrix coefficients to dst in row-major order. Use to extract the matrix for inspection or external use.
requirements: dst must be a valid pointer to at least 20 writable float locations.

functions.name: SkColorMatrixFilter::MakeLightingFilter
functions.description: Deprecated factory that creates a color filter equivalent to SkColorFilters::Lighting(mul, add). Intended to produce a filter that modulates source colors by a multiply color and then adds an offset color per channel. Use SkColorFilters::Lighting instead in new code. Returns a reference-counted SkColorFilter smart pointer.
requirements: mul must be a valid SkColor value (typically 32-bit ARGB).
add must be a valid SkColor value (typically 32-bit ARGB).
May be called without an instance (static member function).
Caller should be prepared to handle a null sk_sp<SkColorFilter> return if creation fails (not documented here, but common for factory functions).

functions.name: SkBlurMaskFilter::MakeEmboss
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkMaskFilter> SkBlurMaskFilter::MakeEmboss(SkScalar blurSigma, const SkScalar direction[3], SkScalar ambient, SkScalar specular);
functions.description: Factory function that creates an emboss-style SkMaskFilter. It applies a Gaussian blur with the given standard deviation before applying lighting based on a light direction, ambient term, and a specular coefficient. Typical usage: pass a 3-element direction vector [x,y,z], an ambient in [0..1], and a specular coefficient (e.g., 8). Returns a reference-counted SkMaskFilter or possibly null on failure. Note: This API is gated by SK_SUPPORT_LEGACY_EMBOSSMASKFILTER; it may be unavailable if that macro is not enabled at build time.
requirements: Requires SK_SUPPORT_LEGACY_EMBOSSMASKFILTER to be defined at build time for this API to be available.
The direction parameter must point to an array of at least 3 SkScalar elements representing [x, y, z].
ambient must be within the range 0 to 1 inclusive, representing the amount of ambient light.
blurSigma is a standard deviation for a Gaussian blur and must be non-negative.
Callers must handle the possibility that the returned sk_sp<SkMaskFilter> is null (factory may fail).

functions.name: SkDashPathEffect::Make
functions.signature: static sk_sp<SkPathEffect> SkDashPathEffect::Make(SkSpan<const SkScalar> intervals, SkScalar phase)
functions.description: Constructs a dash path effect from an array of alternating on/off lengths (in device units) and a starting phase. The intervals are provided as a SkSpan and are copied internally. This effect only impacts stroked paths. Typical usage: pass an even-length span of SkScalar values where even indices are “on” lengths and odd indices are “off” lengths, plus a phase offset that is interpreted modulo the sum of all intervals.
requirements: intervals.size() must be an even number and >= 2 (explicitly stated)
intervals entries represent alternating on/off segment lengths; lengths are expected in the same units as the stroke (inferred from context)
phase is an offset measured modulo the sum of all interval lengths; any SkScalar value is accepted (explicitly stated about modulo behavior)
The effect applies only to stroked paths; filling is unaffected (explicit note)
Intervals are copied by the function; the caller does not need to keep the storage alive after the call (explicitly stated)

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::Uniform::isArray
functions.description: Returns true if the uniform was declared as an array in SkSL (flag kArray_Flag set). Usage: query before supplying data to understand whether 'count' and array-sized data are expected.
requirements: The Uniform instance must be a valid descriptor obtained from SkRuntimeEffect::uniforms() or SkRuntimeEffect::findUniform().

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::Uniform::isColor
functions.description: Returns true if the uniform was declared with layout(color) (flag kColor_Flag set). Such uniforms expect unpremultiplied, extended-range sRGB inputs and will be transformed to working space automatically.
requirements: The Uniform instance must be a valid descriptor obtained from SkRuntimeEffect::uniforms() or SkRuntimeEffect::findUniform().
Callers providing values for color uniforms should supply unpremultiplied, extended-range sRGB values (e.g., SkColor4f).

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::Uniform::sizeInBytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes required for this uniform's storage within the packed uniform data block. Use to allocate or validate SkData passed to effect creation calls or builder assignments.
requirements: The Uniform instance must be a valid descriptor obtained from SkRuntimeEffect::uniforms() or SkRuntimeEffect::findUniform().

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::MakeForColorFilter
functions.signature: static SkRuntimeEffect::Result SkRuntimeEffect::MakeForColorFilter(SkString sksl, const SkRuntimeEffect::Options& options)
functions.description: Compiles SkSL source for a color filter runtime effect. Entry point must be: vec4 main(vec4 inColor). Returns a Result containing the effect or a compilation error string.
requirements: SkSL must provide an entry point compatible with a color filter: vec4/half4/float4 main(vec4 inColor).
If compilation fails, callers must check Result::errorText and not use the null effect.

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::MakeForShader
functions.signature: static SkRuntimeEffect::Result SkRuntimeEffect::MakeForShader(SkString sksl, const SkRuntimeEffect::Options& options)
functions.description: Compiles SkSL source for a shader runtime effect. Entry point must be: vec4 main(vec2 inCoords). The returned color should be premultiplied.
requirements: SkSL must provide an entry point compatible with a shader: vec4/half4/float4 main(vec2 inCoords).
Returned color from main should be premultiplied.
If compilation fails, callers must check Result::errorText and not use the null effect.

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::MakeForBlender
functions.signature: static SkRuntimeEffect::Result SkRuntimeEffect::MakeForBlender(SkString sksl, const SkRuntimeEffect::Options& options)
functions.description: Compiles SkSL source for a blender runtime effect. Entry point must be: vec4 main(vec4 srcColor, vec4 dstColor).
requirements: SkSL must provide an entry point compatible with a blender: vec4/half4/float4 main(vec4 srcColor, vec4 dstColor).
If compilation fails, callers must check Result::errorText and not use the null effect.

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::ChildPtr::ChildPtr
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty child pointer representing no child effect.
requirements: None beyond standard object lifetime rules.

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::ChildPtr::type
functions.description: Returns the contained child type if present (shader, color filter, or blender); std::nullopt if empty.
requirements: The ChildPtr must be initialized; returns std::nullopt when no child is set.

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::ChildPtr::shader
functions.description: Returns the contained SkShader pointer if the child is a shader; otherwise returns nullptr.
requirements: Only valid to dereference if non-null and of shader type; caller must null-check.

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::ChildPtr::colorFilter
functions.description: Returns the contained SkColorFilter pointer if the child is a color filter; otherwise returns nullptr.
requirements: Only valid to dereference if non-null and of color-filter type; caller must null-check.

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::ChildPtr::blender
functions.description: Returns the contained SkBlender pointer if the child is a blender; otherwise returns nullptr.
requirements: Only valid to dereference if non-null and of blender type; caller must null-check.

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::ChildPtr::flattenable
functions.description: Returns the contained object as SkFlattenable*, or nullptr if empty. Use to pass generically where a flattenable is needed.
requirements: Caller must treat the returned pointer as non-owning; lifetime is managed by the sk_sp inside ChildPtr.

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffect::makeShader

functions.name: SkRuntimeEffectBuilder::~SkRuntimeEffectBuilder

functions.name: SkEncoder::encodeRows

Internally delegates to the subclass-provided onEncodeRows implementation. Output destination/format specifics are unknown from this header.
requirements: numRows must be greater than 0.
The SkEncoder instance must be properly constructed with a valid SkPixmap source (provided at construction).
Requesting more rows than remain is allowed; the function will encode only the remaining rows.
Callers must check the boolean return value to handle encoding failures appropriately.
Behavior after all rows have been encoded is not specified; callers should stop requesting rows once the remaining rows have been encoded (inferred from the API’s design).

functions.name: SkEncoder::~SkEncoder
functions.description: Virtual destructor for SkEncoder, ensuring proper cleanup via base-class pointers. Use to destroy an encoder instance safely, including when referenced polymorphically. No return value and no parameters. Additional side effects or resource management details are not specified in this header.
requirements: Only destroy objects that were properly constructed.
Do not use the object after destruction.
Destruction occurs automatically at end of scope or when delete is called; do not delete the same object more than once.

functions.name: SkJpegEncoder::Encode
functions.signature: SK_API bool SkJpegEncoder::Encode(SkWStream* dst, const SkPixmap& src, const SkJpegEncoder::Options& options)
functions.description: Encodes the pixels from the given SkPixmap to the provided SkWStream as a JPEG. Encoding behavior (quality, chroma downsampling, alpha handling, optional XMP, origin) is controlled via Options. Returns true on success and false if the source is invalid or unsupported.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable SkWStream pointer that remains valid for the duration of the call.
src must reference initialized, readable pixel data in a supported color type/format.
options.fQuality must be in the range [0, 100].
JPEG is opaque; if src contains alpha, handling is determined by options.fAlphaOption (ignore or blend on black).
If options.fDownsample is set, it selects U/V subsampling when applicable (ignored if src is grayscale).
Caller must check the boolean return value for success/failure.

functions.name: SkJpegEncoder::Encode
functions.signature: SK_API bool SkJpegEncoder::Encode(SkWStream* dst, const SkYUVAPixmaps& src, const SkColorSpace* srcColorSpace, const SkJpegEncoder::Options& options)
functions.description: Encodes YUVA data described by SkYUVAPixmaps to the provided SkWStream as a JPEG. The source color space can be provided via srcColorSpace. Options control quality, metadata, and alpha handling (though JPEG is opaque). Returns true on success and false if the source is invalid or unsupported.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable SkWStream pointer that remains valid for the duration of the call.
src must describe a valid set of YUVA planes compatible with JPEG encoding; the subsampling used will follow src, not options.fDownsample.
srcColorSpace, if non-null, should describe the source color space; if null, a default/embedded behavior may be used (unspecified).
options.fQuality must be in the range [0, 100].
JPEG is opaque; if src implies alpha, handling is determined by options.fAlphaOption (e.g., blend on black) prior to encoding.
Caller must check the boolean return value for success/failure.

functions.name: SkJpegEncoder::Encode

functions.description: Encodes the pixels from the given SkPixmap to JPEG and returns the resulting bytes as an SkData object. Returns nullptr on failure.
requirements: src must reference initialized, readable pixel data in a supported color type/format.
options.fQuality must be in the range [0, 100].
JPEG is opaque; if src contains alpha, handling is determined by options.fAlphaOption (ignore or blend on black).
If options.fDownsample is set, it selects U/V subsampling when applicable (ignored if src is grayscale).
Caller must check for a non-null return to detect success.

functions.name: SkJpegEncoder::Make

functions.description: Creates a streaming JPEG encoder that will encode the given SkPixmap to the provided SkWStream with the specified options. Returns nullptr on invalid or unsupported source.
requirements: dst is unowned and must remain valid for the entire lifetime of the returned SkEncoder.
dst must be a valid, writable SkWStream pointer.
src must reference initialized, readable pixel data in a supported color type/format.

functions.name: SkJpegEncoder::Make
functions.signature: SK_API std::unique_ptr<SkEncoder> SkJpegEncoder::Make(SkWStream* dst, const SkYUVAPixmaps& src, const SkColorSpace* srcColorSpace, const SkJpegEncoder::Options& options)
functions.description: Creates a streaming JPEG encoder that will encode the given SkYUVAPixmaps to the provided SkWStream with the specified options. The source color space can be provided via srcColorSpace. Returns nullptr on invalid or unsupported source.
requirements: dst is unowned and must remain valid for the entire lifetime of the returned SkEncoder.
dst must be a valid, writable SkWStream pointer.
src must describe a valid set of YUVA planes compatible with JPEG encoding; the encoder will use the subsampling defined by src (ignoring options.fDownsample).
srcColorSpace, if non-null, should describe the source color space; if null, a default/embedded behavior may be used (unspecified).
options.fQuality must be in the range [0, 100].

Caller must check for a non-null return to ensure the encoder was created.

functions.name: SkPngEncoder::Encode
functions.signature: SK_API bool Encode(SkWStream* dst, const SkPixmap& src, const Options& options);
functions.description: Encodes the pixels in src to PNG format and writes the result to the output stream dst. The options parameter controls filtering, compression level, comments, HDR metadata, and optional gainmap embedding. Returns true on success and false if src is invalid/unsupported or encoding otherwise fails. Typical usage is for encoding a prepared SkPixmap to a file or memory-backed stream.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable SkWStream pointer and must not be null.
src must reference valid, readable pixel data; unsupported/invalid src will cause the function to return false.
options.fZLibLevel must be in the range [0, 9]; 0 disables zlib compression and produces much larger PNGs.
options.fFilterFlags selects PNG row filters; multiple flags allow libpng to choose per-row; using fewer filters can be faster.
If options.fGainmap is non-null, then options.fGainmapInfo must also be non-null; otherwise the gainmap will fail to encode.
If options.fComments is provided, entries must be key/value pairs where even indices are keywords and odd indices are corresponding text.
Caller must handle the boolean return value to detect encoding failure.

functions.name: SkPngEncoder::Encode
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkData> Encode(const SkPixmap& src, const Options& options);
functions.description: Encodes the pixels in src to PNG format and returns the encoded bytes as an SkData object. Returns nullptr on failure (e.g., invalid/unsupported src). Useful when the encoded result is needed in-memory rather than written to a stream.
requirements: src must reference valid, readable pixel data; unsupported/invalid src will cause the function to return nullptr.
options.fZLibLevel must be in the range [0, 9]; 0 disables zlib compression and produces much larger PNGs.
options.fFilterFlags selects PNG row filters; multiple flags allow libpng to choose per-row.
If options.fGainmap is non-null, then options.fGainmapInfo must also be non-null; otherwise the gainmap will fail to encode.
If options.fComments is provided, entries must be key/value pairs where even indices are keywords and odd indices are corresponding text.
Caller must check the return value for nullptr to detect encoding failure.

functions.name: SkPngEncoder::Encode
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkData> Encode(GrDirectContext* ctx, const SkImage* img, const Options& options);
functions.description: Encodes the given SkImage to PNG format and returns the encoded bytes as an SkData object. If img is texture-backed on a GPU, the corresponding GrDirectContext ctx must be provided so pixels can be read before encoding. For raster-backed images, ctx can be nullptr. Returns nullptr if pixels cannot be read or encoding fails.
requirements: img must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SkImage.
If img is texture-backed on a GPU context, the matching GrDirectContext* ctx must be provided and valid to allow reading pixels prior to encoding.
For raster-backed images, ctx may be nullptr.
options.fZLibLevel must be in the range [0, 9]; 0 disables zlib compression and produces much larger PNGs.
options.fFilterFlags selects PNG row filters; multiple flags allow libpng to choose per-row.
If options.fGainmap is non-null, then options.fGainmapInfo must also be non-null; otherwise the gainmap will fail to encode.
If options.fComments is provided, entries must be key/value pairs where even indices are keywords and odd indices are corresponding text.
Caller must check the return value for nullptr to detect encoding failure.

functions.name: SkPngEncoder::Make
functions.signature: SK_API std::unique_ptr<SkEncoder> Make(SkWStream* dst, const SkPixmap& src, const Options& options);
functions.description: Creates a PNG encoder instance that will encode the pixels in src incrementally to the stream dst, using the provided options. The returned SkEncoder enables incremental encoding workflows. Returns nullptr if src is invalid or unsupported. The dst stream is unowned and must remain valid for the lifetime of the encoder.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable SkWStream pointer, non-null, and must remain valid for the entire lifetime of the returned SkEncoder.
src must reference valid, readable pixel data; unsupported/invalid src will cause the function to return nullptr.
options.fZLibLevel must be in the range [0, 9]; 0 disables zlib compression and produces much larger PNGs.
options.fFilterFlags selects PNG row filters; multiple flags allow libpng to choose per-row.
If options.fGainmap is non-null, then options.fGainmapInfo must also be non-null; otherwise the gainmap will fail to encode.
If options.fComments is provided, entries must be key/value pairs where even indices are keywords and odd indices are corresponding text.
Caller must check for nullptr to detect creation/validation failure before using the returned encoder.

functions.name: SkWebpEncoder::Encode
functions.signature: SK_API bool SkWebpEncoder::Encode(SkWStream* dst, const SkPixmap& src, const SkWebpEncoder::Options& options)
functions.description: Encodes the pixels in src as a WebP image and writes the result to the dst stream. Options controls lossy vs lossless compression and quality/effort. Returns true on success and false if src is invalid/unsupported or encoding fails. Typical usage: prepare a valid SkPixmap and an output SkWStream (e.g., file or memory stream), set Options (compression and quality), and call Encode.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable SkWStream pointer (must not be null).
src must reference valid/initialized pixel data; unsupported or invalid pixel configurations will cause the function to return false.
options.fQuality must be in the range [0.0f, 100.0f].
options.fCompression selects lossy vs lossless; quality semantics follow libwebp (visual quality for lossy; encoding effort for lossless).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle false (encoding failed).

functions.name: SkWebpEncoder::EncodeAnimated
functions.signature: SK_API bool SkWebpEncoder::EncodeAnimated(SkWStream* dst, SkSpan<const SkEncoder::Frame> src, const SkWebpEncoder::Options& options)
functions.description: Encodes a sequence of frames as an animated WebP and writes the result to the dst stream. The first frame’s size defines the canvas; any subsequent frame whose size differs is an error. Options controls lossy vs lossless compression and quality/effort. Returns true on success, false on invalid/unsupported inputs or other failures.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable SkWStream pointer (must not be null).
The first frame’s dimensions establish the canvas; every other frame must match these dimensions or encoding fails.
Frames in src must be valid/initialized; invalid or unsupported frames will cause the function to return false.
options.fQuality must be in the range [0.0f, 100.0f].
options.fCompression selects lossy vs lossless; quality semantics follow libwebp (visual quality for lossy; encoding effort for lossless).
Caller must check the boolean return value and handle false (encoding failed).

functions.name: Op
functions.signature: std::optional<SkPath> SK_API Op(const SkPath& one, const SkPath& two, SkPathOp op)
functions.description: Performs a boolean operation between two paths and returns the resulting path, or {} on failure. Intended for path combination such as difference, intersection, union, XOR, and reverse-difference. The result is constructed from non-overlapping contours and curve order may be reduced.
requirements: 'one' and 'two' must be valid, initialized SkPath instances.
'op' must be a valid SkPathOp enumerator (kDifference_SkPathOp, kIntersect_SkPathOp, kUnion_SkPathOp, kXOR_SkPathOp, kReverseDifference_SkPathOp).
Callers must check the returned std::optional for a value before using the result; if it has no value, the operation failed.

functions.name: Simplify
functions.description: Simplifies a path to an area-equivalent form with non-overlapping contours, reducing curve order where possible. Returns the simplified path, or {} on failure.
requirements: 'path' must be a valid, initialized SkPath.
Callers must check the returned std::optional for a value before using the result; if it has no value, simplification failed.

functions.name: TightBounds
functions.signature: [[deprecated]] static inline bool TightBounds(const SkPath& path, SkRect* result)
functions.description: Computes the tight bounding rectangle of the path and writes it to 'result'. Returns true if the bounds are finite; otherwise returns false and does not modify 'result'. Deprecated in favor of SkPath::computeTightBounds().
requirements: 'path' must be a valid, initialized SkPath.
'result' must be a non-null pointer to a valid SkRect storage location.
On success, '*result' is assigned to the finite tight bounds of 'path'.
On failure (non-finite bounds), '*result' is not modified; callers must ignore any previous contents.

functions.name: AsWinding
functions.description: Converts a path to an area-equivalent path with winding fill type. Does not detect self-crossings within or across contours and may return a result that is not area-equivalent in such cases. Returns {} on failure.
requirements: 'path' must be a valid, initialized SkPath.
Callers must check the returned std::optional for a value before using the result; if it has no value, conversion failed.

functions.name: SkOpBuilder::add
functions.description: Adds a path and its operator to the builder. The first add combines an implicit empty path with the provided path using the given operator. Subsequent adds combine cumulatively.
requirements: 'path' must be a valid, initialized SkPath.
'_operator' must be a valid SkPathOp enumerator.
May be called multiple times before resolve().

functions.name: SkOpBuilder::resolve
functions.description: Computes the combined result of all added paths and operators, returning the resulting path or {} on failure. Resets the builder to its initial empty state after completion.
requirements: Builder must have been default-constructed or previously reset; it may have zero or more paths added via add().
Callers must check the returned std::optional for a value before using the result.
After this call, the builder is reset; to continue building, add() must be called again.

functions.name: SkOpBuilder::resolve
functions.description: Deprecated overload. Computes the combined result of all added paths and operators and writes it to 'result'. Returns true on success, false on failure. Resets the builder to its initial state on return.
requirements: 'result' must be a non-null pointer to a valid SkPath storage location.
May be called after zero or more add() calls.
On failure (return false), '*result' is not modified; callers should not read '*result' unless true is returned.
After this call—regardless of success—the builder is reset; to continue building, add() must be called again.

functions.name: SkFontConfigInterface::FontIdentity::writeToMemory
functions.description: Serializes this FontIdentity into a flat memory representation. If buffer is nullptr, it returns the number of bytes that would be written. When writing, the serialization pads to a multiple of 4 bytes.

If buffer is non-null, it must point to writable memory large enough to hold the entire serialized and padded data; the required size can be obtained by first calling with buffer == nullptr.

Serialization format details (endianness, field layout) are not documented; only that it can be round-tripped with readFromMemory.

functions.name: SkFontConfigInterface::FontIdentity::readFromMemory
functions.description: Deserializes this FontIdentity from a previously flattened memory buffer, updating this object and returning the number of bytes consumed from the buffer.

The buffer content is expected to be produced by writeToMemory; behavior with other data is unspecified.
Endianness and versioning details are unknown.

functions.name: SkFontConfigInterface::matchFamilyName
functions.signature: virtual bool SkFontConfigInterface::matchFamilyName(const char familyName[], SkFontStyle requested, FontIdentity* outFontIdentifier, SkString* outFamilyName, SkFontStyle* outStyle) = 0;

requirements: Available only when SK_BUILD_FOR_WIN is defined (Windows builds).

functions.name: SkTypeface_SetEnsureLOGFONTAccessibleProc

functions.name: SkSVGCanvas::Make
functions.signature: static std::unique_ptr<SkCanvas> Make(const SkRect& bounds, SkWStream* dst, SkSVGCanvas::Options opts)
functions.description: Creates an SkCanvas that records drawing operations as SVG and writes them to the provided SkWStream. The bounds define the initial SVG viewport (root viewBox). The stream is not owned by the canvas and must remain valid for the canvas lifetime. Output may be buffered; destroy the returned SkCanvas (let the std::unique_ptr go out of scope/reset) to ensure all SVG is flushed. Options allow setting SVG emission flags and an optional PNG encoder callback used when the SVG needs to embed/encode raster content.
requirements: dst must be a valid, non-null SkWStream pointer and must remain valid for the entire lifetime of the returned SkCanvas; ownership is not transferred.
The returned SkCanvas buffers some output; callers must destroy/reset the canvas when finished to guarantee complete SVG output is written.
bounds defines the SVG root viewBox; no additional constraints are documented.
If opts.pngEncoder is provided, it must be a valid function matching bool (*)(SkWStream* dst, const SkPixmap& src) and capable of encoding the provided SkPixmap to PNG into dst.
opts.flags is a bitmask of SkSVGCanvas::Flags values; if no flags are desired, use 0 (i.e., static_cast<Flags>(0x00)).

functions.name: SkSVGCanvas::Make
functions.signature: static std::unique_ptr<SkCanvas> Make(const SkRect& bounds, SkWStream* dst, uint32_t flags = 0)
functions.description: Legacy factory (available only when SK_DISABLE_LEGACY_SVG_FACTORIES is not defined) that creates an SkCanvas which records drawing operations as SVG and writes them to the provided SkWStream. The bounds define the initial SVG viewport (root viewBox). The stream is not owned by the canvas and must remain valid for the canvas lifetime. Output may be buffered; destroy the returned SkCanvas to ensure all SVG is flushed. The flags parameter configures SVG emission behavior and corresponds to SkSVGCanvas::Flags bit values.
requirements: This overload is available only if !defined(SK_DISABLE_LEGACY_SVG_FACTORIES) at compile time.
dst must be a valid, non-null SkWStream pointer and must remain valid for the entire lifetime of the returned SkCanvas; ownership is not transferred.
The returned SkCanvas buffers some output; callers must destroy/reset the canvas when finished to guarantee complete SVG output is written.
bounds defines the SVG root viewBox; no additional constraints are documented.
flags should be a bitmask composed of SkSVGCanvas::Flags values (e.g., kConvertTextToPaths_Flag, kNoPrettyXML_Flag, kRelativePathEncoding_Flag); use 0 for no flags.

functions.name: SkSL::DebugTrace::dump
functions.description: Writes a human-readable dump of this debug trace to the provided SkWStream. This is a const, pure-virtual interface method; a concrete subclass of SkSL::DebugTrace must implement it. Typical usage is to pass a writable SkWStream (e.g., file or memory stream) and invoke dump to serialize the trace for diagnostics or logging. Return type is void; any error reporting (if any) is implementation-defined or via the stream.
requirements: Must be called on an instance of a concrete subclass of SkSL::DebugTrace (method is pure virtual).
Parameter o should be a valid, writable SkWStream pointer; it should not be null. (inferred from parameter name/type)
No status is returned; callers should not expect a success/failure code and should handle any stream-side errors via the SkWStream implementation. (inferred)

functions.name: skgpu::ShaderErrorHandler::compileError

functions.description: Reports a shader compilation error. This legacy two-parameter overload is kept for backward compatibility. Typical implementations log or surface the provided shader source and compiler error text. The default implementation does nothing.
requirements: The ShaderErrorHandler instance must be valid and alive for the duration of the call.
Parameter shader is expected to point to the shader source text as a readable, null-terminated C string; lifetime must cover the call (exact encoding/format unspecified).
Parameter errors is expected to point to the compiler’s error/output text as a readable, null-terminated C string; lifetime must cover the call (exact format unspecified).

requirements: backendTexture must remain valid and unchanged until Skia calls textureReleaseProc with releaseContext.
context must be a valid GrRecordingContext compatible with backendTexture.
alphaType must describe the alpha semantics of the compressed data (e.g., typically kOpaque_SkAlphaType for opaque compressed formats).
colorSpace should reflect the content as seen after sampling (SRGB formats usually pair with linear color space; linear formats should include a transfer function).
origin must match the texture’s actual origin orientation.
A non-null result requires the GPU backend to recognize/support the compressed format.
textureReleaseProc and releaseContext are optional; if provided, Skia will call them when it no longer needs the texture (or on failure per backend behavior noted for DDL in similar APIs).

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromCompressedTextureData
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::TextureFromCompressedTextureData(GrDirectContext* direct, sk_sp<SkData> data, int width, int height, SkTextureCompressionType type, skgpu::Mipmapped mipmapped = skgpu::Mipmapped::kNo, GrProtected isProtected = GrProtected::kNo);
functions.description: Creates a GPU-backed SkImage from compressed image data. If the GPU supports the specified compression type, the compressed data will be used directly; otherwise, the data is decompressed and uploaded to create a GPU-backed image. Returns nullptr on failure.
requirements: direct must be a valid GrDirectContext.
data must contain compressed image data encoded with the specified compression type.
width and height describe the full image dimensions and must correspond to the data; unsupported sizes or mismatches may cause failure.
mipmapped indicates whether the data includes all mip levels; if kYes, the data must contain valid mipmap data for the format.
isProtected indicates whether DRM protection is required for the contents (platform/driver dependent).
Supported compression formats can be queried via GrRecordingContext::compressedBackendFormat; unsupported formats will trigger a CPU decompression fallback or failure.

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromImage
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::TextureFromImage(GrDirectContext*, const SkImage*, skgpu::Mipmapped = skgpu::Mipmapped::kNo, skgpu::Budgeted = skgpu::Budgeted::kYes);
functions.description: Ensures an SkImage is backed by a GPU texture associated with the given direct context, optionally allocating mipmaps and controlling budgeting. If the image is already texture-backed with a compatible context and mipmap state, the original image is returned. Returns nullptr if the context is null or the image was created with another GrDirectContext.
requirements: The GrDirectContext parameter must not be nullptr; otherwise nullptr is returned.
The SkImage pointer must be non-null and valid.
If the SkImage is already texture-backed, the provided GrDirectContext must match the image’s context; otherwise nullptr is returned.
If requested mipmapping is incompatible with the existing texture, Skia may create a new texture; skgpu::Budgeted applies only when a new texture is created (ignored otherwise).
The GPU may ignore mipmap requests if MIP maps are not supported.

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromImage
functions.signature: inline sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::TextureFromImage(GrDirectContext* ctx, const sk_sp<const SkImage>& img, skgpu::Mipmapped m = skgpu::Mipmapped::kNo, skgpu::Budgeted b = skgpu::Budgeted::kYes);
functions.description: Inline convenience overload that forwards to TextureFromImage(ctx, img.get(), ...). See the pointer overload for behavior and requirements.
requirements: ctx must not be nullptr for a successful result.
img must hold a non-null SkImage.
All requirements from SkImages::TextureFromImage(GrDirectContext*, const SkImage*, ...) apply.

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromYUVAPixmaps
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::TextureFromYUVAPixmaps(GrRecordingContext* context, const SkYUVAPixmaps& pixmaps, skgpu::Mipmapped buildMips, bool limitToMaxTextureSize, sk_sp<SkColorSpace> imageColorSpace);
functions.description: Creates a GPU-backed SkImage from planar YUVA data provided as SkYUVAPixmaps, converting to RGB according to the pixmaps’ SkYUVAInfo. Each plane is uploaded as a texture on the provided recording context. The imageColorSpace describes the RGB space of the resulting image. Returns nullptr on failure (e.g., if context is nullptr).
requirements: context must be a valid GrRecordingContext; this API currently only works with the GPU backend and fails if context is nullptr.
pixmaps must contain planes with a supported SkYUVAInfo describing the YUV->RGB transform.
buildMips controls mipmap allocation for internal YUVA textures and is ignored if the context does not support mip maps.
If limitToMaxTextureSize is true, Skia may downscale to fit GPU limits; otherwise creation may fail for oversized content.
imageColorSpace may be nullptr; if provided, it specifies the color space of the RGB result.
SkYUVAPixmaps need not remain valid after this call returns.

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromYUVAPixmaps
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::TextureFromYUVAPixmaps(GrRecordingContext* context, const SkYUVAPixmaps& pixmaps, skgpu::Mipmapped buildMips = skgpu::Mipmapped::kNo, bool limitToMaxTextureSize = false);
functions.description: Overload of TextureFromYUVAPixmaps that omits an explicit image color space. The resulting image’s RGB color space is implementation-defined or inferred from conversion defaults. Returns nullptr on failure.
requirements: context must be a valid GrRecordingContext (fails if nullptr).
pixmaps must include supported planes and SkYUVAInfo for YUV->RGB conversion.
buildMips is honored if mip maps are supported by the context; otherwise ignored.
limitToMaxTextureSize limits the size to GPU maximum if true.
SkYUVAPixmaps need not remain valid after return.

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromYUVATextures
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::TextureFromYUVATextures(GrRecordingContext* context, const GrYUVABackendTextures& yuvaTextures, sk_sp<SkColorSpace> imageColorSpace, TextureReleaseProc textureReleaseProc = nullptr, ReleaseContext releaseContext = nullptr);
functions.description: Creates a GPU-backed SkImage from existing YUVA backend textures. The textures must remain valid for the lifetime of the image. An optional release proc is called (with releaseContext) when Skia no longer needs the textures; on failure, the release proc is also called before returning. The imageColorSpace describes the RGB color space after YUV->RGB conversion.
requirements: context must be a valid GrRecordingContext.
yuvaTextures must identify a set of valid backend textures and the YUVA-to-RGBA transformation; these textures must stay valid for the lifetime of the created image.
imageColorSpace may be nullptr; if provided, it specifies the color space of the resulting RGB image.
If textureReleaseProc is provided, Skia will call it with releaseContext when the textures can be released, and it will also be called before return on failure.

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromYUVATextures
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::TextureFromYUVATextures(GrRecordingContext* context, const GrYUVABackendTextures& yuvaTextures);
functions.description: Overload of TextureFromYUVATextures that omits color space and release proc. The provided YUVA textures must remain valid for the image’s lifetime. Returns nullptr on failure.
requirements: context must be a valid GrRecordingContext.
yuvaTextures must refer to valid backend textures and describe the YUVA-to-RGBA transformation.
The provided textures must remain valid for the lifetime of the SkImage.

functions.name: SkImages::GetBackendTextureFromImage
functions.signature: SK_API bool SkImages::GetBackendTextureFromImage(const SkImage* img, GrBackendTexture* outTexture, bool flushPendingGrContextIO, GrSurfaceOrigin* origin = nullptr);
functions.description: Retrieves the underlying Ganesh backend texture of a texture-backed SkImage. If the image does not have a Ganesh backend texture, returns false and does not modify outTexture. Optionally flushes pending GPU I/O and returns the texture’s origin.
requirements: img must be a valid SkImage pointer; if not texture-backed by Ganesh, the function returns false.
outTexture, if non-null, will be set to the image’s underlying texture on success; the caller must provide storage.
If flushPendingGrContextIO is true, Skia will complete deferred GPU I/O before retrieval.
origin, if non-null, will be set to the image’s origin orientation on success.

functions.name: SkImages::GetBackendTextureFromImage
functions.signature: inline bool SkImages::GetBackendTextureFromImage(const sk_sp<const SkImage>& img, GrBackendTexture* outTexture, bool flushPendingGrContextIO, GrSurfaceOrigin* origin = nullptr);
functions.description: Inline convenience overload that forwards to GetBackendTextureFromImage(img.get(), ...). Retrieves the backend texture if the image is a Ganesh texture-backed image; otherwise returns false.
requirements: img must hold a non-null SkImage for a successful retrieval.
All requirements from the const SkImage* overload apply.

functions.name: SkImages::GetBackendTextureFromImage
functions.signature: inline bool SkImages::GetBackendTextureFromImage(GrDirectContext* context, sk_sp<SkImage> image, GrBackendTexture* backendTexture, BackendTextureReleaseProc* backendTextureReleaseProc);
functions.description: Legacy inline alias for MakeBackendTextureFromImage that forwards to it. Produces a backend texture from an SkImage and a release proc to manage its lifetime.
requirements: Same as SkImages::MakeBackendTextureFromImage: context must be valid; image must be valid; backendTexture and backendTextureReleaseProc must be non-null storage for outputs.

functions.name: SkImages::MakeBackendTextureFromImage
functions.signature: SK_API bool SkImages::MakeBackendTextureFromImage(GrDirectContext* context, sk_sp<SkImage> image, GrBackendTexture* backendTexture, BackendTextureReleaseProc* backendTextureReleaseProc);
functions.description: Extracts or creates a GPU backend texture from an SkImage. If the image is not GPU-backed, its raster data is uploaded as a texture. If this call holds the only reference to the image, its existing texture may be moved out; otherwise a copy is made. On success, backendTexture is set and a release proc is provided for lifetime management.
requirements: context must be a valid GrDirectContext.
image may be CPU- or GPU-backed; it must be a valid SkImage smart pointer.
backendTexture must be a non-null pointer to storage that will receive the resulting backend texture on success.
backendTextureReleaseProc must be a non-null pointer; on success, it will be set to a callable that Skia will invoke when the texture can be released.
Returns false if the image cannot be uploaded or a texture cannot be produced.

functions.name: SkImages::SubsetTextureFrom
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::SubsetTextureFrom(GrDirectContext* context, const SkImage* img, const SkIRect& subset);
functions.description: Returns a texture-backed SkImage containing a subset of the source image, uploaded to the provided direct context. Returns nullptr if the subset is empty, out of bounds, pixels cannot be read/copied, or if the source image is texture-backed with a different context.
requirements: context must be a non-null GrDirectContext to which the subset will be uploaded.
img must be a valid SkImage pointer.
subset must be non-empty and fully contained within the bounds of img.
If img is texture-backed, its context must match the provided context.
Operation may fail if pixels cannot be read or copied (returns nullptr).

functions.name: SkImages::MakeWithFilter
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::MakeWithFilter(GrRecordingContext* context, sk_sp<SkImage> src, const SkImageFilter* filter, const SkIRect& subset, const SkIRect& clipBounds, SkIRect* outSubset, SkIPoint* offset);
functions.description: Applies an SkImageFilter to a region of a source image on the GPU, potentially changing color, position, and size. The subset describes the portion of src processed; clipBounds specify expected bounds of the filtered result. On success, returns a filtered image along with the actual resulting bounds (outSubset) and an offset to align subsequent frames. Returns nullptr if creation fails or the provided recording context doesn’t match the image’s GPU context.
requirements: context should be the GrRecordingContext associated with the GPU work; if it doesn’t match the image’s context, the call fails.
src must be a valid SkImage smart pointer.
filter specifies how the image is processed; may affect size, position, and color.
subset is the region of src to process; must be valid for src.
clipBounds are expected bounds of the filtered result.
outSubset must be a non-null pointer to receive the actual bounds of the returned image on success; undefined if the function returns nullptr.
offset must be a non-null pointer to receive the translation of the returned image on success; undefined if the function returns nullptr.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::InsertStatus::operator skgpu::graphite::InsertStatus::V
functions.description: Implicit conversion operator that returns the underlying InsertStatus::V enum value stored by this InsertStatus wrapper. Intended to ease migration where code expects the raw enum value.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::InsertStatus::operator bool
functions.description: Implicit conversion to bool. Returns true only when the status is kSuccess; returns false for any error status. Provided to ease migration from older APIs that returned bool.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::InsertFinishInfo::InsertFinishInfo
functions.description: Default constructor for InsertFinishInfo. Initializes all fields to defaults (null callbacks/context and GpuStatsFlags::kNone). Used when the caller intends to set fields manually.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::InsertFinishInfo::InsertFinishInfo
functions.description: Constructor that sets a completion callback without GPU stats. The provided proc will be invoked when a Recording is submitted and finishes on the GPU or fails to submit.
requirements: proc, if provided, must point to a valid callable function and remain valid until the callback is invoked.
context must remain valid and usable by the callback until the callback is invoked.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::InsertFinishInfo::InsertFinishInfo
functions.description: Constructor that sets a completion callback with GPU stats. The provided proc will be invoked when a Recording is submitted and finishes on the GPU or fails to submit. When CallbackResult is kSuccess, only the stats requested via GpuStatsFlags will be valid.
requirements: proc, if provided, must point to a valid callable function and remain valid until the callback is invoked.
context must remain valid and usable by the callback until the callback is invoked.
Only requested stats (via GpuStatsFlags) are valid when CallbackResult is kSuccess.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::ToSampleCount
functions.description: Converts an integer to a strictly typed SampleCount, rounding down to the nearest valid value among {1,2,4,8,16}. Useful for sanitizing arbitrary sample counts to the supported set.
requirements: sampleCount may be any uint32_t; the return value is clamped to the largest supported value not exceeding sampleCount (or 1 if sampleCount < 2).

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::SampleCount::operator==
functions.description: Compares two SampleCount values for equality.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::SampleCount::operator<
functions.description: Strict-weak ordering comparison of two SampleCount values.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::SampleCount::operator<=
functions.description: Less-than-or-equal comparison of two SampleCount values.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::SampleCount::operator>
functions.description: Greater-than comparison of two SampleCount values.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::SampleCount::operator>=
functions.description: Greater-than-or-equal comparison of two SampleCount values.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::SampleCount::operator skgpu::graphite::SampleCount::V
functions.description: Explicit conversion operator that returns the underlying SampleCount::V enumerator corresponding to this SampleCount.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::SampleCount::operator unsigned int
functions.signature: explicit constexpr skgpu::graphite::SampleCount::operator unsigned int() const
functions.description: Explicit conversion operator that returns this SampleCount as an unsigned int (1, 2, 4, 8, or 16).

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::SampleCount::operator=
functions.description: Assignment from an 8-bit integer. Wraps the value as a SampleCount, asserting in debug builds if the value is not one of {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::~Context
functions.description: Destructor for a Graphite Context. Cleans up underlying GPU/CPU resources owned by the Context instance.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::backend
functions.description: Returns the backend API used by this Context (e.g., Metal, Vulkan, Dawn). Useful for feature checks or conditional behavior.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::makeRecorder
functions.description: Creates a new Recorder tied to this Context for recording drawing and resource operations that can be later submitted.
requirements: > The Context must be valid (not destroyed/abandoned) when creating the Recorder.
> The returned Recorder is owned by the caller and must be destroyed or submitted according to usage; do not use after the Context is destroyed.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::makeCPURecorder
functions.description: Creates a CPU-side recorder for Graphite CPU backend operations. Intended for recording work without a GPU.
requirements: > The Context must be valid when creating the CPU Recorder.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::makePrecompileContext
functions.description: Creates a helper object that can be moved to a different thread and used for precompiling shaders/pipelines.
requirements: > The PrecompileContext may be used on a different thread; ensure thread-safety as implied by the API.
> The Context must remain valid for the duration of any operations that depend on it.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::insertRecording
functions.description: Inserts a previously recorded set of GPU tasks into this Context's submission queue.
requirements: > The InsertRecordingInfo must have been produced for this Context (or a compatible one) and contain valid recordings.
> Do not reuse invalidated or already-inserted recordings unless explicitly allowed by InsertRecordingInfo/InsertStatus semantics (details not specified here).

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::submit
functions.description: Submits queued work from this Context to the GPU (or backend). May also drive completion of asynchronous operations.
requirements: > The Context must not be lost. Submission behavior and error reporting are backend dependent.
> If callers rely on asynchronous read callbacks, they may need to call submit with appropriate sync flags (e.g., SyncToCpu::kYes, referenced in comments elsewhere) to trigger callbacks.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::hasUnfinishedGpuWork
functions.description: Returns true if previously submitted GPU work has not yet finished.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::asyncRescaleAndReadPixels
functions.description: Asynchronously reads pixel data from a Graphite-backed SkImage, optionally rescales and color converts it to match dstImageInfo, then invokes callback with an AsyncReadResult containing one plane of pixel data (or nullptr on failure).
requirements: > src must be a Graphite-backed SkImage created for this Context.
> srcRect must be fully contained within the image bounds; otherwise the call fails.
> dstImageInfo specifies the requested size, color type, alpha type, and color space of the result.
> rescaleGamma selects whether rescaling occurs in the image’s gamma or after conversion to linear gamma.
> rescaleMode selects the resampling technique.
> callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be called when data is ready (or on failure with nullptr).
> The AsyncReadResult’s data remains valid only for the lifetime of the AsyncReadResult; it is immediately invalidated if the Context is abandoned or destroyed.
> To ensure callbacks are triggered, callers may need to call Context::submit with appropriate sync (e.g., SyncToCpu::kYes).

> dstImageInfo specifies the requested size, color type, alpha type, and color space of the result.

functions.signature:
void skgpu::graphite::Context::asyncRescaleAndReadPixelsYUV420(const SkImage* src,
                                         SkYUVColorSpace yuvColorSpace,
                                         sk_sp<SkColorSpace> dstColorSpace,
                                         const SkIRect& srcRect,
                                         const SkISize& dstSize,
                                         SkImage::RescaleGamma rescaleGamma,
                                         SkImage::RescaleMode rescaleMode,
                                         SkImage::ReadPixelsCallback callback,
                                         SkImage::ReadPixelsContext context);
functions.description: Asynchronously reads from a Graphite-backed SkImage, rescales to dstSize, converts to dstColorSpace, then converts to YUV420. Invokes callback with an AsyncReadResult containing three planes (Y, U, V) with U and V at half resolution. On failure, callback is invoked with nullptr.
requirements: > src must be a Graphite-backed SkImage created for this Context.
> srcRect must be fully contained within the image bounds; otherwise the call fails.
> dstSize width and height must be even; currently this fails if they are not even.
> yuvColorSpace controls the RGB→YUV transform, applied after rescaling and conversion to dstColorSpace.
> rescaleGamma selects whether rescaling occurs in the image’s gamma or after conversion to linear gamma.
> rescaleMode controls the rescaling sampling technique.
> callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with 3-plane data or nullptr on failure.
> The AsyncReadResult’s data remains valid only for its lifetime and is immediately invalidated if the Context is abandoned or destroyed.
> To ensure callbacks are triggered, callers may need to call Context::submit with appropriate sync (e.g., SyncToCpu::kYes).
