functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::checkAsyncWorkCompletion
functions.description: Polls for completion of asynchronous work and invokes any related callbacks whose work has finished.
requirements: > Call periodically to drive callback invocation if not otherwise triggered by submissions.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::deleteBackendTexture
functions.description: Deletes/releases the backend object wrapped by the given BackendTexture, if valid and created by a Recorder from this Context; resets the BackendTexture to an invalid state.
requirements: > The BackendTexture must have been created by Recorder::createBackendTexture using a Recorder from this Context.
> If the BackendTexture is invalid or its backend API does not match this Context, the call is a no-op.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::freeGpuResources
functions.description: Frees GPU resources created and held by this Context to reduce memory pressure. Resources still in active use will not be deleted.
requirements: > To ensure all resources can be freed, first submit and wait for outstanding work so that no resources are in use.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::performDeferredCleanup
functions.description: Purges GPU resources that have not been used recently (within msNotUsed) or are otherwise marked for deletion, regardless of budget status.
requirements: > msNotUsed specifies the age threshold; resources unused for at least this duration may be purged.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::currentBudgetedBytes
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes of the Context's GPU memory cache budget that are currently in use.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::currentPurgeableBytes
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes in the resource cache that are currently purgeable.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::maxBudgetedBytes
functions.description: Returns the GPU memory cache budget size in bytes for this Context.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::setMaxBudgetedBytes
functions.description: Sets the GPU memory cache budget size in bytes. The cache may immediately evict resources to comply if the current usage exceeds the new budget.
requirements: > bytes specifies the new budget; if smaller than current usage, the cache will attempt to free resources to get under the new budget.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::dumpMemoryStatistics
functions.description: Enumerates cached GPU resources and dumps their memory usage to the provided SkTraceMemoryDump.
requirements: > traceMemoryDump must be a valid pointer for the duration of the call.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::isDeviceLost
functions.description: Returns true if the backend-specific context is in an unrecoverable, lost state (e.g., device lost errors).

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::maxTextureSize

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::supportsProtectedContent
functions.description: Returns true if the backend supports protected content.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Context::supportedGpuStats
functions.description: Returns the supported GPU statistics types for this Context.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recorder::createBackendTexture
functions.description: Creates a new backend GPU texture with the given dimensions and TextureInfo. Returns an invalid BackendTexture if the TextureInfo is invalid or unsupported. Valid textures must be explicitly deleted by the client via Recorder::deleteBackendTexture or Context::deleteBackendTexture.
requirements: Caller must check the returned BackendTexture for validity (e.g., isValid()) before use.
On success, caller must delete the texture by calling Recorder::deleteBackendTexture or Context::deleteBackendTexture when finished.
deleteBackendTexture may be called on this Recorder, the creating Context, or another Recorder from the same Context.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recorder::updateBackendTexture
functions.signature: bool skgpu::graphite::Recorder::updateBackendTexture(const skgpu::graphite::BackendTexture& texture, const SkPixmap srcData[], int numLevels, GpuFinishedProc finishedProc = nullptr, GpuFinishedContext finishedContext = nullptr);
functions.description: Asynchronously uploads pixmap data into a compatible backend texture (including all mip levels if the texture is mipmapped). On success, the caller must insert the resulting Recording into a Context and submit for the upload to execute. A completion callback can be provided to know when the texture is safe to destroy.
requirements: The BackendTexture must be compatible with the base pixmap’s SkColorType (backend format compatibility).

If the BackendTexture is mipmapped, data for all mip levels must be provided; all pixmaps’ color types must match; each mip level must have correct dimensions (see SkMipmap::ComputeLevelSize and ComputeLevelCount).
Pixmap alpha types and color spaces are ignored.
After calling this, the caller must insert a Recording into the Context and call submit to perform the upload.
Source data (pixmaps) may be freed once the call returns.
The BackendTexture must not be destroyed until the provided GpuFinishedProc is called by Skia indicating it is safe.
On Vulkan backends, after a successful update the VkImage layout will be VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recorder::updateCompressedBackendTexture
functions.signature: bool skgpu::graphite::Recorder::updateCompressedBackendTexture(const skgpu::graphite::BackendTexture& texture, const void* data, size_t dataSize, GpuFinishedProc finishedProc = nullptr, GpuFinishedContext finishedContext = nullptr);
functions.description: Asynchronously uploads compressed texture data into a compatible backend texture (including all mip levels if mipmapped). On success, the caller must insert the resulting Recording into a Context and submit for the upload to execute. A completion callback can be provided to know when the texture is safe to destroy.
requirements: If the BackendTexture is mipmapped, data for all mip levels must be provided; mip level sizes must be correct (see SkMipMap::ComputeLevelSize and ComputeLevelCount).
After calling this, the caller must insert a Recording into the Context and call submit to perform the upload.
The BackendTexture must not be destroyed until the provided GpuFinishedProc is called by Skia indicating it is safe.
On Vulkan backends, after a successful update the VkImage layout will be VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recorder::deleteBackendTexture
functions.description: Deletes/releases the backend object wrapped by the given BackendTexture if it was created by a Recorder associated with the same Context and matches the Recorder’s BackendApi. Resets the BackendTexture to an invalid state.
requirements: Only call for BackendTexture objects created via Recorder::createBackendTexture on a Recorder associated with the same Context.
If the BackendTexture is invalid or its BackendApi does not match this Recorder, the call is a no-op.
After deletion, the BackendTexture becomes invalid and must not be used again.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recorder::addFinishInfo
functions.description: Registers a callback/proc to be transferred to the Recording on snap, attached to the CommandBuffer when the Recording is added, and invoked upon GPU submission completion. If the Recorder or Recording is destroyed before it’s attached, the proc is called with Failure.
requirements: The proc is moved to the Recording upon snap and called when the associated CommandBuffer finishes.
If the Recorder or Recording is deleted before the proc is attached to a CommandBuffer, it will be invoked with result Failure.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recorder::makeDeferredCanvas
functions.signature: SkCanvas* skgpu::graphite::Recorder::makeDeferredCanvas(const SkImageInfo& imageInfo, const skgpu::graphite::TextureInfo& textureInfo);
functions.description: Creates a canvas that records into a proxy surface to be instantiated during replay. Only one deferred canvas can be created per Recording; the returned canvas is valid only until the next snap.
requirements: May be called at most once per Recording; subsequent calls before a snap will return null.
The returned SkCanvas remains valid only until the next Recording is snapped, at which time it is deleted.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recorder::freeGpuResources
functions.description: Frees GPU resources created and held by the Recorder to reduce memory pressure. Resources still in use by submitted GPU work will not be deleted.
requirements: To ensure all resources can be freed, the caller should first submit and wait for completion of any outstanding GPU work (otherwise in-use resources are retained).

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recorder::performDeferredCleanup
functions.description: Purges Recorder-owned GPU resources that have not been used for the specified duration or are otherwise marked for deletion, independent of current budget pressure.
requirements: msNotUsed specifies the minimum age (in milliseconds) of unused resources to purge.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recorder::currentBudgetedBytes
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes of the Recorder’s GPU memory cache budget that are currently in use.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recorder::currentPurgeableBytes

functions.description: Sets the Recorder’s GPU memory cache budget in bytes. If the new budget is less than current usage, the cache will attempt to free resources to become budget compliant.

functions.description: Enumerates all cached GPU resources owned by the Recorder and dumps their memory usage to the provided trace dumper interface.

functions.description: Destructor for Recording. Cleans up any resources held by the Recording, including task lists, extra resource refs, and any lazy proxy data. Typical usage is automatic destruction when a Recording goes out of scope or is explicitly deleted.
requirements: The Recording object must not be used after the destructor runs.
No specific preconditions are documented; callers should ensure no concurrent use from other threads during destruction (thread-safety not documented).

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recording::priv
functions.description: Returns a RecordingPriv helper that provides privileged/internal accessors or operations for a Recording. Intended for internal or advanced usage patterns rather than general client use.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recording::LazyProxyData::LazyProxyData
functions.signature: skgpu::graphite::Recording::LazyProxyData::LazyProxyData(const skgpu::graphite::Caps* caps, SkISize dimensions, const skgpu::graphite::TextureInfo& info);
functions.description: Constructs a LazyProxyData to support replaying a Recording to a target provided at replay time. Initializes state required to lazily instantiate a TextureProxy with the provided capabilities, dimensions, and texture parameters.
requirements: caps must point to a valid skgpu::graphite::Caps instance (not null).
dimensions must describe the intended texture size; exact constraints are not documented here.
info must reference a valid TextureInfo describing the desired texture properties.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recording::LazyProxyData::~LazyProxyData
functions.description: Destructor for LazyProxyData. Releases any held references to the target Texture and TextureProxy.
requirements: The LazyProxyData instance must not be used after destruction.
No specific preconditions are documented.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recording::LazyProxyData::lazyProxy
functions.description: Returns a raw, non-owning pointer to the lazily created TextureProxy associated with this LazyProxyData, if any. Useful for accessing the proxy without modifying ownership.
requirements: The returned pointer is owned by LazyProxyData; do not retain it beyond the lifetime of the LazyProxyData.
May return null if the proxy has not been created/instantiated; callers must handle a null return.

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recording::LazyProxyData::refLazyProxy
functions.description: Returns a reference-counted smart pointer (sk_sp) to the TextureProxy managed by this LazyProxyData, increasing its ref-count. Use this to safely hold the proxy beyond the function call.
requirements: Callers must handle the case where the returned sk_sp is null if the proxy is not yet created.
The caller assumes a shared reference and must release it when done (by letting sk_sp go out of scope).

functions.name: skgpu::graphite::Recording::LazyProxyData::lazyInstantiate
functions.description: Attempts to lazily instantiate the TextureProxy using the provided ResourceProvider and target Texture at replay time. Returns true on success, false on failure. Enables recordings to bind to a concrete texture provided later.
requirements: resourceProvider must be a valid, non-null pointer to a ResourceProvider.
target must be a valid sk_sp<skgpu::graphite::Texture> representing the concrete texture to back the proxy; may be null only if implementation explicitly allows it (not documented).
Callers must check the boolean return value to detect failure and avoid using the proxy on failure.

functions.name: SkSurfaces::AsImage
functions.description: Creates an SkImage that directly references the same GPU backing store as the provided Graphite SkSurface (no copy-on-write). Intended for Graphite-only usage when the caller wants an image view of the current surface content. The returned image shares the surface’s backing resource and thus reflects subsequent mutations unless the client carefully controls usage. Returns null if the surface’s backing GPU buffer is not textureable. The image’s mipmapping matches that of the source surface.
requirements: Only available/valid for Graphite SkSurface usage.
The surface’s backing GPU buffer must be textureable; otherwise this returns null and no copy is attempted.
Caller must ensure the image contents are in the desired state when consumed by the GPU since the surface and image share the same backing resource (no implicit copy-on-write).
The resource backing the surface will not change during the lifetime of the returned image (behavioral note from API).

functions.name: SkSurfaces::AsImageCopy
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkSurfaces::AsImageCopy(sk_sp<const SkSurface> surface, const SkIRect* subset = nullptr, skgpu::Mipmapped mipmapped = skgpu::Mipmapped::kNo);
functions.description: Creates a copy of the provided Graphite SkSurface’s contents as a new SkImage. Allows optionally specifying a subset rectangle and requesting mipmaps to be generated as part of the copy. Because this makes a copy, the returned image does not share the surface’s backing resource.
requirements: Only available/valid for Graphite SkSurface usage.
subset may be null to copy the full surface; when provided, it specifies a rectangular subset (exact bounds/validation behavior not documented here).
mipmapped controls whether the copied image includes mipmaps (kYes) or not (kNo).
The resource backing the original surface does not change due to this call (copy semantics).
Return value may be null if creation/copy fails (not explicitly documented; success is conditional on implementation).

functions.name: SkSurfaces::RenderTarget
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkSurface> SkSurfaces::RenderTarget(skgpu::graphite::Recorder* recorder, const SkImageInfo& imageInfo, skgpu::Mipmapped mipmapped = skgpu::Mipmapped::kNo, const SkSurfaceProps* surfaceProps = nullptr, std::string_view label = {});
functions.description: Creates a GPU render-target SkSurface using the provided Graphite Recorder and image description. While a client holds a ref to the returned SkSurface, its backing GPU object does not count against the cache budget; after the surface is freed, the backing object may become a scratch resource and then count against the budget. Optional surface properties and a debug label can be supplied.
requirements: recorder must be a valid skgpu::graphite::Recorder for the target GPU/context (Graphite).
imageInfo specifies the color type, dimensions, and color space for the surface; it must describe a configuration supported by the recorder (exact constraints not documented here).
mipmapped selects whether the render target should be created with mipmaps (kYes) or not (kNo).
surfaceProps may be null to use defaults.
label is optional and may be empty.

functions.name: SkSurfaces::WrapBackendTexture
functions.signature: SK_API sk_sp<SkSurface> SkSurfaces::WrapBackendTexture(skgpu::graphite::Recorder* recorder, const skgpu::graphite::BackendTexture& backendTexture, SkColorType colorType, sk_sp<SkColorSpace> colorSpace, const SkSurfaceProps* props, SkSurfaces::TextureReleaseProc releaseProc = nullptr, SkSurfaces::ReleaseContext releaseContext = nullptr, std::string_view label = {});
functions.description: Wraps an existing GPU-backed texture as an SkSurface for Graphite. Returns an SkSurface if all parameters are valid and the recorder supports the texture. Texture lifetime requirements depend on the backend: for Metal, Skia retains the underlying MTLTexture so the caller may drop its reference after this call; other backends may require the texture to remain valid for the lifetime of the SkSurface. The backend texture’s format must be compatible with the specified color space and recorder capabilities (e.g., sRGB requires recorder sRGB support and a non-null colorSpace). Width and height must not exceed recorder capabilities. An optional release proc/context can be provided for resource release callbacks, and optional surface props and label may be supplied.
requirements: recorder must be a valid skgpu::graphite::Recorder whose capabilities support the provided backend texture.
backendTexture must refer to a valid GPU texture object usable by the recorder; its width/height must not exceed the recorder’s capabilities.
The texture’s format must agree with colorSpace and the recorder; e.g., sRGB textures require recorder sRGB support and a present colorSpace.
colorType must be compatible with backendTexture and colorSpace for the intended usage (exact mappings not documented here).
colorSpace may be required depending on texture format (e.g., sRGB example); passing null when required will cause failure.
props may be null to use defaults.
releaseProc and releaseContext are optional; their exact call timing/threading semantics are not documented here.

Backend lifetime requirements are backend-API dependent: for Metal, Skia retains the MTLTexture so the caller can release it after this call; for other APIs, the caller may need to ensure the texture remains valid for the lifetime of the returned SkSurface.
label is optional and may be empty.

functions.name: SkImages::WrapTexture
functions.signature:
SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::WrapTexture(skgpu::graphite::Recorder* recorder,
                                  const skgpu::graphite::BackendTexture& backendTexture,
                                  SkColorType colorType,
                                  SkAlphaType alphaType,
                                  sk_sp<SkColorSpace> colorSpace,
                                  skgpu::Origin origin,
                                  SkImages::GenerateMipmapsFromBase generateMipmapsFromBase,
                                  TextureReleaseProc textureReleaseProc = nullptr,
                                  ReleaseContext = nullptr,
                                  std::string_view label = {})
functions.description: Creates an SkImage from an existing GPU BackendTexture associated with the given Graphite Recorder. The client manages the backend texture’s lifetime. If generateMipmapsFromBase is kYes, upper mip levels are generated from the base level during image creation; otherwise, if the texture is already mipmapped, upper levels are assumed valid. Returns nullptr if the backend texture’s format isn’t recognized/supported or if mipmap generation requirements aren’t met. Provide a colorSpace consistent with the texture’s format (e.g., linear color space for sRGB textures). Optional label tags the created resource.
requirements: backendTexture must be a valid, existing GPU texture recognized/supported by the active backend.
If generateMipmapsFromBase == kYes, the texture must be mipmapped and renderable; otherwise image creation fails.

colorSpace should describe sampling-time color space/transfer characteristics compatible with the backend texture’s format (e.g., linear for sRGB textures, or include transfer function for linear textures).
origin specifies whether the texture’s logical origin is top-left or bottom-left and must match how the texture’s data will be sampled.
Caller is responsible for keeping backendTexture alive for as long as the returned SkImage may use it.
If provided, textureReleaseProc will be invoked with the provided ReleaseContext when Skia is done with the texture (exact timing semantics not further documented here).

functions.name: SkImages::PromiseTextureFrom
functions.signature:
SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::PromiseTextureFrom(skgpu::graphite::Recorder* recorder,
                                         SkISize dimensions,
                                         const skgpu::graphite::TextureInfo& textureInfo,
                                         const SkColorInfo& colorInfo,
                                         skgpu::Origin origin,
                                         skgpu::graphite::Volatile isVolatile,
                                         GraphitePromiseTextureFulfillProc fulfill,
                                         GraphitePromiseImageReleaseProc imageRelease,
                                         GraphitePromiseTextureReleaseProc textureRelease,
                                         GraphitePromiseImageContext imageContext,
                                         std::string_view label = {})
functions.description: Creates a promise SkImage whose backing GPU texture is provided later via fulfill. The client supplies the texture’s description (dimensions, TextureInfo), color characteristics (colorInfo), and volatility. fulfill must return a BackendTexture and a per-texture release context matching the provided description; Skia calls textureRelease when it is done using that texture. imageRelease is called exactly once when Skia will no longer attempt to fulfill the image. Semantics differ for volatile vs. non-volatile images as documented.
requirements: dimensions, textureInfo, and colorInfo must describe the texture that fulfill will return; fulfill must supply a BackendTexture matching these properties.
fulfill must return a valid, existing BackendTexture that is already populated with data in the backend API/device.
The returned BackendTexture must not be deleted by the client until textureRelease is called with the GraphitePromiseTextureReleaseContext returned by fulfill.
imageRelease will be called exactly once when Skia is done attempting to use the promise image (regardless of fulfill success/failure).

Non-volatile images: fulfill is called at Context::insertRecording time and may be called multiple times if used in multiple recordings; textureRelease is called once if a fulfill succeeded, when the GPU is done; if fulfill fails, insertRecording fails and textureRelease is not called.

Volatile images: fulfill is called each time the Recording is inserted; each successful fulfill will have a corresponding textureRelease when the GPU is done; if fulfill fails, textureRelease is not called.
If fulfill fails (does not return a valid backend texture), subsequent insertRecording calls may continue to call fulfill until it succeeds.
origin must match how the texture will be sampled (top-left or bottom-left).

functions.name: SkImages::PromiseTextureFromYUVA
functions.signature:
SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::PromiseTextureFromYUVA(skgpu::graphite::Recorder* recorder,
                                             const skgpu::graphite::YUVABackendTextureInfo& backendTextureInfo,
                                             sk_sp<SkColorSpace> imageColorSpace,
                                             skgpu::graphite::Volatile isVolatile,
                                             GraphitePromiseTextureFulfillProc fulfill,
                                             GraphitePromiseImageReleaseProc imageRelease,
                                             GraphitePromiseTextureReleaseProc textureRelease,
                                             GraphitePromiseImageContext imageContext,
                                             GraphitePromiseTextureFulfillContext planeContexts[],
                                             std::string_view label = {})
functions.description: Creates a GPU-backed SkImage from promised YUV[A] planar textures. backendTextureInfo describes the planar layout, formats, and conversion to RGB. Skia will call fulfill separately for each plane using the corresponding entry in planeContexts; each successful fulfill returns a BackendTexture and per-plane release context, and Skia later calls textureRelease for that plane. imageRelease is called exactly once even on failure. The mipmapped property of backendTextureInfo is currently ignored (but may be required in the future).
requirements: backendTextureInfo must describe the planes, formats, and YUVA-to-RGB conversion for the promised textures.
planeContexts must contain one entry per plane indicated by backendTextureInfo; fulfill will be called per plane with its corresponding context.

For each plane, fulfill must return a valid, existing BackendTexture already populated with data in the backend API/device; that texture must not be deleted until the matching textureRelease is called with the per-plane release context returned by fulfill.
imageRelease is called once, regardless of fulfill success/failure.
Volatile vs. non-volatile callback timing semantics mirror PromiseTextureFrom (fulfill at insertRecording time, may be called multiple times; textureRelease only for successful fulfills).
imageColorSpace may be nullptr; if provided, it defines the color space of the result after YUVA-to-RGB conversion.

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromImage
functions.description: Returns an SkImage backed by a Graphite texture, using the provided Recorder to create/upload as needed. If the source image is already Graphite-backed and compatible with the requested properties (e.g., mipmaps), the original image may be returned. Returns nullptr if no Recorder is provided, if the source image was created with another Recorder whose work has not been submitted, or if required mipmapping is incompatible with the existing Graphite backing.
requirements: Recorder must be non-null; otherwise returns nullptr.
If the source SkImage was created with a different Recorder, prior work on that Recorder must have been submitted; otherwise returns nullptr.
If required mipmapping is incompatible with the existing Graphite texture backing, returns nullptr.
When the source image is already Graphite-backed and compatible with required properties, the original image may be returned.

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromYUVAPixmaps
functions.signature:
SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::TextureFromYUVAPixmaps(skgpu::graphite::Recorder* Recorder,
                                             const SkYUVAPixmaps& pixmaps,
                                             SkImage::RequiredProperties = {},
                                             bool limitToMaxTextureSize = false,
                                             sk_sp<SkColorSpace> imgColorSpace = nullptr,
                                             std::string_view label = {})
functions.description: Creates a texture-backed SkImage from planar YUV[A] data provided as SkYUVAPixmaps, using the given Recorder to convert each plane to a texture. The SkYUVAInfo within pixmaps describes the YUV→RGB transformation; imgColorSpace specifies the color space of the resulting RGB image. Optionally limits the result to the GPU’s maximum texture size. Only supported on the GPU backend.
requirements: Recorder must be non-null; otherwise this will fail and return nullptr.
pixmaps must have a supported SkYUVAInfo describing the conversion to RGB.
SkYUVAPixmaps does not need to remain valid after this function returns.
If limitToMaxTextureSize is true, the output may be downscaled to the GPU’s maximum texture size.
imgColorSpace may be nullptr; if provided, it sets the SkColorSpace of the resulting image.

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromYUVATextures
functions.signature:
SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::TextureFromYUVATextures(
        skgpu::graphite::Recorder* recorder,
        const skgpu::graphite::YUVABackendTextures& yuvaBackendTextures,
        sk_sp<SkColorSpace> imageColorSpace,
        TextureReleaseProc = nullptr,
        ReleaseContext = nullptr,
        std::string_view label = {})
functions.description: Creates an SkImage from YUV[A] planar backend textures associated with the given Recorder. yuvaBackendTextures packages the textures and the description of their layout and conversion to RGBA. Optionally provides a TextureReleaseProc that will be called when Skia is done with the backend textures. imageColorSpace specifies the color space of the resulting image after conversion to RGB.
requirements: yuvaBackendTextures must accurately describe the provided textures and their YUVA→RGBA transformation.
imageColorSpace may be nullptr; if provided, it sets the SkColorSpace of the converted RGB image.
If provided, TextureReleaseProc will be called with the ReleaseContext when the backend textures can be released (exact timing not further documented here).
The provided textures must be valid and associated with the same GPU device/context as used by the Recorder.

functions.name: SkImages::TextureFromYUVAImages
functions.signature:
SK_API sk_sp<SkImage> SkImages::TextureFromYUVAImages(
        skgpu::graphite::Recorder* recorder,
        const SkYUVAInfo& yuvaInfo,
        SkSpan<const sk_sp<SkImage>> images,
        sk_sp<SkColorSpace> imageColorSpace)
functions.description: Creates an SkImage from YUV[A] data supplied as separate SkImages, using the specified Recorder. yuvaInfo describes the YUVA format and transformation to RGB. All input images must be Graphite-backed; if any are not, nullptr is returned. The resulting SkImage does not take a ref on the provided SkImages, but does ref their underlying TextureProxies; any release callbacks for those textures remain as originally set.
requirements: All entries in images must be SkImages of type kGraphite; otherwise returns nullptr.
yuvaInfo must correctly describe the YUVA layout corresponding to images.
imageColorSpace may be nullptr; if provided, it sets the color space of the converted RGB image.
The function does not take a ref on the provided SkImages but will reference their underlying TextureProxies; release procs associated with those textures remain in effect.

functions.name: SkImages::SubsetTextureFrom
functions.description: Returns a texture-backed SkImage that is a subset of the source image. Returns nullptr if the subset is empty, lies outside the source image’s bounds, if pixels could not be read or copied, or if the source image is texture-backed and the context does not match the source image’s context.
requirements: recorder must be non-null to create the new image.
subset must be non-empty and contained within the bounds of img; otherwise returns nullptr.
Source pixels must be readable or copyable; failure to do so results in nullptr.
If the source image is texture-backed, the GPU context must match; otherwise returns nullptr.
props specifies required properties (e.g., mipmaps) for the returned image.

functions.name: SkImages::MakeWithFilter
functions.description: Creates a filtered SkImage on the GPU by applying filter to the specified subset of src, clipped by clipBounds. The returned image may be larger to facilitate reuse across frames; outSubset reports the valid bounds within the returned image, and offset indicates the translation to keep animations aligned. Returns nullptr if the image could not be created; in that case outSubset and offset are undefined.
requirements: recorder specifies where the filtering work is recorded and must be valid.
filter may be nullptr to indicate no-op filtering semantics per Skia’s standard behavior (details not specified here).
outSubset must be a valid, non-null pointer for receiving the bounds of the filtered result.
offset must be a valid, non-null pointer for receiving the translation of the returned image.
subset specifies the bounds of src to process; clipBounds is the expected bounds of the filtered image.

import os
import random
from typing import List

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Favor printable ASCII with occasional NULs and high bytes
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        roll = r.random()
        if roll < 0.80:
            out.append(r.randint(0x20, 0x7E))  # printable
        elif roll < 0.85:
            out.append(0)  # NUL
        elif roll < 0.93:
            out.append(r.randint(0x80, 0xFF))  # non-ASCII
        else:
            # Include line breaks and common control chars
            out.append(r.choice([0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D]))
    return bytes(out)

def _bias_payloads(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Construct a diverse set of buffers that exercise streams well
    payloads: List[bytes] = []

    # Small strings
    payloads.append(b"")
    payloads.append(b"a")
    payloads.append(b"hello world\n")

    # Typical text with newlines and tabs
    payloads.append(_rand_ascii(r, 16, 64))

    # Binary-like data with NULs and high-bytes
    payloads.append(bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(r.randint(32, 128))))

    # Repetitive patterns to expose run-length behavior
    rep = r.choice([b"A", b"\x00", b"\xFF", b"abc"])
    payloads.append(rep * r.randint(8, 64))

    # Length near common boundaries
    for L in [31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1023]:
        chunk = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(L))
        payloads.append(chunk)

    # Mixed ASCII + binary
    mixed = bytearray()
    for _ in range(r.randint(64, 200)):
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            mixed.extend(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 4))
        else:
            mixed.append(r.getrandbits(8))
    payloads.append(bytes(mixed))

    # JSON-like and XML-like snippets (as bytes)
    payloads.append(b"{\"key\": \"value\", \"arr\": [1,2,3]}\n")
    payloads.append(b"<root><child attr=\"v\"/>text</root>\n")

    # Large but capped sequences (to 1024, as stubs limit writes)
    large = bytearray()
    block = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(16))
    for _ in range(64):  # 64*16 = 1024
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            large.extend(block)
        else:
            # Slightly mutate
            b = bytearray(block)
            for _m in range(r.randint(0, 2)):
                idx = r.randrange(len(b))
                b[idx] ^= r.randrange(1, 256)
            large.extend(b)
    payloads.append(bytes(large))

    return payloads

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Produce a single buffer used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to exercise SkWStream/SkNullWStream writes
    and SkMemoryStream content. We assemble multiple concatenated sub-payloads separated by
    random delimiters so the stream implementations can encounter varied content and lengths.
    The overall size is capped to 4096 bytes.
    """
    r = random.Random(seed)

    payloads = _bias_payloads(r)

    # Shuffle and pick a subset to keep within global size limit
    r.shuffle(payloads)

    # Random delimiters to vary content (including NUL and newline)
    delims = [b"\n", b"\x00", b"--SEP--", b"\r\n", b"::", b"\t"]

    out = bytearray()
    for p in payloads:
        # Occasionally insert a delimiter
        if out and r.random() < 0.5:
            d = r.choice(delims)
            if len(out) + len(d) <= 4096:
                out.extend(d)
        if len(out) + len(p) > 4096:
            # Trim last chunk if it would overflow
            remaining = 4096 - len(out)
            if remaining <= 0:
                break
            out.extend(p[:remaining])
            break
        out.extend(p)

    # Ensure non-empty
    if not out:
        out.extend(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 32))

    return bytes(out)

def _rand_ident(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    first = rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest = ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_") for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 10)))
    return first + rest

def _gen_shader(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a minimal yet varied GLSL-like shader source
    version = rnd.choice(["#version 100", "#version 300 es", "#version 330 core", "#version 310 es"]) if rnd.random() < 0.8 else ""
    precision = rnd.choice(["precision highp float;", "precision mediump float;", "precision lowp float;", ""]) if "es" in version else ""

    uniforms = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 3)):
        uname = _rand_ident(rnd)
        utype = rnd.choice(["float", "vec2", "vec3", "vec4", "int", "sampler2D"])

            io = rnd.choice(["in", "out"])
            varyings.append(f"{io} {vtype} {vname};")
    else:
        # older style
        for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 2)):
            vname = _rand_ident(rnd)
            vtype = rnd.choice(["vec2", "vec3", "vec4"])
            io = rnd.choice(["varying", "attribute"])
            varyings.append(f"{io} {vtype} {vname};")

    functions = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 2)):
        fname = _rand_ident(rnd)
        argt = rnd.choice(["float", "vec2", "vec3", "vec4"]) 
        ret = rnd.choice(["float", "vec2", "vec3", "vec4"]) 
        builtin = rnd.choice(GLSL_BUILTINS)
        functions.append(
            f"{ret} {fname}({argt} a) {{ return {builtin}(a); }}"
        )

    main_lines = []
    # Sprinkle unicode comments and random statements
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        main_lines.append("// " + rnd.choice(UNICODE_EXTRAS) + " shader fragment")
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 6)):
        lhs = _rand_ident(rnd)
        ty = rnd.choice(["float", "vec2", "vec3", "vec4", "int"])
        rhs = rnd.choice([
            str(rnd.uniform(-1.0, 1.0)),
            f"{rnd.choice(GLSL_BUILTINS)}({rnd.uniform(0.0, 3.14):.3f})",
            f"{ty}({', '.join(f'{rnd.uniform(-1,1):.2f}' for _ in range(min(4, 1 if ty=='int' else 4)))})",
        ])
        if ty == "int":
            rhs = str(rnd.randint(-5, 5))
        main_lines.append(f"{ty} {lhs} = {rhs};")
    # Ensure a valid main signature most handlers can accept
    out_assign = ""
    if "#version 300" in version or "#version 330" in version:
        out_name = _rand_ident(rnd)
        out_assign = f"out vec4 {out_name};\n    {out_name} = vec4(0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);"
    else:
        out_assign = "gl_FragColor = vec4(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);"

    main_body = "\n    ".join(main_lines + [out_assign])
    main_fn = f"void main() {{\n    {main_body}\n}}"

    sections = [s for s in [version, precision] if s]
    sections += defs + uniforms + varyings + functions + [main_fn]
    shader = "\n".join(sections)
    # Occasionally inject tricky tokens/comments
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        shader += "\n/* unicode */ // " + " ".join(UNICODE_EXTRAS[:rnd.randint(1, 4)])
    return shader


def _gen_error_log(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of typical compiler diagnostics and random lines
    lines = []
    n = rnd.randint(2, 8)
    for _ in range(n):
        prefix = rnd.choice(["0:", "1:", "2:", "vertex:", "fragment:", "line "])
        line_no = rnd.randint(1, 200)
        col = rnd.randint(1, 80)
        msg = rnd.choice(ERROR_PHRASES)
        extra = ""
        if rnd.random() < 0.4:
            extra = f" ({rnd.choice(GLSL_KEYWORDS)})"
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            extra += " " + rnd.choice(UNICODE_EXTRAS)
        lines.append(f"{prefix}{line_no}:{col}: {msg}{extra}")
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        lines.append("note: compilation terminated")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Produce multiple pairs to give FUZZ_PARAM_STR diverse slices.
    parts = []
    count = rnd.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(count):
        shader = _gen_shader(rnd)
        log = _gen_error_log(rnd)
        # Separate sections by NUL to increase chance of distinct string extraction
        parts.append(shader)
        parts.append("\0")
        parts.append(log)
        # Add record separator
        parts.append("\n\n--\n")

    blob = ("".join(parts)).encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    if len(blob) > MAX_SIZE:
        blob = blob[:MAX_SIZE]
    return blob
